declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineBigSiteQuasiCoherentDerivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H00.** Let `S` be a scheme in a big fppf site `B`. Then `QC((Aff/S), O)` — the
triangulated category of quasi-coherent objects (Stacks 0GYV) of the derived category of
`O`-modules on the category `(Aff/S)` of affine schemes over `S` with the chaotic topology and
its sheaf of rings of global functions, that is `QC((Sch/S)_{fppf})` of Stacks 0H0H for the
identity of `(Sch/S)_{fppf}` — is canonically equivalent to `D_QCoh(O_S)`, the full subcategory
of the derived category of `O_S`-modules (in any model) of the objects with quasi-coherent
cohomology sheaves; the modules have their sections in `max (u + 1) t`.

The equivalence is the composite of the three equivalences of the proof of Stacks 0H0K, for the
Zariski topology: `ε^*` from `QC((Aff/S), O)` onto the objects `K` of `D((Aff/S)_{Zar}↑)` with
`Rε_*K` cartesian (Stacks 0H0J, 0GZS); the direct image along the morphism of ringed sites given
by the affine opens of `S`, inverse to the derived pullback on the 0GZS subcategories (the
argument of Stacks 09J1); and the identification of the 0GZS subcategory of the lifted small
affine Zariski site of `S` with `D_QCoh(O_S)` (Descent 03FG, Stacks 0F1B, 0H04).
declarations.statement:
def affineBigSiteQuasiCoherentDerivedEquivalence
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max (u + 1) t} S.ringCatSheaf)] :
    quasiCoherentDerived.{u, u + 1, u, t} B S hS (𝟭 (BigFppfOver B S hS)) ≌
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite S.ringCatSheaf :
        ObjectProperty (SheafOfModules.{max (u + 1) t} S.ringCatSheaf))).FullSubcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AffineEtale
declarations.doc:
The *affine étale site* of a presheaf `F` on the big fppf site of `S`, as a category: its
objects are the étale charts of `F` with affine source, and its morphisms are the morphisms of
schemes whose triangle over `F` commutes.
declarations.statement: abbrev AffineEtale
declarations.comment: objects and morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AffineEtale.IsCovering
declarations.doc:
A family of affine étale charts of `F` is a covering family exactly when it is a covering
family of the small étale site and its index type is finite.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (AffineEtale B S hS F)) : Prop
declarations.comment: coverings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleRestriction_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Restriction from the small étale site of an algebraic space to its affine étale charts is an
equivalence on sheaves of sets, at the universe of the objects of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineEtaleRestriction_isEquivalence :
    (affineEtaleRestriction B S hS F hF (Type (u + 1))).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: equivalence of topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleToSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism from the affine étale ringed topos of an algebraic space to its small
étale ringed topos.

Its inverse image is restriction to affine charts and is an equivalence, and its structure map
is an isomorphism which, after forgetting the ring operations, is the identity of the restricted
structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineEtaleToSmallEtale :
    { f : RingedToposHom
        (affineEtaleRingedTopos B S hS F hF)
        (liftedSmallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS F) //
      f.toToposHom.inverseImage =
        affineEtaleRestriction B S hS F hF (Type (u + 1)) ∧
      f.toToposHom.inverseImage.IsEquivalence ∧
      IsIso f.fSharpInverseImage ∧
      HEq ((affineEtaleRingedTopos B S hS F hF).forgetRing.map
        f.fSharpInverseImage)
        (𝟙 ((affineEtaleRingedTopos B S hS F hF).forgetRing.obj
          (affineEtaleRingedTopos B S hS F hF).O)) }
declarations.comment: canonical morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_restrictionBaseChange_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on the affine étale site of an algebraic space is
cartesian: each restriction map exhibits its target as a base change of its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_restrictionBaseChange_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (M : SheafOfModules.{max m (u + 1)} (affineEtaleRingSheaf B S hS F hF))
    (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    {U V : AffineEtale B S hS F} (f : U ⟶ V) :
    IsIso (Stacks.PresheafOfModules.restrictionBaseChange.{u + 1, u, u + 1, m} M.val f.op)
declarations.comment: quasi-coherent implies cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtale_quasicoherent_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H04.**  Let `F` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `𝓕` be a presheaf
of `𝒪_F`-modules on the affine étale site of `F`.  The following are equivalent:

1. for every morphism `U ⟶ U'` of `F_{affine, étale}` the base-change map
   `𝓕(U') ⊗_{𝒪_F(U')} 𝒪_F(U) ⟶ 𝓕(U)` is an isomorphism;
2. `𝓕` is a sheaf and is quasi-coherent on the ringed site `(F_{affine, étale}, 𝒪_F)` in the
   sense of Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (6);
3. `𝓕` is a sheaf and corresponds, under the equivalence of Stacks 0H03, to a quasi-coherent
   `𝒪_F`-module on the small étale site of `F`.

Conditions (2) and (3) carry the sheaf condition as a conjunct, because quasi-coherence is a
condition on a sheaf of modules; the source's proof of (1) ⇒ (2) likewise begins by proving the
sheaf condition.

(1) ⇒ (2) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isIso_restrictionBaseChange`,
(2) ⇒ (1) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_restrictionBaseChange_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, and
(2) ⇔ (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleLiftedModuleRestriction_iff` together
with the essential surjectivity of restriction to the affine charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineEtale_quasicoherent_tfae
    (M : PresheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      ((affineEtaleStructureSheaf B S hS F hF).obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)) :
    List.TFAE
      [∀ (U V : AffineEtale B S hS F) (f : U ⟶ V),
          IsIso (Stacks.PresheafOfModules.restrictionBaseChange.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1} M f.op),
        ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (AffineEtale.topology B S hS F) M.presheaf,
          (⟨M, h⟩ : SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
            (affineEtaleRingSheaf B S hS F hF)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite,
        ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (AffineEtale.topology B S hS F) M.presheaf,
          ∃ G : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (liftedSmallEtaleRingSheaf B S hS F),
            G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
              Nonempty ((affineEtaleLiftedModuleRestriction B S hS F hF).obj G ≅ ⟨M, h⟩)]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology_affineEtaleChaotic
declarations.doc:
**Categories (3) and (4) of Stacks 0H06 agree.**  On the affine étale charts of an algebraic
space with the chaotic topology, an object of the derived category of `𝒪_F`-modules is a
cartesian object in the sense of Stacks 0GYU exactly when all of its cohomology sheaves are
quasi-coherent; that is, `QC(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F) = D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`.

This is Stacks 0GZR,
`Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentCohomology.isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology`, whose
two hypotheses are supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChaoticRingedSite_J` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_affineEtaleChaoticRingedSite_O_map`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology_affineEtaleChaotic
    (bc : BaseChangeData.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (affineEtaleChaoticRingedSite B S hS F hF).O).obj)
    (K : DMod.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (affineEtaleChaoticRingedSite B S hS F hF).O).obj) :
    IsQC.{w} bc K ↔
      hasQuasicoherentCohomology.{w} (affineEtaleChaoticRingedSite B S hS F hF) K
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) and (4) QC(X_affine, O_X), as an equality of the two conditions on an object of D(O_X) of the chaotic affine etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQC_eq_hasQuasicoherentCohomology_affineEtaleChaotic
declarations.doc:
**Categories (3) and (4) of Stacks 0H06 are cut out of `D(𝒪_F)` by the same object
property.**  This is the previous result as an equality of object properties, which is the form
that exhibits the two full subcategories as the same subcategory of `D(𝒪_F)` rather than merely
as equivalent ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQC_eq_hasQuasicoherentCohomology_affineEtaleChaotic
    (bc : BaseChangeData.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (affineEtaleChaoticRingedSite B S hS F hF).O).obj) :
    (fun K ↦ IsQC.{w} bc K :
        ObjectProperty (DMod.{w}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (affineEtaleChaoticRingedSite B S hS F hF).O).obj)) =
      hasQuasicoherentCohomology.{w} (affineEtaleChaoticRingedSite B S hS F hF)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) and (4) QC(X_affine, O_X), as an equality of object properties on D(O_X) of the chaotic affine etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedCategoryB_isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleRestriction_iff
declarations.doc:
**Categories (1) and (2) of Stacks 0H06 agree**, over the single named input `hrefl`.

Restriction to the affine étale charts is an equivalence of the unbounded derived categories of
`𝒪_F`-modules (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleDerivedRestrictionEquivalence`), and under it
a complex has quasi-coherent cohomology exactly when its restriction does; so it identifies
`D_QCoh(𝒪_F)` with `D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`.

One direction of the identification of quasi-coherence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleModuleRestriction`, proved above; the
other is the hypothesis `hrefl`, a statement about single modules and therefore the degree-zero
part of the conclusion rather than the conclusion itself.  The passage from modules to complexes
is `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyIso`, which identifies the cohomology
sheaves of the restricted complex with the restrictions of the cohomology sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleRestriction_iff
    (hrefl : ∀ M : SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O)),
      ((affineEtaleModuleRestriction B S hS F hF).obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
        M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O)))) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite (affineEtaleRingRestriction B S hS F hF))
        ((affineEtaleDerivedRestrictionEquivalence B S hS F hF).functor.obj K) ↔
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))) K
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) D_QCoh(O_X) and (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X), at the level of the object properties cutting them out, carrying as the hypothesis hrefl the converse of isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleModuleRestriction: a module on the small etale site whose restriction to the affine charts is quasi-coherent is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Categories (1) and (2) of Stacks 0H06 are equivalent**, over the single named input
`hrefl`: restriction to the affine étale charts is an exact equivalence

`D_QCoh(𝒪_F) ⟶ D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`.

It is the equivalence of unbounded derived categories
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleDerivedRestrictionEquivalence`, which is triangulated, cut
down to the two full subcategories by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedCategoryB_isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleRestriction_iff`; so
the comparison is the canonical one, being the restriction of the derived restriction functor,
and not merely some equivalence.  See the module docstring for the status of `hrefl`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleEquivalence
    (hrefl : ∀ M : SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O)),
      ((affineEtaleModuleRestriction B S hS F hF).obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
        M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS F hF ≌
      affineEtaleQuasicoherentDerivedCategory B S hS F hF
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) D_QCoh(O_X) and (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X), as an equivalence of categories induced by derived restriction, carrying as the hypothesis hrefl the converse of isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleModuleRestriction: a module on the small etale site whose restriction to the affine charts is quasi-coherent is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology_affineEtaleChartChaotic
declarations.doc:
**Categories (3) and (4) of Stacks 0H06 agree.** On the chaotic affine étale site of `F`, an
object of the derived category of modules is cartesian in the sense of Stacks 0GYU exactly when
all of its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent, for every base-change datum.

This is Stacks 0GZR, `isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology`: a morphism of affine étale charts is
flat on the underlying affine schemes, so the restriction maps of `𝒪_F` are flat
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_affineEtaleChartRings_map`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology_affineEtaleChartChaotic
    (bc : BaseChangeData.{w} (affineEtaleRingRestriction B S hS F hF).obj)
    (K : DMod.{w} (affineEtaleRingRestriction B S hS F hF).obj) :
    IsQC.{w} bc K ↔
      hasQuasicoherentCohomology.{w} (affineEtaleChartChaoticRingedSite B S hS F hF) K
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) and (4) QC(X_affine, O_X), as an equality of the two conditions on an object of D(X_affine, O_X), with O_X the structure sheaf of D_QCoh(O_X) restricted to the affine charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of categories (3) and (4) of Stacks 0H06**,
`D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F) ≌ QC(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`: the two are the same full subcategory of
`D(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology_affineEtaleChartChaotic`, and the
equivalence is the identity on objects.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence :
    affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, w} B S hS F hF ≌
      QC.{w} (affineEtaleBaseChangeData.{u, w} B S hS F hF)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) and (4) QC(X_affine, O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Categories (2) and (3) of Stacks 0H06 are equivalent**: for the change of topology
`ε : (F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F) ⟶ (F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)` from the étale to the chaotic topology on the
affine étale charts, `Rε_*` is an equivalence

`D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F) ≌ D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`

with quasi-inverse `ε^*`.

It is Stacks 0GZS for `ε` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleCartesianPushforwardEquivalence`),
whose hypothesis is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyKFlatAcyclic_affineEtale`, with its source
identified with `D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedCartesianEquivalence`) and its
target with `D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence`). That its functor
is `Rε_*` is `affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence_functor_comp_ι`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence :
    affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, w} B S hS F hF ≌
      affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, w} B S hS F hF
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X) and (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X), given by Rε_* for the change of topology ε from the etale to the chaotic topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Categories (1) and (2) of Stacks 0H06 are equivalent**: restriction to the affine étale
charts induces an equivalence

`D_QCoh(𝒪_F) ≌ D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`.

Restriction of sheaves of `𝒪_F`-modules to the affine charts is an equivalence of abelian
categories (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleRestrictionEquivalence`, the Comparison Lemma
along the dense subsite inclusion of Stacks 04JS, i.e. the equivalence of ringed topoi of
Stacks 0H03 on modules); it is exact, so it derives to an equivalence of the unbounded derived
categories, and it preserves and reflects quasi-coherence
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleModulePushforward_iff`), so that
equivalence matches the two subcategories. Its functor is the derived functor of restriction,
`quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence_functor_obj_obj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence :
    QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, max (u + 1) w} B S hS F hF ≌
      affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, w} B S hS F hF
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) D_QCoh(O_X) and (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X), induced by restriction to the affine charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H06.** For an algebraic space `F` over `S`, the four categories

1. `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)`,
2. `D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`,
3. `D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`, and
4. `QC(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`

are equivalent, by the canonical equivalences `(1) ≌ (2)` induced by restriction to the affine
charts (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence`),
`(2) ≌ (3)` given by `Rε_*` for the change of topology from the étale to the chaotic topology
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence`), and
`(3) ≌ (4)` the identity of the common full subcategory of `D(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain :
    (QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, max (u + 1) w} B S hS F hF ≌
        affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, w} B S hS F hF) ×
      (affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, w} B S hS F hF ≌
        affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, w} B S hS F hF) ×
      (affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, w} B S hS F hF ≌
        QC.{w} (affineEtaleBaseChangeData.{u, w} B S hS F hF))
declarations.comment: the chain of equivalences (1) ≃ (2) ≃ (3) ≃ (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain
declarations.doc:
**The four categories of Stacks 0H06 are full triangulated subcategories** of the derived
categories they sit in: in order, `D_QCoh(𝒪_F) ⊆ D(𝒪_F)`,
`D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F) ⊆ D(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`, and
`D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F), QC(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F) ⊆ D(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`.

A full triangulated subcategory is exactly what
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated` says: the subcategory contains a zero object, is
stable under the translation in both directions, and is closed under extensions in distinguished
triangles.  From it Mathlib derives the shift and the pretriangulated structure of the
subcategory itself, whose distinguished triangles are the triangles distinguished in the ambient
derived category, and the triangulatedness of the inclusion.  This is the triangulated structure
the tag's phrase *the following triangulated categories* refers to.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) w} B S hS F hF) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated
        (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, max (u + 1) w}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated
        (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u,
          max (u + 1) w} (affineEtaleRingRestriction B S hS F hF))) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated
        (hasQuasicoherentCohomologyAffineEtaleChart.{u, w} B S hS F hF) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated
        (IsQC.{w} (affineEtaleBaseChangeData.{u, w} B S hS F hF))
declarations.comment: the four categories (1) D_QCoh(O_X), (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X), (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) and (4) QC(X_affine, O_X) are full triangulated subcategories of the derived categories they sit in, which is the triangulated structure the tag speaks of

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commShiftAffineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of categories (3) and (4) of Stacks 0H06 commutes with the translation.**
Its functor, followed by the inclusion of `QC(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`, is the inclusion of
`D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence_functor_comp_ι`),
and the inclusion of a full triangulated subcategory commutes with the translation.

This is the canonical shift-compatibility of the equivalence `(3) ≌ (4)`, and it is an instance:
the compatibility of the equivalence with the translation `[1]` is half of the tag's assertion
that the equivalence is *exact*, so it is a registered fact about the equivalence and not a
structure chosen inside the statement of the other half.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance commShiftAffineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence :
    (affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F hF).functor.CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the equivalence (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) ≃ (4) QC(X_affine, O_X) commutes with the translation [1]: half of the tag's assertion that it is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commShiftAffineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of categories (2) and (3) of Stacks 0H06 commutes with the translation.**
Its functor, followed by the inclusion of `D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`, is the inclusion of
`D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)` followed by `Rε_*`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence_functor_comp_ι`),
and `Rε_*` commutes with the translation
(`Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.ChaoticComparison.derivedEpsilonPushforwardCommShift`).

This is the canonical shift-compatibility of the equivalence `(2) ≌ (3)`, and it is an instance,
for the reason given at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commShiftAffineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance commShiftAffineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence :
    (affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F
      hF).functor.CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the equivalence (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X) ≃ (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) commutes with the translation [1]: half of the tag's assertion that it is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commShiftQuasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of categories (1) and (2) of Stacks 0H06 commutes with the translation.**
Its functor, followed by the inclusion of `D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`, is the inclusion of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_F)` followed by the derived functor of restriction to the affine charts
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence_functor_comp_ι`), and
the derived functor of an exact functor commutes with the translation.

This is the canonical shift-compatibility of the equivalence `(1) ≌ (2)`, and it is an instance,
for the reason given at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commShiftAffineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence`.  The
derived category of `𝒪_F`-modules it is read over is the standard model, introduced by the `letI`
of the first line as everywhere in the chain; that `letI` names the *category*, not the
shift-compatibility, and the goal it is found at carries the same one.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance commShiftQuasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) w} B S hS F hF) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    haveI := isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedChart.{u, w} B S hS F hF
    (quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F hF).functor.CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the equivalence (1) D_QCoh(O_X) ≃ (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X) commutes with the translation [1]: half of the tag's assertion that it is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChainEquivalences
declarations.doc:
**The three equivalences of Stacks 0H06 are exact.**  For an algebraic space `F` over `S`, the
canonical equivalences

1. `D_QCoh(𝒪_F) ≌ D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`, induced by restriction to the affine charts,
2. `D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F) ≌ D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`, given by `Rε_*` for the change
   from the étale to the chaotic topology, and
3. `D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F) ≌ QC(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`, the identity of the common full subcategory
   of `D(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`,

are exact functors of triangulated categories: each carries distinguished triangles to
distinguished triangles, over the shift-compatibility of the equivalence it belongs to.  That
shift-compatibility is not chosen here: `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsTriangulated` takes the
`CategoryTheory.Functor.CommShift` structure it is read over as an instance, and the instance
found at each of the three functors is the one registered for it under this tag, namely
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commShiftQuasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commShiftAffineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.commShiftAffineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence`.  So both
halves of *exact* — compatibility with the translation `[1]` and preservation of distinguished
triangles — are registered facts about the three equivalences.

Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain`, which says that
the four categories are full triangulated subcategories of the derived categories they sit in,
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain`, which is the chain of
equivalences itself, this is the assertion of the tag;
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTriangulatedEquivalence_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain` states
the same exactness in Mathlib's bundled form.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChainEquivalences :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) w} B S hS F hF) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    haveI := isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedChart.{u, w} B S hS F hF
    (quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F hF).functor.IsTriangulated ∧
      (affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F
        hF).functor.IsTriangulated ∧
      (affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F
        hF).functor.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the three equivalences of the chain are exact: (1) D_QCoh(O_X) ≃ (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X), (2) ≃ (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) and (3) ≃ (4) QC(X_affine, O_X) each carry distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles, over the compatibilities with the translation [1] registered for them under this tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTriangulatedEquivalence_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain
declarations.doc:
**The three equivalences of Stacks 0H06 are exact equivalences of triangulated categories**,
in Mathlib's bundled form: for an algebraic space `F` over `S`, each of

1. `D_QCoh(𝒪_F) ≌ D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`,
2. `D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F) ≌ D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`, and
3. `D_QCoh(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F) ≌ QC(F_{affine}, 𝒪_F)`

is a `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.IsTriangulated`: its functor and its inverse both commute with
the translation `[1]`, those two compatibilities agree on the unit and the counit, and both
carry distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles.  This is the tag's phrase *canonical
exact equivalences between the following triangulated categories* with nothing left implicit:
the triangulated structure of the four categories is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain`, the equivalences
are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain`, and exactness is this.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulatedEquivalence_quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChain :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (Modules.{u, max (u + 1) w} B S hS F hF) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    haveI := isTriangulated_quasicoherentDerivedChart.{u, w} B S hS F hF
    (quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleChartEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F hF).IsTriangulated ∧
      (affineEtaleChartQuasicoherentDerivedChaoticEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F hF).IsTriangulated ∧
      (affineEtaleChartChaoticQuasicoherentQCEquivalence.{u, w} B S hS F hF).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: each of the three equivalences (1) D_QCoh(O_X) ≃ (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X), (2) ≃ (3) D_QCoh(X_affine, O_X) and (3) ≃ (4) QC(X_affine, O_X) is an exact equivalence of triangulated categories: functor and inverse both commute with the translation [1], compatibly on unit and counit, and both preserve distinguished triangles

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleRestrictionEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Categories (1) and (2) of Stacks 0H06 are equivalent, at the universe of the schemes**:
restriction to the affine étale charts is an exact equivalence

`D_QCoh(𝒪_F) ⟶ D_QCoh(F_{affine,étale}, 𝒪_F)`

for module sections in the universe of the schemes. It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleEquivalence` with its hypothesis
discharged by the reflection of quasi-coherence under restriction to the affine charts,
`isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineEtaleModuleRestriction`, so it is the
restriction of the derived restriction functor
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineEtaleDerivedRestrictionEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentDerivedAffineEtaleRestrictionEquivalence :
    QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS F hF ≌
      affineEtaleQuasicoherentDerivedCategory B S hS F hF
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) D_QCoh(O_X) and (2) D_QCoh(X_affine_etale, O_X), induced by derived restriction, for module sections in the universe of the schemes

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representableQuasiCoherentDerivedEquivalence
registrations.comment: the equivalence QC((Aff/X), 𝒪) ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_X), on the proof of Stacks 0H0K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.associatedAffineChaoticTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H09.** The associated affine site of a category `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}`: the
affine subcategory `𝒳_{affine}` carrying the chaotic topology, in which the maximal sieve is
the only covering sieve.
declarations.statement: abbrev associatedAffineChaoticTopology : GrothendieckTopology (AffineCategory B S hS p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.sheafAssociatedAffineChaoticEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H09.** Sheaves on the associated affine site are the same as presheaves on the
affine subcategory: the forgetful functor from sheaves to presheaves is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
def sheafAssociatedAffineChaoticEquivalence (A : Type*) [Category A] :
    Sheaf (associatedAffineChaoticTopology B S hS p) A ≌ (AffineCategory B S hS p)ᵒᵖ ⥤ A
declarations.comment: sheaves are presheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0A.** The affine subcategory of a category over the big fppf category of `S`:
the full subcategory of the objects lying over an affine scheme.
declarations.statement: abbrev AffineCategory
declarations.comment: the affine subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.isStronglyCartesian_toAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0A.** Every arrow between affine objects of a category fibred in groupoids is
strongly cartesian for the restricted structure functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStronglyCartesian_toAffine (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    {x y : AffineCategory B S hS p} (φ : y ⟶ x) :
    (toAffine B S hS p).IsStronglyCartesian ((toAffine B S hS p).map φ) φ
declarations.comment: arrows are strongly cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.associatedAffineTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0A.** The associated affine site of a category `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` and a
topology `τ` on the affine schemes over `S`: the topology the affine subcategory inherits
from `τ`.

The five associated affine sites of the source — Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf —
are the values of this at the five big affine topologies.
declarations.statement:
abbrev associatedAffineTopology (τ : GrothendieckTopology (BigAffineFppf B S hS)) :
    GrothendieckTopology (AffineCategory B S hS p)
declarations.comment: the associated affine topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.generate_mem_associatedAffineTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0A.** A family in the affine subcategory of a category fibred in groupoids whose
image in the affine schemes over `S` generates a covering sieve generates a covering sieve for
the associated affine topology.

This is the description of the coverings of `𝒳_{affine, τ}` in the paragraph following the
source's definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem generate_mem_associatedAffineTopology (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology (BigAffineFppf B S hS))
    (E : Covering.{v, w, u + 1} (AffineCategory B S hS p))
    (hE : Sieve.generate (E.2.map (AffineCategory.toAffine B S hS p)).presieve₀ ∈
      τ ((AffineCategory.toAffine B S hS p).obj E.1)) :
    Sieve.generate E.2.presieve₀ ∈ associatedAffineTopology B S hS p τ E.1
declarations.comment: the covering families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.isFiberedInGroupoids_toAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0B.** The structure functor of the affine subcategory of a category fibred in
groupoids is again fibred in groupoids, over the big affine fppf category of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiberedInGroupoids_toAffine (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    (toAffine B S hS p).IsFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.comment: the affine structure functor is fibred in groupoids

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.isCoverDense_inclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0B.** The affine inclusion of a category fibred in groupoids is cover dense for
the inherited topology, as soon as the affine inclusion of the big fppf category over `S` is
cover dense.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoverDense_inclusion (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (K : GrothendieckTopology (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (hj : (BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).IsCoverDense K) :
    (inclusion B S hS p).IsCoverDense (p.inheritedTopology K)
declarations.comment: cover density

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0B.** The inclusion of the affine subcategory of a category fibred in groupoids
is a special cocontinuous functor from the associated affine site to the associated site, for
any topology on the big affine fppf category of `S` and any topology on the big fppf category
over `S` for which the affine inclusion downstairs is a dense subsite inclusion.

Consequently the inclusion induces an equivalence of sheaf topoi. The five topologies of the
source are the five instances.
declarations.statement:
theorem inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (J : GrothendieckTopology (BigAffineFppf B S hS))
    (K : GrothendieckTopology (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (hbase : (BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).IsDenseSubsite J K) :
    IsSpecialCocontinuous (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p J) (p.inheritedTopology K)
      (inclusion B S hS p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0B** for the fppf topology: the inclusion of the affine subcategory into a
category fibred in groupoids is special cocontinuous from the associated affine fppf site to
the associated fppf site, and so induces an equivalence of the sheaf topoi.
declarations.statement:
theorem inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_fppf (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    IsSpecialCocontinuous
      (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineFppf.topology B S hS))
      (associatedTopology B S hS p B.topology) (inclusion B S hS p)
declarations.comment: the fppf topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0B** for the étale topology: the inclusion of the affine subcategory into a
category fibred in groupoids is special cocontinuous from the associated affine étale site to
the associated étale site, and so induces an equivalence of the sheaf topoi.
declarations.statement:
theorem inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_etale (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    IsSpecialCocontinuous
      (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineEtale.topology B.toBigEtaleSite S hS))
      (p.inheritedTopology (BigEtaleOver.topology B.toBigEtaleSite S hS))
      (inclusion B S hS p)
declarations.comment: the étale topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0B** for the smooth topology: the inclusion of the affine subcategory into a
category fibred in groupoids is special cocontinuous from the associated affine smooth site to
the associated smooth site, and so induces an equivalence of the sheaf topoi.
declarations.statement:
theorem inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_smooth (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    IsSpecialCocontinuous
      (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineSmooth.topology B.toBigSmoothSite S hS))
      (p.inheritedTopology (BigSmoothOver.topology B.toBigSmoothSite S hS))
      (inclusion B S hS p)
declarations.comment: the smooth topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_zariski
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0B** for the Zariski topology: the inclusion of the affine subcategory into a
category fibred in groupoids is special cocontinuous from the associated affine Zariski site to
the associated Zariski site, and so induces an equivalence of the sheaf topoi.
declarations.statement:
theorem inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_zariski (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    IsSpecialCocontinuous
      (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineZariski.topology B.toBigZariskiSite S hS))
      (p.inheritedTopology (BigZariskiOver.topology B.toBigZariskiSite S hS))
      (inclusion B S hS p)
declarations.comment: the Zariski topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_syntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0B** for the syntomic topology: the inclusion of the affine subcategory into a
category fibred in groupoids is special cocontinuous from the associated affine syntomic site to
the associated syntomic site, and so induces an equivalence of the sheaf topoi.
declarations.statement:
theorem inclusion_isSpecialCocontinuous_syntomic (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    IsSpecialCocontinuous
      (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineSyntomic.topology B.toBigSyntomicSite S hS))
      (p.inheritedTopology (BigSyntomicOver.topology B.toBigSyntomicSite S hS))
      (inclusion B S hS p)
declarations.comment: the syntomic topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineToFull
declarations.doc:
The morphism of ringed topoi induced by the inclusion of the affine subsite: its underlying
morphism of topoi is the equivalence of Stacks 0H0B and its structure morphism is the adjunct of
the identification of the inverse image of the structure sheaf with its restriction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineToFull
    (O : Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p τ) CommRingCat.{max u v w}) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom (affineRingedTopos B S hS p τ J O)
      (fullRingedTopos B S hS p τ O)
declarations.comment: the morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_affineToFull_fSharpInverseImage
declarations.doc: The structure morphism of `affineToFull` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_affineToFull_fSharpInverseImage
    (O : Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p τ) CommRingCat.{max u v w}) :
    IsIso (affineToFull B S hS p τ J O).fSharpInverseImage
declarations.comment: the structure morphism is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_affineToFull_inverseImage
declarations.doc: The inverse image of `affineToFull` is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_affineToFull_inverseImage
    (O : Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p τ) CommRingCat.{max u v w}) :
    (affineToFull B S hS p τ J O).toToposHom.inverseImage.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the inverse image is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineToFullFppf
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the affine subsite of the associated fppf site of a category fibred in
groupoids, as a morphism of ringed topoi for the lifted structure sheaf of Stacks 06TV.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineToFullFppf (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    letI : (AffineCategory.inclusion B S hS p).IsDenseSubsite
        (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineFppf.topology B S hS))
        (associatedTopology B S hS p B.topology) :=
      isDenseSubsite_affineInclusion_fppf B S hS p hp
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom
      (affineRingedTopos B S hS p B.topology (BigAffineFppf.topology B S hS)
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.topology hp le_rfl))
      (fullRingedTopos B S hS p B.topology
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.topology hp le_rfl))
declarations.comment: the fppf topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineToFullZariski
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the affine subsite of the associated Zariski site of a category fibred in
groupoids, as a morphism of ringed topoi for the lifted structure sheaf of Stacks 06TV. Its
inverse image is an equivalence and its structure morphism is an isomorphism, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_affineToFull_inverseImage` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_affineToFull_fSharpInverseImage`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineToFullZariski (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    letI : (AffineCategory.inclusion B S hS p).IsDenseSubsite
        (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p
          (BigAffineZariski.topology B.toBigZariskiSite S hS))
        (associatedTopology B S hS p B.zariskiTopology) :=
      isDenseSubsite_affineInclusion_zariski B S hS p hp
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom
      (affineRingedTopos B S hS p B.zariskiTopology
        (BigAffineZariski.topology B.toBigZariskiSite S hS)
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.zariskiTopology hp (zariskiTopology_le_topology B)))
      (fullRingedTopos B S hS p B.zariskiTopology
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.zariskiTopology hp
          (zariskiTopology_le_topology B)))
declarations.comment: the Zariski topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineToFullEtale
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the affine subsite of the associated étale site of a category fibred in
groupoids, as a morphism of ringed topoi for the lifted structure sheaf of Stacks 06TV. Its
inverse image is an equivalence and its structure morphism is an isomorphism, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_affineToFull_inverseImage` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_affineToFull_fSharpInverseImage`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineToFullEtale (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    letI : (AffineCategory.inclusion B S hS p).IsDenseSubsite
        (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineEtale.topology B.toBigEtaleSite S hS))
        (associatedTopology B S hS p B.etaleTopology) :=
      isDenseSubsite_affineInclusion_etale B S hS p hp
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom
      (affineRingedTopos B S hS p B.etaleTopology
        (BigAffineEtale.topology B.toBigEtaleSite S hS)
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.etaleTopology hp (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
      (fullRingedTopos B S hS p B.etaleTopology
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.etaleTopology hp (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
declarations.comment: the étale topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineToFullSmooth
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the affine subsite of the associated smooth site of a category fibred in
groupoids, as a morphism of ringed topoi for the lifted structure sheaf of Stacks 06TV. Its
inverse image is an equivalence and its structure morphism is an isomorphism, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_affineToFull_inverseImage` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_affineToFull_fSharpInverseImage`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineToFullSmooth (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    letI : (AffineCategory.inclusion B S hS p).IsDenseSubsite
        (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineSmooth.topology B.toBigSmoothSite S hS))
        (associatedTopology B S hS p B.smoothTopology) :=
      isDenseSubsite_affineInclusion_smooth B S hS p hp
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom
      (affineRingedTopos B S hS p B.smoothTopology
        (BigAffineSmooth.topology B.toBigSmoothSite S hS)
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.smoothTopology hp (smoothTopology_le_topology B)))
      (fullRingedTopos B S hS p B.smoothTopology
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.smoothTopology hp (smoothTopology_le_topology B)))
declarations.comment: the smooth topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineToFullSyntomic
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the affine subsite of the associated syntomic site of a category fibred in
groupoids, as a morphism of ringed topoi for the lifted structure sheaf of Stacks 06TV. Its
inverse image is an equivalence and its structure morphism is an isomorphism, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_affineToFull_inverseImage` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_affineToFull_fSharpInverseImage`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affineToFullSyntomic (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    letI : (AffineCategory.inclusion B S hS p).IsDenseSubsite
        (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p
          (BigAffineSyntomic.topology B.toBigSyntomicSite S hS))
        (associatedTopology B S hS p B.syntomicTopology) :=
      isDenseSubsite_affineInclusion_syntomic B S hS p hp
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom
      (affineRingedTopos B S hS p B.syntomicTopology
        (BigAffineSyntomic.topology B.toBigSyntomicSite S hS)
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.syntomicTopology hp
          (syntomicTopology_le_topology B)))
      (fullRingedTopos B S hS p B.syntomicTopology
        (liftedStructureSheaf B S hS p B.syntomicTopology hp
          (syntomicTopology_le_topology B)))
declarations.comment: the syntomic topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AffineCategory.tfae_isQuasicoherent
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isQuasicoherent (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).chaotic.O)) :
    [∀ ⦃x x' : AffineCategory B S hS p⦄ (f : x ⟶ x'),
        IsIso (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalMap
          (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).chaotic F f),
      F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite,
      ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .zariski).J F.val.presheaf,
        (⟨F.val, h⟩ : SheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .zariski).O)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite,
      ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .etale).J F.val.presheaf,
        (⟨F.val, h⟩ : SheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .etale).O)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite,
      ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .smooth).J F.val.presheaf,
        (⟨F.val, h⟩ : SheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .smooth).O)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite,
      ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .syntomic).J F.val.presheaf,
        (⟨F.val, h⟩ : SheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .syntomic).O)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite,
      ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).J F.val.presheaf,
        (⟨F.val, h⟩ : SheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).O)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite,
      ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).J F.val.presheaf,
        letI := isDenseSubsite_inclusion_siteKind B S hS p hp .fppf
        ∃ G : SheafOfModules.{u} (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf),
          G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
            Nonempty ((Stacks.DenseSubsiteModules.moduleRestriction
              (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).J
              (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS p .fppf) (inclusion B S hS p)
              (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)).obj G ≅
              (⟨F.val, h⟩ : SheafOfModules.{u}
                (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
                  (siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).O)))].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.tfae_locallyQuasicoherent_affine
declarations.doc:
Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` be a category fibred in groupoids and `𝓕` a module over the
structure sheaf `𝒪` of the affine subcategory `𝒳_{affine}`. The following are equivalent:

1. for every arrow `x ⟶ x'` of `𝒳_{affine}` lying over an étale morphism of affine schemes, the
   map `𝓕(x') ⊗_{𝒪(x')} 𝒪(x) ⟶ 𝓕(x)` is an isomorphism;
2. `𝓕` is a sheaf for the étale topology on `𝒳_{affine}` and, for every object `x` of
   `𝒳_{affine}`, the restriction `x^*𝓕|_{U_{affine, étale}}` to the small affine étale site of
   `U = p(x)` is quasi-coherent;
3. `𝓕` corresponds to a locally quasi-coherent module on `𝒳` via the equivalence of Stacks 0H0C
   for the étale topology: it is isomorphic to the restriction to `𝒳_{affine}` of a locally
   quasi-coherent module `𝓖` on `𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_locallyQuasicoherent_affine
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (affineStructurePresheaf B S hS p)) :
    List.TFAE [
      ∀ ⦃x x' : AffineCategory B S hS p⦄ (f : x ⟶ x'),
        Etale ((p ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f.hom) →
          IsIso (restrictionBaseChange.{v, w, u, u}
            (R := affineStructureCommPresheaf B S hS p) F f.op),
      Presheaf.IsSheaf
          (associatedAffineTopology B S hS p (BigAffineEtale.topology B.toBigEtaleSite S hS))
          F.presheaf ∧
        ∀ x : AffineCategory B S hS p,
          ∃ hM : Presheaf.IsSheaf
              (SmallAffineEtale.topology E (p.obj x.obj).left.1 (contains_base B E h S hS p x.obj))
              (affineChartModule B E h S hS p hp x F).presheaf,
            (⟨affineChartModule B E h S hS p hp x F, hM⟩ : SheafOfModules.{u}
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
                (smallAffineEtaleRingedSite E (p.obj x.obj).left.1
                  (contains_base B E h S hS p x.obj)).O)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite,
      ∃ G : PresheafOfModules.{u}
          (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj,
        IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp G ∧
          Nonempty ((PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀ (AffineCategory.inclusion B S hS p) _).obj G ≅
            F)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasiCoherentDerived
declarations.doc:
The *triangulated category of quasi-coherent objects in the derived category* of a category
`p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` over the big fppf category of `S`:

  `QC(𝒳) = QC(𝒳_{affine}, O)`,

the full subcategory of `D(𝒳_{affine}, O)` of the objects `K` such that for every arrow `U → V`
of `𝒳_{affine}` the canonical map `RΓ(V, K) ⊗^L_{O(V)} O(U) ⟶ RΓ(U, K)` is an isomorphism, where
`𝒳_{affine}` is the associated affine site of Stacks 0H09 with its chaotic topology and `O` is
the structure sheaf of `𝒳` restricted to it.
declarations.statement: abbrev quasiCoherentDerived : Type _

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineHomologySheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0I.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` be a category fibred in groupoids, let `M` be
an object of the triangulated category `QC(𝒳)` of Stacks 0H0H, and let `b ∈ ℤ` be such that
`H^i(M) = 0` for all `i > b`. Then `H^b(M)` is a quasi-coherent module on the ringed site
`(𝒳_{affine}, O)`, in the sense of Stacks 0H0E.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_affineHomologySheaf
    (M : quasiCoherentDerived.{u, v, w, t} B S hS p) (b : ℤ)
    (hvan : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (PresheafOfModules.{max v w u t} (affineStructurePresheaf B S hS p)) i).obj M.obj)) :
    (affineHomologySheaf.{u, v, w, t} B S hS p M.obj b).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyKFlatAcyclic_affineEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0J, hypothesis (2) of Stacks 0GZS.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` be a category
fibred in groupoids and `ε : (𝒳_{affine, étale}, O) ⟶ (𝒳_{affine}, O)` the comparison morphism to
the associated affine site with its chaotic topology.  For every object `x` of `𝒳_{affine}` and
every K-flat complex `M^•` of `O(x)`-modules the canonical map
`M^• ⟶ RΓ((𝒳_{affine, étale}/x), (M^• ⊗_{O(x)} O_x)^#)` is a quasi-isomorphism.  (Hypothesis
(1) of Stacks 0GZS, that the target topology is chaotic, is the construction of `ε`: modules on
the chaotic site are presheaves of modules.)
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyKFlatAcyclic_affineEtale :
    IsLocallyKFlatAcyclic.{t}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (AffineCategory.siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .etale).O)
      (affineStructurePresheaf_comm B S hS p)
declarations.comment: ε : 𝒳_{affine,étale} ⟶ 𝒳_{affine} satisfies the assumptions of Stacks 0GZS: hypothesis (2), the target being the chaotic site by construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineEtaleQuasiCoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0J, the conclusion of Stacks 0GZS.** For a category fibred in groupoids
`p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` and the comparison `ε : (𝒳_{affine, étale}, O) ⟶ (𝒳_{affine}, O)`,
`ε^*` and `Rε_*` are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between `QC(𝒳)` (Stacks 0H0H) and the
full subcategory of `D(𝒳_{affine, étale}, O)` of the objects `K` with `Rε_*K` in `QC(𝒳)`.  The
functor of the equivalence is `ε^*` and its inverse is `Rε_*`, both on the nose
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineQuasiCoherentEquivalence_functor` and `_inverse`).
declarations.comment: ε : 𝒳_{affine,étale} ⟶ 𝒳_{affine} satisfies the conclusions of Stacks 0GZS: ε^* and Rε_* are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between QC(𝒳) and the objects K of D(𝒳_{affine,étale}, O) with Rε_*K in QC(𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representableQuasiCoherentDerivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0K.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` be a category fibred in groupoids, represented
by the algebraic space `F` through the equivalence `e` over the site between `𝒳` and the
category of elements of `F` (Stacks 04SV). Then `QC(𝒳)` (Stacks 0H0H) is canonically equivalent
to `D_QCoh(O_F)` (Stacks 071X), with modules in the universe `max v w u t`.

The equivalence is the composite of the three equivalences of the source's proof, on the
single-universe lifts `X↑` of `𝒳_{affine, étale}` and `Y↑` of `F_{affine, étale}`: `ε^*` from
`QC(𝒳)` onto the objects `K` of `D(X↑)` with `Rε_*K` cartesian (Stacks 0H0J, 0GZS); the direct
image `f_*` along the morphism of ringed sites `f : X↑ ⟶ Y↑` given by the affine étale charts of
`F` (Stacks 073M), inverse to the derived pullback `Lf^*` on the 0GZS subcategories (the
argument of Stacks 09J1); and the identification of the 0GZS subcategory of `D(Y↑)` with
`D_QCoh(O_F)` (Stacks 0H0J, 0H06, 03DX).
declarations.comment: QC(𝒳) is canonically equivalent to D_QCoh(O_X) for 𝒳 represented by an algebraic space X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.quasiCoherentDerivedEquivalenceDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0L.** Let `S` be a scheme and `X = Spf(A)`, where `A` is an adic Noetherian
topological `S`-algebra with ideal of definition `I` (More on Algebra, Definition 07E8; Formal
Spaces, Definition 0AIF). Let `p : 𝒳 → (Sch/S)_{fppf}` be the category fibred in sets associated
to the functor `X` (Categories, Example 04TM). Then `QC(𝒳)` (Definition 0H0H) is equivalent to the
category `D_comp(A, I)` of objects of `D(A)` which are derived complete with respect to `I`.

The equivalence is constructed: if the powers of `I` stabilize, `I^{N+1} = I^{N+2}`, then
`I^{N+1} = 0`, `Spec(A) = Spec(A/I^{N+1})` is a final object of `𝒳_{affine}` and the equivalence
is `RΓ(Spec(A), -)` (Stacks 0H0R), every object of `D(A)` being derived complete; otherwise it is
the composite of the source's proof, `qcEquivalenceOfStrict`. Here `D(A)` is the derived category
of `A`-modules in the universe `max (u + 1) t` of the modules of `QC(𝒳)`, in any model.
declarations.statement:
def quasiCoherentDerivedEquivalenceDerivedComplete :
    Stack.quasiCoherentDerived.{u, u + 1, u, t} B S hS (formalSpectrumProjection D) ≌
      ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
        (fun K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) t} A) => IsDerivedComplete I K)
declarations.comment: QC(𝒳) ≌ D_comp(A, I) for 𝒳 the category fibred in sets of Spf(A), A an adic Noetherian topological S-algebra with ideal of definition I

declarations.name: Stacks.Triangulated.AdmissibleSubcategories.isLeftOrthogonal_iff_bijective_precompMap
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 0H0M, Lemma 13.40.3).**
Let `B ⊂ D` be a full subcategory invariant under all shifts, and let
`X --f--> Y --g--> Z --h--> X[1]` be a distinguished triangle. Then `X` lies in the left
orthogonal `ᗮB` if and only if, for every object `B` of `B`, the precomposition map
`g* : Hom_D(Z, B) → Hom_D(Y, B)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftOrthogonal_iff_bijective_precompMap
    (B : D → Prop) (hB : ShiftInvariant B)
    (T : Triangle D) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) :
    IsLeftOrthogonal B T.obj₁ ↔
      ∀ (b : D), B b → Function.Bijective (precompMap T b)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isTriangulated_extensionProduct_leftOrthogonal_self
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a triangulated category and let `B` be a triangulated subcategory of `C`. Then
the objects `X` of `C` that fit in a distinguished triangle `A ⟶ X ⟶ B' ⟶ A⟦1⟧` with `A` in the
left orthogonal of `B` and `B'` in `B` form a triangulated subcategory of `C`: they are stable
under shifts, two out of three of them in a distinguished triangle forces the third, and they are
stable under direct sums. This is the property `P` of [Stacks, Tag 0H0N].
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_extensionProduct_leftOrthogonal_self (B : ObjectProperty C)
    [B.IsTriangulated] :
    (B.leftOrthogonal.extensionProduct B).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.tfae_isRightAdmissible_isLeftAdmissible_extensionProduct_and_isEquivalence_ι_comp
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a triangulated category and let `A B : ObjectProperty C` be strictly full and
invariant under all shifts. Then: `A` is right admissible with `B = Aᗮ` if and only if `B` is left
admissible with `A = ᗮB` if and only if `Hom(A', B') = 0` for `A'` in `A` and `B'` in `B` and every
object `X` of `C` fits in a distinguished triangle `A' ⟶ X ⟶ B' ⟶ A'⟦1⟧` with `A' ∈ A`, `B' ∈ B`.
If this holds, then for every Verdier quotient `L : C ⥤ Q` of `C` by `B`, i.e. every localization
of `C` at `B.trW`, the composite `A.ι ⋙ L : A ⥤ Q` is an equivalence and a right adjoint of the
inclusion `A.ι` is `L ⋙ G` for some `G : Q ⥤ A`, necessarily a quasi-inverse of `A.ι ⋙ L`; and
dually for the Verdier quotient of `C` by `A`, the inclusion `B.ι` and its left adjoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isRightAdmissible_isLeftAdmissible_extensionProduct_and_isEquivalence_ι_comp
    (A B : ObjectProperty C) [A.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] [B.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
    [A.IsStableUnderShift ℤ] [B.IsStableUnderShift ℤ] :
    [A.IsRightAdmissible ∧ B = A.rightOrthogonal,
      B.IsLeftAdmissible ∧ A = B.leftOrthogonal,
      A ≤ B.leftOrthogonal ∧ A.extensionProduct B = ⊤].TFAE ∧
    (A ≤ B.leftOrthogonal → A.extensionProduct B = ⊤ →
      (∀ {Q : Type w} [Category.{w'} Q] (L : C ⥤ Q) [L.IsLocalization B.trW],
          (A.ι ⋙ L).IsEquivalence ∧
            ∃ G : Q ⥤ A.FullSubcategory, Nonempty (A.ι ⊣ L ⋙ G)) ∧
      (∀ {Q : Type w} [Category.{w'} Q] (L : C ⥤ Q) [L.IsLocalization A.trW],
          (B.ι ⋙ L).IsEquivalence ∧
            ∃ G : Q ⥤ B.FullSubcategory, Nonempty (L ⋙ G ⊣ B.ι)))

declarations.name: CplxCplx.total_H0_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0H0Q (Lemma 15.105.1).**
Let `A_0^• → A_1^• → ⋯` be a complex of complexes of abelian groups such that
`H^{-p}(A_p^•) = 0` for all `p ≥ 0`.  Then `H^0(Tot_π(A^{•,•})) = 0`, i.e. every
degree-`0` cocycle of the product total complex is a coboundary: every
`x ∈ Tot_π^0` with `D^0 x = 0` is `D^{-1} y` for some `y ∈ Tot_π^{-1}`.
(Together with `D ∘ D = 0`, recorded in `totalD_totalD_eq_zero` below, this says
exactly that `ker(D^0) = im(D^{-1})`, i.e. `H^0(Tot_π) = 0`.)

Rigorous proof (recursion on `p`; see the block comment above for the math).
Build, by `Nat.rec`, a dependent stream
`Y : (p : ℕ) → Σ' (yp : c.A p (-1 - (p:ℤ))), c.StageInvariant x p yp` such that the
component equation of `D^{-1} (fun p => (Y p).fst) = x` holds at every `p`; set
`y p := (Y p).fst`.
* **Base (`Y 0`).**  `d_eq_zero_of_totalD_eq_zero` says `x 0` is a `0`-cocycle, so `hH 0`
  (after reconciling `0 - ↑0 = -↑0`) yields `w` with
  `d_2(w) = x_0`; take `(Y 0).fst := w`.  `StageInvariant x 0 w` reduces (`(-1)^0 = 1`) to
  `f_0(d_2 w) = f_0(x_0)`, immediate from `d_2 w = x_0`.
* **Step (`Y (p+1)` from `Y p`).**  Let `yp := (Y p).fst`, `hinv := (Y p).snd`.
  `d_sub_eq_zero_of_stageInvariant c hx hinv` shows `r_{p+1} = x_{p+1} - f_p(yp)` is a
  `(-(p+1))`-cocycle, so `hH (p+1)` yields `w'` with
  `d_2(w') = (-1)^{p+1} r_{p+1}` (scale the witness by `(-1)^{p+1}`, valid since
  `(-1)^{p+1}` is a unit; or equivalently apply `hH` to `(-1)^{p+1} r_{p+1}`,
  which is also a cocycle).  Take `(Y (p+1)).fst := w'`.  Then `StageInvariant x (p+1) w'`
  follows because `f_{p+1}(d_2 w') = (-1)^{p+1} f_{p+1}(r_{p+1}) =
  (-1)^{p+1}(f_{p+1}(x_{p+1}) - f_{p+1}(f_p yp)) = (-1)^{p+1} f_{p+1}(x_{p+1})`
  using `c.f_f p` (`f_{p+1}∘f_p = 0`).
Finally `c.totalD (-1) y = x` by `funext p`, `cases p`, reading off the recorded
construction equations (the `p=0` and `p+1` cases of `totalD_apply_zero` /
`totalD_apply_succ`, `dPartHom_apply`, `fPartHom_apply`).
declarations.statement:
theorem total_H0_eq_zero (c : CplxCplx)
    (hH : ∀ p : ℕ, c.InternalCohomologyVanishes p)
    (x : c.Tot 0) (hx : c.totalD 0 x = 0) :
    ∃ y : c.Tot (-1), c.totalD (-1) y = x

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.main_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 21.43.4 (tag 0H0R).** The adjunction `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` along the morphism of sites
`f : (C, O) → (pt, O(X))` of a terminal object `X` exhibits `Lf^*` and `Rf_*` as mutually
quasi-inverse equivalences between `D(O(X))` and `QC(O)`: the derived pullback lands in `QC(O)`,
the unit is invertible on all of `D(O(X))`, and the counit is invertible on every object of
`QC(O)`.

Both the base change and the derived pullback are the library's own constructions here — the
canonical base-change datum, and the morphism of sites of `X` — so the only hypothesis is the
commutativity `hO` of the section rings of `O`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_equivalence (hO : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x y : O.obj U), x * y = y * x) :
    (∀ P, IsQC.{w} (baseChangeDataOfComm.{r, v, u, w} O hO)
        ((morphismOfSites O hO hX).Lpullback.obj P)) ∧
    (∀ P : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v r w} (O.obj (Opposite.op X))),
      IsIso ((morphismOfSites O hO hX).adj.unit.app P)) ∧
    (∀ K, IsQC.{w} (baseChangeDataOfComm.{r, v, u, w} O hO) K →
      IsIso ((morphismOfSites O hO hX).adj.counit.app K))

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.MorphismsOverAnObject.homDerivedRestriction_bijective
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a derived module with cartesian derived sections and let `M` be an arbitrary derived
module. Applying derived sections over the terminal object `id_U` of `C/U` and conjugating by
`derivedSectionsIso` identifies the morphisms `K|_U ⟶ M|_U` in `D(O_U)` with the morphisms
`RΓ(U, K) ⟶ RΓ(U, M)` in `D(O(U))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homDerivedRestriction_bijective
    (hO : ∀ (V : Cᵒᵖ) (x y : O.obj V), x * y = y * x)
    (K M : DMod.{w} O)
    (hK : IsQC.{w} (baseChangeDataOfComm.{r, v, u, w} O hO) K) :
    Function.Bijective (fun f : (derivedRestriction.{w} O U).obj K ⟶
        (derivedRestriction.{w} O U).obj M =>
      ((derivedSectionsIso.{w} O U).app K).inv ≫
        (RGamma.{w} (overRingPresheaf O U)
          (Opposite.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).map f ≫
        ((derivedSectionsIso.{w} O U).app M).hom)

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.ChaoticComparison.homEpsilonPullback_bijective
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be an object of `QC(O)` and let `M` be an arbitrary object of `D((O_U)_τ)`.
Transposing under the adjunction `ε^* ⊣ Rε_*` over `C/U` and then taking derived sections over the
terminal object `id_U` of `C/U` identifies the morphisms `ε^*(K|_U) ⟶ M` of `D((O_U)_τ)` with the
morphisms `RΓ(U, K) ⟶ RΓ(U, Rε_*M)` of `D(O(U))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homEpsilonPullback_bijective
    (hO : ∀ (V : Cᵒᵖ) (x y : R.obj.obj V), x * y = y * x)
    (K : DMod.{w} R.obj)
    (hK : IsQC.{w} (baseChangeDataOfComm.{r, v, u, w} R.obj hO) K)
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} (overRingSheaf R U))) :
    Function.Bijective (fun f : (epsilonPullback.{w} (overRingSheaf R U)).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((derivedRestriction.{w} R.obj U).obj K) ⟶ M =>
      ((derivedSectionsIso.{w} R.obj U).app K).inv ≫
        (RGamma.{w} (overRingPresheaf R.obj U) (Opposite.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).map
          ((derivedEpsilonAdjunction.{w} (overRingSheaf R U)).unit.app
              ((derivedRestriction.{w} R.obj U).obj K) ≫
            (derivedEpsilonPushforward.{w} (overRingSheaf R U)).map f))
declarations.comment: morphisms out of a sheafified cartesian object are maps of derived sections over U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineFppf.isIso_derivedComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0U.** For a complex `M^•` of `A`-modules the canonical map
`M^• ⟶ RΓ((Aff/S)_fppf, F^•)` is a quasi-isomorphism, where `F^•` is the complex of sheaves of
`𝒪`-modules `U ↦ M^• ⊗_A Γ(U, 𝒪_U)` on the big affine fppf site of `S = Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_derivedComparison
    (RGamma : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B A hS)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (unit : homotopyGlobalSections B A hS ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RGamma)
    (hRGamma : RGamma.IsRightDerivedFunctor unit
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B A hS))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) :
    IsIso (derivedComparison B A hS RGamma unit M)
declarations.comment: the canonical map to derived global sections is a quasi-isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineFppf.isIso_derivedComparison_totalRightDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0U for the canonical derived functor.** The conclusion of
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineFppf.isIso_derivedComparison` with no derived-functor parameter
left: for the total right derived functor of global sections supplied by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.totalRightDerived`, the canonical map
`M^• ⟶ RΓ((Aff/S)_fppf, F^•)` is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_derivedComparison_totalRightDerived
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) :
    IsIso (derivedComparison B A hS
      ((homotopyGlobalSections B A hS).totalRightDerived DerivedCategory.Qh
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B A hS))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
      ((homotopyGlobalSections B A hS).totalRightDerivedUnit DerivedCategory.Qh
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B A hS))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) M)
declarations.comment: the canonical map M^• ⟶ RΓ((Aff/S)_fppf, F^•) is a quasi-isomorphism, for the canonical total right derived functor of global sections -- no derived-functor parameter assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineFppf.baseChangePresheaf_map_smul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0U.** Restriction in the base-change presheaf is semilinear over restriction of
functions: the rule `U ↦ M ⊗_A Γ(U, 𝒪_U)` is a presheaf of `𝒪`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem baseChangePresheaf_map_smul (M : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    ⦃X Y : (BigAffineFppf B (Spec A) hS)ᵒᵖ⦄ (φ : X ⟶ Y)
    (r : (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf (Spec A) (toOver B A hS)).obj X)
    (m : (baseChangePresheaf B A hS M).obj X) :
    (baseChangePresheaf B A hS M).map φ (r • m) =
        (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf (Spec A) (toOver B A hS)).map φ r •
        (baseChangePresheaf B A hS M).map φ m
declarations.comment: the rule is a presheaf of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineFppf.baseChangePresheaf_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0U.** Each term of the rule `U ↦ M ⊗_A Γ(U, 𝒪_U)` is a sheaf: a complex of
`A`-modules gives a complex of modules, not merely a complex of presheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem baseChangePresheaf_isSheaf (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (affineTopology B A hS) (baseChangePresheaf B A hS M)
declarations.comment: the rule is a complex of modules, not only of presheaves of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigAffineFppf.baseChangeComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0U.** The complex `F^•` of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules attached to a complex `M^•`
of `A`-modules: in degree `n` it is the rule `U ↦ M^n ⊗_A Γ(U, 𝒪_U)`, with the base changes of
the differentials of `M^•`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev baseChangeComplex : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ ⥤
    CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B A hS)) ℤ
declarations.comment: the displayed rule on a complex is a complex of modules

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.sectionsProductSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0V**, the spectral sequence. For a cochain complex `Z^•` of abelian sheaves on
the total site of a simplicial-site situation, with no boundedness hypothesis, the filtration
`F^i Tot_π^n = ∏_{p + q = n, p ≥ i} Γ(C_p, Z^q_p)` of the product totalization of
`A^{p,q} = Γ(C_p, Z^q_p)` by the simplicial coordinate has a spectral sequence.

For `Z^•` a K-injective complex of injectives representing `K` in `D(C_total)` this is the
spectral sequence the source constructs; as in the source, no convergence is asserted.
declarations.statement: def sectionsProductSpectralSequence : CohomologicalSpectralSequence Ab.{u} 0
declarations.comment:
the spectral sequence of the filtration by the simplicial coordinate of the
product totalization, for a complex that is not bounded below; the identification of the first
page with `H^q(C_p, K_p)` is not carried

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.sectionsProductSpectralSequenceZeroPageIso
declarations.doc:
**`E_0^{p,q} = Γ(C_p, Z^q_p)`**: the zeroth page of the spectral sequence of Stacks 0H0V is
the complex of sections over `C_p` of the restriction of `Z^q`.

The isomorphism is pinned by
`HomologicalComplex₂.π_productTotalColumnZeroPageIso_hom`: it carries the class of an element of
`F^p Tot_π^{p+q}` to its component in simplicial degree `p`.
declarations.comment: the zeroth page of the spectral sequence is `Γ(C_p, Z^q_p)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.sectionsProductSpectralSequenceOnePageIso
declarations.doc:
**`E_1^{p,q} = H^q(Γ(C_p, Z^•_p))`**: the first page of the spectral sequence of Stacks 0H0V
is the `q`-th cohomology of the complex of sections over `C_p` of the restriction of `Z^•`,
not the `H^q(C_p, K_p)` of the statement of Stacks 0H0V.
declarations.statement:
def sectionsProductSpectralSequenceOnePageIso (p : ℕ) (q : ℤ) :
    ((S.sectionsProductSpectralSequence Z).page 1 zero_le_one).X ((p : ℤ), q) ≅
      (((S.componentSectionsFunctor ⦋p⦌).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj Z).homology q
declarations.comment: the first page of the spectral sequence is `H^q(Γ(C_p, Z^•_p))`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.sectionsProductSpectralSequencePageOneAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0V, the first page: `E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, K_p)`.** For `I^•` a K-injective complex
of abelian sheaves on the total site representing `K` in `D(C_total)`, the first page of the
spectral sequence of the filtration by the simplicial coordinate of the product totalization of
`A^{p,q} = Γ(C_p, I^q_p)` is the cohomology of the component site `C_p` of the restriction `K_p`.

No boundedness hypothesis is made on `I^•`, as in the source. Cohomology is written in its
derived-Hom form, and `K_p` is the restriction of `K = Q(I^•)` to the component in simplicial
degree `p`; the proof uses that restriction to a component preserves K-injectivity, which is
Stacks 09WH.
declarations.statement:
def sectionsProductSpectralSequencePageOneAddEquiv
    (I : CochainComplex (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] (p : ℕ) (q : ℤ) :
    (((S.sectionsProductSpectralSequence I).page 1 zero_le_one).X ((p : ℤ), q)) ≃+
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌) Ab.{u}) 0).obj
          (integerSheaf (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌)) ⟶
        ((S.componentRestrictionDerived ⦋p⦌).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I))⟦q⟧)
declarations.comment:
the first page of the spectral sequence is `H^q(C_p, K_p)`, for a complex that is
not bounded below

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.quasiIso_totalSectionsToProductTotal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0V, `Tot_π(A^{•,•}) = RΓ(C_total, K)`.** For `I^•` a K-injective complex of
abelian sheaves on the total site, the comparison from the complex of global sections
`Γ(C_total, I^•)` — which is `RΓ(C_total, K)` for `K = Q(I^•)` — to the product totalization of
`A^{p,q} = Γ(C_p, I^q_p)` is a quasi-isomorphism.

This is the source's chain of equalities. The global sections complex is the Hom complex out of
the constant integer sheaf `Z`, which is `R Hom(Z, K)`; the integral resolution
`… → g_{2!}Z → g_{1!}Z → g_{0!}Z` of Stacks 09WI resolves `Z`, so for the K-injective target
`I^•` the Hom complex out of it computes the same thing; and that Hom complex is the product
totalization of `A^{p,q} = Hom(g_{p!}Z, I^q) = Γ(C_p, I^q_p)`. No boundedness hypothesis is made
on `I^•`: K-injectivity is what replaces it.
declarations.statement:
instance quasiIso_totalSectionsToProductTotal
    (I : CochainComplex (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    QuasiIso (S.totalSectionsToProductTotal I)
declarations.comment:
`Tot_π(A^{•,•}) = RΓ(C_total, K)` for a K-injective representative, as a
quasi-isomorphism of complexes

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.sectionsProductTotalHomologyAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0V, `Tot_π(A^{•,•}) = RΓ(C_total, K)` degreewise on cohomology**:
`H^n(Tot_π(A^{•,•})) = H^n(C_total, K)`.

Cohomology is written in its derived-Hom form, so the right-hand side is literally the source's
`R Hom(Z, K)` in degree `n`, which is `RΓ(C_total, K)` because the first equality of the source
"holds in any site".
declarations.statement:
def sectionsProductTotalHomologyAddEquiv
    (I : CochainComplex (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] (n : ℤ) :
    ((S.sectionsProductTotal I).homology n) ≃+
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) 0).obj S.totalIntegerSheaf ⟶
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: `H^n(Tot_π(A^{•,•})) = H^n(C_total, K)` for a K-injective representative

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.quasiIso_globalSectionsToProductTotal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0V, `Γ(C_total, I^•) = Tot_π(A^{•,•})`.** For `I^•` a K-injective complex of
abelian sheaves on the total site, the comparison from its complex of global sections to the
product totalization of `A^{p,q} = Γ(C_p, I^q_p)` is a quasi-isomorphism. This is the previous
statement with its source written as the complex of global sections rather than as the Hom
complex out of the constant integer sheaf.
declarations.statement:
instance quasiIso_globalSectionsToProductTotal
    (I : CochainComplex (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    QuasiIso (S.globalSectionsToProductTotal I)
declarations.comment:
`Γ(C_total, I^•) = Tot_π(A^{•,•})` for a K-injective complex, as a
quasi-isomorphism of complexes

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.unboundedSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0V, the spectral sequence of an object `K` of `D(C_total)` with no boundedness
hypothesis**: the spectral sequence of
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.sectionsProductSpectralSequence` for the chosen
K-injective complex with injective terms representing `K`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev unboundedSpectralSequence (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) :
    CohomologicalSpectralSequence Ab.{u} 0
declarations.comment:
the spectral sequence of an arbitrary object of the unbounded derived category of
the total site

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.unboundedSpectralSequencePageOneAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0V, the first page: `E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, K_p)`** for an arbitrary object `K` of
`D(C_total)`.

The first differential of the first page of a cohomological spectral sequence has bidegree
`(1, 0)` by construction, so under this identification it is a map
`H^q(C_p, K_p) → H^q(C_{p + 1}, K_{p + 1})`, as the source's reference to Stacks 09WJ asks.
declarations.statement:
def unboundedSpectralSequencePageOneAddEquiv
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) (p : ℕ) (q : ℤ) :
    (((S.unboundedSpectralSequence K).page 1 zero_le_one).X ((p : ℤ), q)) ≃+
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌) Ab.{u}) 0).obj
          (integerSheaf (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌)) ⟶
        ((S.componentRestrictionDerived ⦋p⦌).obj K)⟦q⟧)
declarations.comment:
the first page is `E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, K_p)`, for an arbitrary object of the
unbounded derived category of the total site
