declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.unboundedProductTotalHomologyAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0V, `Tot_π(A^{•,•}) = RΓ(C_total, K)`** for an arbitrary object `K` of
`D(C_total)`, degreewise on cohomology.
declarations.statement:
def unboundedProductTotalHomologyAddEquiv
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) (n : ℤ) :
    ((S.sectionsProductTotal (S.totalKInjectiveModel K)).homology n) ≃+
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) 0).obj S.totalIntegerSheaf ⟶
        K⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment:
`H^n(Tot_π(A^{•,•})) = H^n(C_total, K)` for an arbitrary object of the unbounded
derived category of the total site

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.subsingleton_hom_totalIntegerSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0W (1).** In the situation of Stacks 09WE, let `K` be an object of
`D(C_total)`. If `H^{-p}(C_p, K_p) = 0` for all `p ≥ 0`, then `H^0(C_total, K) = 0`.

Cohomology is written in its derived-Hom form: `H^i(C, K)` is the group of morphisms from the
constant integer sheaf of `C`, placed in degree zero, to `K[i]`; and the restriction `K_p` of
`K` to the component in simplicial degree `p` is `componentRestrictionDerived S ⦋p⦌` applied
to `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_hom_totalIntegerSheaf
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}))
    (h : ∀ p : ℕ, Subsingleton
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌) Ab.{u}) 0).obj
          (integerSheaf (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌)) ⟶
        ((componentRestrictionDerived S ⦋p⦌).obj K)⟦-(p : ℤ)⟧)) :
    Subsingleton ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) 0).obj
      S.totalIntegerSheaf ⟶ K)
declarations.comment: part (1): vanishing of H^0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.subsingleton_hom_totalIntegerSheaf_shift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0W (2).** In the situation of Stacks 09WE, let `K` be an object of
`D(C_total)`. If `RΓ(C_p, K_p) = 0` for all `p ≥ 0`, then `RΓ(C_total, K) = 0`.

Vanishing of `RΓ` is the vanishing of every cohomology group, written in derived-Hom form as in
`subsingleton_hom_totalIntegerSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_hom_totalIntegerSheaf_shift
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}))
    (h : ∀ (p : ℕ) (i : ℤ), Subsingleton
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌) Ab.{u}) 0).obj
          (integerSheaf (S.componentTopology ⦋p⦌)) ⟶
        ((componentRestrictionDerived S ⦋p⦌).obj K)⟦i⟧)) (i : ℤ) :
    Subsingleton ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) 0).obj
      S.totalIntegerSheaf ⟶ K⟦i⟧)
declarations.comment: part (2): vanishing of RΓ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyKFlatAcyclic_affineFppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0X, hypothesis (2) of Stacks 0GZS.** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` be a category
fibred in groupoids and `ε : (𝒳_{affine, fppf}, O) ⟶ (𝒳_{affine}, O)` the comparison morphism to
the associated affine site with its chaotic topology.  For every object `x` of `𝒳_{affine}` and
every K-flat complex `M^•` of `O(x)`-modules the canonical map
`M^• ⟶ RΓ((𝒳_{affine, fppf}/x), (M^• ⊗_{O(x)} O_x)^#)` is a quasi-isomorphism.  (Hypothesis
(1) of Stacks 0GZS, that the target topology is chaotic, is the construction of `ε`: modules on
the chaotic site are presheaves of modules.)
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyKFlatAcyclic_affineFppf :
    IsLocallyKFlatAcyclic.{t}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (AffineCategory.siteKindRingedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).O)
      (affineStructurePresheaf_comm B S hS p)
declarations.comment: ε : 𝒳_{affine,fppf} ⟶ 𝒳_{affine} satisfies the assumptions of Stacks 0GZS: hypothesis (2), the target being the chaotic site by construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineFppfQuasiCoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0X, the conclusion of Stacks 0GZS.** For a category fibred in groupoids
`p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` and the comparison `ε : (𝒳_{affine, fppf}, O) ⟶ (𝒳_{affine}, O)`,
`ε^*` and `Rε_*` are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between `QC(𝒳)` (Stacks 0H0H) and the
full subcategory of `D(𝒳_{affine, fppf}, O)` of the objects `K` with `Rε_*K` in `QC(𝒳)`.  The
functor of the equivalence is `ε^*` and its inverse is `Rε_*`, both on the nose
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineQuasiCoherentEquivalence_functor` and `_inverse`).
declarations.comment: ε : 𝒳_{affine,fppf} ⟶ 𝒳_{affine} satisfies the conclusions of Stacks 0GZS: ε^* and Rε_* are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between QC(𝒳) and the objects K of D(𝒳_{affine,fppf}, O) with Rε_*K in QC(𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction_counit_constantSheaf_of_isTerminal
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic stack `𝒳` whose flat-fppf site has a terminal object `e` whose image is
terminal in the fppf site, the counit of the derived adjunction `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹` is invertible at the
constant sheaf `ℤ` of `𝒳_{fppf}` in degree zero, so the canonical comparison `Lg_! ℤ ⟶ ℤ` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction_counit_constantSheaf_of_isTerminal
    {e : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳)} (he : IsTerminal e)
    (heX : IsTerminal ((objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.obj e)) :
    IsIso ((derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction B S hS 𝒳
          (abelianLowerShriekAcyclic B S hS 𝒳)).counit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((constantSheaf (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
            (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))))
declarations.comment: for the `Lg_!` of 07AS part (3), the flat-fppf site of an algebraic stack whose flat-fppf site has a terminal object whose image is terminal in the fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction_counit_constantSheaf_schemeStack
declarations.doc:
For the stack of a scheme `U`, the counit of the derived adjunction `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹` is invertible
at the constant sheaf `ℤ` of `(Sch/U)_{fppf}` in degree zero, so the canonical comparison
`Lg_! ℤ ⟶ ℤ` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction_counit_constantSheaf_schemeStack :
    IsIso ((derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U)
          (abelianLowerShriekAcyclic B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U))).counit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((constantSheaf (fppfTopology B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))))
declarations.comment: for the `Lg_!` of 07AS part (3), the flat-fppf site of the stack of a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.derivedAbelianLowerShriek_constantSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H0Z.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack. Then `Lg_! ℤ = ℤ`, both for the `Lg_!` of
Stacks 07AS part (1) — `D(𝒳_{lisse,étale}) ⟶ D(𝒳_{étale})` — and for the `Lg_!` of part (3) —
`D(𝒳_{flat,fppf}) ⟶ D(𝒳_{fppf})`.

For each of the two sites the statement has two clauses: the derived lower shriek of the constant
sheaf `ℤ` of the subsite in degree zero is isomorphic to the constant sheaf `ℤ` of `𝒳` in degree
zero, and the canonical map realizing this — the counit of `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹` at `ℤ[0]`, whose source is
`Lg_!(g⁻¹ℤ) = Lg_! ℤ` — is an isomorphism. Nothing is assumed beyond `𝒳` being algebraic.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedAbelianLowerShriek_constantSheaf :
    (Nonempty ((LisseEtale.derivedAbelianLowerShriek.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((constantSheaf (LisseEtale.inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
            AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
        ((constantSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))) ∧
      IsIso ((LisseEtale.derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).counit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((constantSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))))) ∧
    (Nonempty ((FlatFppf.derivedAbelianLowerShriekFunctor B S hS 𝒳).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((constantSheaf (FlatFppf.inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
            (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
        ((constantSheaf (FlatFppf.fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))) ∧
      IsIso ((FlatFppf.derivedAbelianLowerShriekFunctorAdjunction B S hS 𝒳).counit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((constantSheaf (FlatFppf.fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
            (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ))))))
declarations.comment: both cases of the statement, for every algebraic stack and with nothing assumed: the `Lg_!` of 07AS part (1) (lisse-étale) and of 07AS part (3) (flat-fppf). For each, the first clause is `Lg_!(ℤ[0]) ≅ ℤ[0]` and the second is invertibility of the canonical map, the counit of `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹` at `ℤ[0]`. Both `Lg_!` are the unconditional ones of 07AS (1) and (3); the cohomology comparison of 07AK that the proof runs on is the unconditional `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.globalCohomologyIso` resp. `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.globalCohomologyIso`, so neither `g_!ℤ = ℤ` nor the acyclicity of 0D6X is a hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedGlobalSectionsRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (2)(a), for complexes, with no hypothesis.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic
stack and let `g : Sh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_{fppf})` be the comparison morphism of topoi of
Stacks 08MZ, whose inverse image is restriction to the flat objects. For every `K` in the
unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on `𝒳_{fppf}`,

`RΓ(𝒳_{flat,fppf}, g⁻¹K) = RΓ(𝒳_{fppf}, K)`,

naturally in `K`, where on each side `RΓ` is the total right derived functor of global sections
(`Sheaf.Γ`, the right adjoint of the constant sheaf functor).

The proof is the source's: global sections are corepresented by `ℤ`, and `Lg_! ℤ = ℤ`
(Stacks 0H0Z, `isIso_derivedAbelianLowerShriekFunctorAdjunction_counit_constantSheaf`)
turns the derived adjunction `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹` of Stacks 07AS (3) into the comparison.
declarations.comment: part (2)(a) for complexes, at the flat-fppf site, with NO hypothesis: RΓ(𝒳_{flat,fppf}, g⁻¹K) = RΓ(𝒳_{fppf}, K), from Lg_! ℤ = ℤ (Tag 0H0Z, proved)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.derivedGlobalSectionsRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (1)(a), for complexes, with no hypothesis.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic
stack and let `g : Sh(𝒳_{lisse,étale}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_{étale})` be the comparison morphism of topoi of
Stacks 08MZ, whose inverse image is restriction to the smooth objects. For every `K` in the
unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on `𝒳_{étale}`,

`RΓ(𝒳_{lisse,étale}, g⁻¹K) = RΓ(𝒳_{étale}, K)`,

naturally in `K`, where on each side `RΓ` is the total right derived functor of global sections
(`Sheaf.Γ`, the right adjoint of the constant sheaf functor).

The proof is the source's: global sections are corepresented by `ℤ`, and `Lg_! ℤ = ℤ`
(Stacks 0H0Z, `LisseEtale.isIso_derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction_counit_constantSheaf`)
turns the derived adjunction `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹` of Stacks 07AS (1) into the comparison.
declarations.comment: part (1)(a) for complexes, at the lisse-étale site, with NO hypothesis: RΓ(𝒳_{lisse,étale}, g⁻¹K) = RΓ(𝒳_{étale}, K), from Lg_! ℤ = ℤ (Tag 0H0Z, proved)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedModuleGlobalSectionsRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (2)(a), for sheaves of modules.** For every `K` in the unbounded derived
category of sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_{fppf}`,
`RΓ(𝒳_{flat,fppf}, g^*K) = RΓ(𝒳_{fppf}, K)`, naturally in `K`, both sides computed on complexes
of modules; `𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}} = g⁻¹𝒪_𝒳` and `g^* = g⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedModuleGlobalSectionsRestrictionIso :
    haveI := hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_inclusion_ab.{u, w, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳
    (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLowerShriek.BigSite.moduleInverseImage (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
        (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)
        (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        derivedModuleOf (restrictedRing (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)
          (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳))
          (Sheaf.Γ (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ≅
      derivedModuleOf (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)
        (Sheaf.Γ (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
declarations.comment: part (2)(a) for sheaves of modules (the closing sentence of the statement), with NO hypothesis: derived global sections on the flat-fppf site of g^*K, computed on complexes of modules, are those of K on the fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedModuleSectionsRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (2)(b), for sheaves of modules.** For every object `x` of the flat-fppf
site and every `K` in the unbounded derived category of sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on
`𝒳_{fppf}`, `RΓ(x, g^*K) = RΓ(x, K)`, naturally in `K`, both sides computed on complexes of
modules, cohomology over `x` being the derived functor of sections over `x`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedModuleSectionsRestrictionIso
    (x : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳)) :
    haveI := hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_inclusion_ab.{u, w, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳
    (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLowerShriek.BigSite.moduleInverseImage (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
        (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)
        (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        derivedModuleOf (restrictedRing (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)
          (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳))
          (abelianSections.{u + 1} (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) x) ≅
      derivedModuleOf (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)
        (abelianSections.{u + 1} (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) ((objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.obj x))
declarations.comment: part (2)(b) for sheaves of modules (the closing sentence of the statement), with NO hypothesis; cohomology over an object is the derived functor of sections over it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.derivedModuleGlobalSectionsRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (1)(a), for sheaves of modules.** For every `K` in the unbounded derived
category of sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_{étale}`,
`RΓ(𝒳_{lisse,étale}, g^*K) = RΓ(𝒳_{étale}, K)`, naturally in `K`, both sides computed on
complexes of modules; `𝒪_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}} = g⁻¹𝒪_𝒳` and `g^* = g⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedModuleGlobalSectionsRestrictionIso :
    haveI := isContinuous_inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    haveI := isCocontinuous_inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
      (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLowerShriek.BigSite.moduleInverseImage
        (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
        (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
        (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        derivedModuleOf (restrictedRing (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
          (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳))
          (Sheaf.Γ (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ≅
      derivedModuleOf (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)
        (Sheaf.Γ (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
declarations.comment: part (1)(a) for sheaves of modules (the closing sentence of the statement), with NO hypothesis: derived global sections on the lisse-étale site of g^*K, computed on complexes of modules, are those of K on the étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.derivedModuleSectionsRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (1)(b), for sheaves of modules.** For every object `x` of the
lisse-étale site and every `K` in the unbounded derived category of sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on
`𝒳_{étale}`, `RΓ(x, g^*K) = RΓ(x, K)`, naturally in `K`, both sides computed on complexes of
modules, cohomology over `x` being the derived functor of sections over `x`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedModuleSectionsRestrictionIso (x : LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) :
    haveI := isContinuous_inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    haveI := isCocontinuous_inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
      (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLowerShriek.BigSite.moduleInverseImage
        (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
        (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
        (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        derivedModuleOf (restrictedRing (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
          (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳))
          (abelianSections.{u + 1} (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) x) ≅
      derivedModuleOf (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)
        (abelianSections.{u + 1} (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
          ((smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι.obj x))
declarations.comment: part (1)(b) for sheaves of modules (the closing sentence of the statement), with NO hypothesis; cohomology over an object is the derived functor of sections over it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedSectionsRestrictionIsoOfFlatObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (2)(b), for complexes, with no hypothesis.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic
stack and let `g : Sh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_{fppf})` be the comparison morphism of topoi of
Stacks 08MZ, whose inverse image is restriction to the flat objects. For every object `x` of the
flat-fppf site and every `K` in the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on
`𝒳_{fppf}`,

`RΓ(𝒳_{flat,fppf}/x, g⁻¹K) = RΓ(x, K)`,

naturally in `K`, where on each side cohomology over `x` is the right derived functor of sections
over `x` on the respective site (the convention of Stacks 0DD8 here; it is cohomology of the
slice site by Stacks 03F3). This is `derivedSectionsRestrictionIso` with its hypothesis `hgen`
proved, by `derivedLowerShriekComputesFlatGenerator`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSectionsRestrictionIsoOfFlatObject
    (x : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳)) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLowerShriek.derivedAbelianRestriction.{u + 1}
          (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι ⋙
        derivedSections B S hS 𝒳 x ≅
      derivedSectionsFppf B S hS 𝒳 ((objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.obj x)
declarations.comment: part (2)(b) for complexes, at the flat-fppf site, with NO hypothesis: the half of Tag 0794 that `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedSectionsRestrictionIso` carries as `hgen` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedLowerShriekComputesFlatGenerator`. Cohomology over an object is the derived functor of sections over it (equal to cohomology of the slice site by Tag 03F3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.derivedSectionsRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (1)(b), for complexes, with no hypothesis.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic
stack and let `g : Sh(𝒳_{lisse,étale}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_{étale})` be the comparison morphism of topoi of
Stacks 08MZ, whose inverse image is restriction to the smooth objects. For every object `x` of
the lisse-étale site and every `K` in the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on
`𝒳_{étale}`,

`RΓ(𝒳_{lisse,étale}/x, g⁻¹K) = RΓ(x, K)`,

naturally in `K`, where on each side cohomology over `x` is the right derived functor of sections
over `x` on the respective site (the convention of Stacks 0DD8 here; it is cohomology of the
slice site by Stacks 03F3).

This is Stacks 0DD8 (1) on sites that need not be small,
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLowerShriek.BigSite.derivedAbelianSectionsRestrictionIso`, at the
lisse-étale inclusion: continuity and cocontinuity come from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.closedUnderSmoothMorphisms`, the existence and absoluteness
of `Lg_!` from `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.abelianLowerShriekAcyclic`, and the counit at
the generator from `derivedLowerShriekComputesSmoothGenerator`.
declarations.comment: part (1)(b) for complexes, at the lisse-étale site, with NO hypothesis. Cohomology over an object is the derived functor of sections over it (equal to cohomology of the slice site by Tag 03F3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedSectionsRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H10, part (2)(b), for complexes.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and let
`g : Sh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_{fppf})` be the comparison morphism of topoi of Stacks 08MZ, whose
inverse image is restriction to the flat objects. For every object `x` of the flat-fppf site and
every `K` in the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on `𝒳_{fppf}`,

`RΓ(x, g⁻¹K) = RΓ(x, K)`,

naturally in `K`, where on each side cohomology over `x` is the right derived functor of sections
over `x` on the respective site (the convention of Stacks 0DD8 and Stacks 03YU here; see the
module docstring on why not the slice site).

The closure condition of Stacks 07AK (1), the existence of `g_!` and `g_*`, Grothendieck
abelianness of both categories of abelian sheaves, and the acyclicity statement of Stacks 07AC
that Stacks 07AS (3) needs are all discharged, with no hypothesis on `𝒳`. The single carried
input is `hgen`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSectionsRestrictionIso
    (x : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳))
    (hgen : DerivedLowerShriekComputesFlatGenerator B S hS 𝒳 x) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLowerShriek.derivedAbelianRestriction.{u + 1}
          (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
          (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι ⋙
        derivedSections B S hS 𝒳 x ≅
      derivedSectionsFppf B S hS 𝒳 ((objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.obj x)
declarations.comment: part (2)(b) for complexes, at the flat-fppf site, with cohomology over an object taken as the derived functor of sections over it; conditional only on the half of Stacks 0794 that computes Lg_! on a generator

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSaturated_derivedParasiticFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H11**, last assertion, inside `D(𝒳_{fppf}, 𝒪_𝒳)`.  The subcategory `𝒜` read in
`D(𝒳_{fppf}, 𝒪_𝒳)`, that is the locally quasi-coherent complexes with flat base change which are
left orthogonal to the parasitic ones, is a strictly full, saturated ([Stacks, Tag 05RB]),
triangulated subcategory of `D(𝒳_{fppf}, 𝒪_𝒳)`.

Strict fullness and triangulatedness are those of a left orthogonal ([Stacks, Tag 0FXC] and
[Stacks, Tag 0CQR]) intersected with `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)`, and saturation is stability under
retracts of a left orthogonal, again [Stacks, Tag 0FXC], intersected with the carried stability
under retracts of `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSaturated_derivedParasiticFree :
    (derivedParasiticFree B E h S hS 𝒳).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      (derivedParasiticFree B E h S hS 𝒳).IsSaturated ∧
      (derivedParasiticFree B E h S hS 𝒳).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the last assertion for D(𝒳_fppf, 𝒪_𝒳): 𝒜, hence D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), read inside D(𝒳_fppf, 𝒪_𝒳) is a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory there

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.parasiticInLQCoh_isLeftAdmissible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H11**, first assertion. The subcategory
`D_{Parasitic ∩ LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳) ⊂ D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` is left admissible: a strictly full
triangulated subcategory whose inclusion has a left adjoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem parasiticInLQCoh_isLeftAdmissible :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticIn B S hS 𝒳
      (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsLeftAdmissible
declarations.comment: the first assertion: D_(Parasitic ∩ LQCoh^fbc)(𝒪_𝒳) ⊂ D_LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) is a left admissible subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.parasiticFreeInLQCoh_isRightAdmissible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H11**, second assertion. The left orthogonal `𝒜` of
`D_{Parasitic ∩ LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` in `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` is right admissible: a strictly full
triangulated subcategory whose inclusion has a right adjoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem parasiticFreeInLQCoh_isRightAdmissible :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFreeIn B S hS 𝒳
      (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsRightAdmissible
declarations.comment: the second assertion: the left orthogonal 𝒜 of D_(Parasitic ∩ LQCoh^fbc)(𝒪_𝒳) is right admissible in D_LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.parasiticFreeInLQCoh_ι_comp_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H11**, third assertion. The composition

`𝒜 ⟶ D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`

of the inclusion of the left orthogonal `𝒜` with the Verdier quotient functor of **Stacks 07B6**
is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem parasiticFreeInLQCoh_ι_comp_isEquivalence :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    ((ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFreeIn B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).ι ⋙
      ParasiticQuotient.toQuotient B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the third assertion: the composition 𝒜 ⟶ D_LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) of the inclusion with the Verdier quotient functor of 07B6 is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.parasiticFreeInLQCoh_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H11**, last assertion, inside `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)`. The left orthogonal `𝒜`, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.parasiticFreeInLQCoh_ι_comp_isEquivalence` identifies with
`D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`, is a strictly full, saturated ([Stacks, Tag 05RB]), triangulated subcategory of
`D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem parasiticFreeInLQCoh_isSaturated :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFreeIn B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFreeIn B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsSaturated ∧
      (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFreeIn B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the last assertion for D_LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳): 𝒜, hence D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), is a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory of D_LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.parasiticFreeInDerivedFppf_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H11**, last assertion, inside `D(𝒳_{fppf}, 𝒪_𝒳)`. The subcategory `𝒜` read in
`D(𝒳_{fppf}, 𝒪_𝒳)` — the complexes with cohomology in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` admitting no nonzero
morphism to `D_{Parasitic ∩ LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` — is a strictly full, saturated, triangulated
subcategory of `D(𝒳_{fppf}, 𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem parasiticFreeInDerivedFppf_isSaturated [HasDerivedCategory (fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)] :
    (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFree B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧
      (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFree B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsSaturated ∧
      (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFree B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the last assertion for D(𝒳_fppf, 𝒪_𝒳): 𝒜, hence D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), read inside D(𝒳_fppf, 𝒪_𝒳) is a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory there

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.parasiticFreeToLQCoh_comp_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H11**, the realization of `D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` inside `D(𝒳_{fppf}, 𝒪_𝒳)`: the inclusion
of `𝒜`, presented as a subcategory of `D(𝒳_{fppf}, 𝒪_𝒳)`, followed by the Verdier quotient
functor of **Stacks 07B6** is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem parasiticFreeToLQCoh_comp_isEquivalence :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (ParasiticQuotient.parasiticFreeToClass B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳) ⋙
      ParasiticQuotient.toQuotient B S hS 𝒳
        (𝓛 B E h S hS 𝒳)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the embedding into D(𝒳_fppf, 𝒪_𝒳): the composition of the inclusion of 𝒜, presented as a subcategory of D(𝒳_fppf, 𝒪_𝒳), with the Verdier quotient functor of 07B6 is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isZero_derivedSectionsFppf_of_parasitic_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H13.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and let `K` be an object of `D(𝒳_{fppf})`
whose cohomology sheaves are parasitic — the sections of every cohomology sheaf of `K` vanish at
every object of `𝒳` lying over a scheme `U` such that `U → 𝒳` is flat (**Stacks 0773**). Then
`RΓ(x, K) = 0` for every such object `x`.

Cohomology over an object is the right derived functor of sections over it. The proof is the
source's: by Stacks 0H10 (2)(b), `RΓ(x, K) = RΓ(x, g⁻¹K)`, and `g⁻¹K = 0` because its cohomology
sheaves are the restrictions of those of `K` to the flat objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_derivedSectionsFppf_of_parasitic_cohomology
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, ∀ y : 𝒳.val.val.obj, flatObject B S hS 𝒳.val y →
      Subsingleton (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (Sheaf (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) n).obj K).obj.obj (op y)))
    (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hx : flatObject B S hS 𝒳.val x) :
    IsZero ((derivedSectionsFppf B S hS 𝒳 x).obj K)
declarations.comment: cohomology over an object taken as the derived functor of sections over it, and the parasitic condition of Stacks 0773 written out on abelian sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isZero_cohomology_of_isZero_derivedSectionsFppf_flatAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H14.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and let `K` be an object of `D(𝒳_{fppf})` such
that `RΓ(x, K) = 0` for every object `x` of `𝒳` lying over an affine scheme `U` with `U → 𝒳`
flat. Then `H^i(𝒳, K) = 0` for all `i`.

Here `RΓ(x, -)` is the right derived functor of sections over `x` (the convention of Stacks 0DD8
and Stacks 0H10 (2)(b) in this library), and `H^i(𝒳, K)` is the `i`-th cohomology of the
unbounded derived global sections `RΓ(𝒳_{fppf}, K)`.

This is the source's proof: `g⁻¹K = 0` because its derived sections vanish on a family covering
the flat-fppf site (Stacks 0H10 (2)(b)), so `RΓ(𝒳_{flat,fppf}, g⁻¹K) = 0`, which is
`RΓ(𝒳_{fppf}, K)` by Stacks 0H10 (2)(a).
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_cohomology_of_isZero_derivedSectionsFppf_flatAffine
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
    (hK : ∀ x : 𝒳.val.val.obj, flatObject B S hS 𝒳.val x →
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (𝒳.val.val.p.obj x)) →
      IsZero ((derivedSectionsFppf B S hS 𝒳 x).obj K))
    (i : ℤ) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} i).obj
      ((AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.derivedGlobalSections.{u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val).obj K))
declarations.comment: unconditional. Cohomology over an object is the derived functor of sections over it (Tag 0DD8 convention, equal to cohomology of the slice site by Tag 03F3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.hasAffineDerivedSectionsBaseChange_derivedModuleLowerShriekSucc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H15.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and `H` an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_{𝒳_{flat, fppf}})` (module universe `u + 1`). Then `Lg_! H` has the following
property: for every morphism `x ⟶ x'` of `𝒳_{affine}` the map
`RΓ(x', Lg_! H) ⊗^L_{𝒪(x')} 𝒪(x) ⟶ RΓ(x, Lg_! H)` is a quasi-isomorphism
(`HasAffineDerivedSectionsBaseChange`). The derived categories are the standard models.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffineDerivedSectionsBaseChange_derivedModuleLowerShriekSucc :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (subsiteRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳))
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳))
    ∀ H : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (subsiteRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)),
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (flatQuasicoherentModulesSucc B S hS 𝒳) H →
        HasAffineDerivedSectionsBaseChange B S hS 𝒳
          ((derivedModuleLowerShriekSucc B S hS 𝒳).obj H)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.quasiCoherentDerivedEquivalenceSucc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H16.** For an algebraic stack `𝒳`, `QC(𝒳)` is canonically equivalent to
`D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`, both at module universe `u + 1` (see the module docstring for why `u + 1`):
`QC(𝒳) ≌ Q_𝒳` by Stacks 0H0X and 0H0C, `Q_𝒳 = 𝒜` by Stacks 0H15, and `𝒜 ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` by
Stacks 0H11, where `D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is the quotient of `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` by
`D_{Parasitic ∩ LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` (Stacks 07B6).
declarations.statement:
def quasiCoherentDerivedEquivalenceSucc :
    quasiCoherentDerived.{u, u + 1, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p ≌
      DerivedCategory.KernelColocalization.quotient (parasiticModulesSucc B S hS 𝒳)
        (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow
declarations.doc:
A **dotted arrow** for the `2`-commutative square with `x : S ⟶ X`, `j : S ⟶ T`,
`f : X ⟶ Y`, `y : T ⟶ Y` and witnessing `2`-morphism `γ : j ≫ y ⟶ x ≫ f`: a diagonal
`1`-morphism `a : T ⟶ X` together with `2`-morphisms `α : j ≫ a ⟶ x` and `β : y ⟶ a ≫ f`
pasting to `γ`.
declarations.statement:
structure DottedArrow {S T X Y : B} (x : S ⟶ X) (j : S ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : T ⟶ Y)
    (γ : (j ≫ y) ⟶ (x ≫ f))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.Hom
declarations.doc:
A **morphism of dotted arrows** `(a, α, β) ⟶ (a', α', β')` is a `2`-morphism
`θ : a ⟶ a'` such that `α = α' ∘ (θ ⋆ id_j)` and `β' = (id_f ⋆ θ) ∘ β`.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (d d' : DottedArrow x j f y γ)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.instCategoryDottedArrow
declarations.doc:
The **category of dotted arrows** for the square and the witness `γ`: objects are dotted
arrows and morphisms are morphisms of dotted arrows.
declarations.statement:
instance instCategoryDottedArrow {S T X Y : B} {x : S ⟶ X} {j : S ⟶ T} {f : X ⟶ Y} {y : T ⟶ Y}
    {γ : (j ≫ y) ⟶ (x ≫ f)} : Category (DottedArrow x j f y γ)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrowBaseChange.dottedArrows_equiv
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Project, Tag 0H1A / Lemma 4.44.2).**

Let `B` be a $(2,1)$-category (a bicategory in which every $2$-morphism is invertible,
encoded by the hypothesis `hgpd`). Given a $2$-commutative diagram with an
outer rectangle decomposed into a left square (with witness `γ'`) and a right square that
is $2$-cartesian (with witness `φ`), the category of dotted arrows `D'` for the left square
and the category of dotted arrows `D` for the outer rectangle (with the induced witness
`γ = outerGamma φ γ'`) are equivalent categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem dottedArrows_equiv
    (hgpd : ∀ {A C : B} {u v : A ⟶ C} (θ : u ⟶ v), IsIso θ)
    {S T X X' Y Y' : B}
    (j : S ⟶ T) (x' : S ⟶ X') (q : X' ⟶ X) (p : X' ⟶ Y') (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (y' : T ⟶ Y') (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (φ : (p ≫ g) ≅ (q ≫ f)) (γ' : (j ≫ y') ≅ (x' ≫ p))
    (hcart : IsTwoCartesian q p f g φ) :
    -- `D'` : dotted arrows for the left square `(x', j, p, y')` with witness `γ'`
    -- `D`  : dotted arrows for the outer rectangle `(x' ≫ q, j, f, y' ≫ g)` with witness `γ`
    Nonempty (IsoDottedArrow x' j p y' γ' ≌
              IsoDottedArrow (x' ≫ q) j f (y' ≫ g) (outerGamma φ γ'))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.toWithFactorization_isEquivalence
declarations.doc: `toWithFactorization` is an equivalence of categories `𝒟 ≌ 𝒟''`.
declarations.statement:
instance toWithFactorization_isEquivalence {S T X Y Z : B} (x : S ⟶ X) (j : S ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (z : T ⟶ Z) (γ : (j ≫ z) ⟶ (x ≫ f ≫ g)) :
    (toWithFactorization x j f g z γ).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.fiber_categoryIso
declarations.doc:
The fibre of `compose` over an object `d'` of `𝒟'` is isomorphic, as a category (a
`CategoryIso`, not merely an equivalence), to the category of dotted arrows of the upper solid
square, whose bottom arrow is `d'.a` and whose witness is `d'.α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiber_categoryIso {S T X Y Z : B}
    (x : S ⟶ X) (j : S ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (z : T ⟶ Z)
    (γ : (j ≫ z) ⟶ (x ≫ f ≫ g))
    (d' : DottedArrow (x ≫ f) j g z (γ ≫ (α_ x f g).inv)) :
    Nonempty (CategoryIso ((compose x j f g z γ).Fiber d')
      (DottedArrow x j f d'.a d'.α))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.compose_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc: `compose : 𝒟'' ⥤ 𝒟'` is fibred in groupoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem compose_isFiberedInGroupoids {S T X Y Z : B} (x : S ⟶ X) (j : S ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (z : T ⟶ Z) (γ : (j ≫ z) ⟶ (x ≫ f ≫ g)) :
    (compose x j f g z γ).IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: exteriorPower.ker_eq_span_of_tprod_eq_ιMulti
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1C.** Let `A → B` be a ring map, let `M` be a `B`-module and let `n ≥ 1`.
The kernel of the canonical `A`-linear map `M ⊗_A ⋯ ⊗_A M → ⋀[B]^n M`,
`m₁ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ mₙ ↦ m₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ mₙ`, is generated as an `A`-module by the pure tensors
`m₁ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ mₙ` with `mᵢ = b • mⱼ` for some `i ≠ j` and `b ∈ B`, together with the
differences `m₁ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ b mᵢ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ mₙ - m₁ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ b mⱼ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ mₙ` for `i ≠ j` and `b ∈ B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorPower.ker_eq_span_of_tprod_eq_ιMulti
    {A B M : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (φ : (⨂[A]^n M) →ₗ[A] ⋀[B]^n M)
    (hφ : ∀ m : Fin n → M, φ (PiTensorProduct.tprod A m) = exteriorPower.ιMulti B n m) :
    LinearMap.ker φ =
      Submodule.span A
        ({x | ∃ (m : Fin n → M) (i j : Fin n) (b : B), i ≠ j ∧ m i = b • m j ∧
              PiTensorProduct.tprod A m = x} ∪
          {x | ∃ (m : Fin n → M) (i j : Fin n) (b : B), i ≠ j ∧
              PiTensorProduct.tprod A (Function.update m i (b • m i)) -
                PiTensorProduct.tprod A (Function.update m j (b • m j)) = x})
declarations.comment: first family `mᵢ = b • mⱼ`, not `mᵢ = mⱼ`: the latter fails for `n = 2`

declarations.name: exteriorPower.ker_eq_span_of_tprod_eq_ιMulti_of_two_lt
declarations.doc:
For `2 < n` the tensors with two equal entries, together with the scaling differences,
already generate the kernel.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorPower.ker_eq_span_of_tprod_eq_ιMulti_of_two_lt
    {A B M : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M] {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 < n)
    (φ : (⨂[A]^n M) →ₗ[A] ⋀[B]^n M)
    (hφ : ∀ m : Fin n → M, φ (tprod A m) = exteriorPower.ιMulti B n m) :
    LinearMap.ker φ =
      Submodule.span A
        ({x | ∃ (m : Fin n → M) (i j : Fin n), i ≠ j ∧ m i = m j ∧ tprod A m = x} ∪
          {x | ∃ (m : Fin n → M) (i j : Fin n) (b : B), i ≠ j ∧
              tprod A (update m i (b • m i)) - tprod A (update m j (b • m j)) = x})
declarations.comment: the stated form, for `n ≥ 3`

declarations.name: FormallyEtaleH1D.quotMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
If `φ : R → S` is formally étale and `R → S/J` is surjective, with `I = ker(R → S/J)`, then
for every `n ≥ 1` the canonical map `φ̄ₙ : R/I^n → S/J^n` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotMap_bijective
    (hφ : RingHom.FormallyEtale φ)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective ((Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp φ))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Function.Bijective (quotMap φ J n)

declarations.name: FormallyEtaleH1D.grMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
If `φ : R → S` is formally étale and `R → S/J` is surjective, with `I = ker(R → S/J)`, then
the induced map of associated graded rings `gr(φ) : ⊕_n I^n/I^{n+1} → ⊕_n J^n/J^{n+1}` is an
isomorphism: for every `n` its degree-`n` component `I^n/I^{n+1} → J^n/J^{n+1}` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem grMap_bijective
    (hφ : RingHom.FormallyEtale φ)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective ((Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp φ))
    (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (grMap φ J n)

declarations.name: Koszul.nonempty_qcIdealPow_qcKoszul_derivedComplete_equivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1E.** Let `R` be a ring and let `f₁, …, f_r` be a weakly proregular sequence
generating the ideal `I`. Then the arguments of the proof of Proposition 0GZK continue to work:
the three categories `QC({R / I ^ n})` (the sheaf of algebras `𝒜 = (R / I ^ n)` on `ℕ` with the
chaotic topology), `QC(ℬ)` (the sheaf `ℬ` of Koszul algebras on `f₁ ^ n, …, f_r ^ n`) and the
category `D_comp(R, I)` of derived complete objects of `D(R)` are equivalent, as `R`-linear
triangulated categories: `QC(𝒜) ≃ QC(ℬ)` and `QC(ℬ) ≃ D_comp(R, I)`, and hence
`QC(𝒜) ≃ D_comp(R, I)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_qcIdealPow_qcKoszul_derivedComplete_equivalences (I : Ideal R) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → R) (proregular : IsWeaklyProregular f)
    (generators : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    Nonempty (LinearTriangulatedEquivalence R
        (Chaotic.QC (liftedIdealPowSheafAlgebra.{u} I)).FullSubcategory
        (Chaotic.QC (liftedPowSheafAlgebra.{u} f)).FullSubcategory) ∧
      Nonempty (LinearTriangulatedEquivalence R
        (Chaotic.QC (liftedPowSheafAlgebra.{u} f)).FullSubcategory
        (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
          (fun K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) => IsDerivedComplete I K))) ∧
      Nonempty (LinearTriangulatedEquivalence R
        (Chaotic.QC (liftedIdealPowSheafAlgebra.{u} I)).FullSubcategory
        (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
          (fun K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) => IsDerivedComplete I K)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isRegular_isProjectiveMorphism_compactification
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a regular curve over `k`. Then there is a nonsingular
projective curve `X̄` over `k` and an open immersion `j : X ⟶ X̄` over `k` whose complement is a
finite set of closed points of `X̄`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isRegular_isProjectiveMorphism_compactification
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k p]
    (hX : IsRegular X) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (j : X ⟶ Y) (hj : IsOpenImmersion j),
      letI : IsOpenImmersion j := hj
      j ≫ q = p ∧ IsCurve k q ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism q ∧ IsRegular Y ∧
        ((Set.range j.base)ᶜ).Finite ∧
        ∀ y : Y, y ∉ Set.range j.base → IsClosed ({y} : Set Y)
declarations.comment: the regular projective compactification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smooth_isProjectiveMorphism_compactification_of_perfectField
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a perfect field and let `X` be a regular curve over `k`. Then `X` is smooth over
`k`, and there is a nonsingular projective curve `X̄` over `k`, smooth over `k`, with an open
immersion `j : X ⟶ X̄` over `k` whose complement is a finite set of closed points of `X̄`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_smooth_isProjectiveMorphism_compactification_of_perfectField
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [PerfectField k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k p] (hX : IsRegular X) :
    Smooth p ∧ ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (j : X ⟶ Y) (hj : IsOpenImmersion j),
      letI : IsOpenImmersion j := hj
      j ≫ q = p ∧ IsCurve k q ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism q ∧ IsRegular Y ∧ Smooth q ∧
        ((Set.range j.base)ᶜ).Finite ∧
        ∀ y : Y, y ∉ Set.range j.base → IsClosed ({y} : Set Y)
declarations.comment: the smooth projective compactification over a perfect field

declarations.name: Stacks.MoreMorphisms.coordinateEmbedding_ker_eq_span
declarations.doc: The scheme-theoretic centre is cut out by exactly the last `n` coordinates.
declarations.statement:
public theorem coordinateEmbedding_ker_eq_span :
    coordinateRingIdeal R m n = RingHom.ker (coordinateProjection R m n)
declarations.comment: ideal of the center

declarations.name: Stacks.MoreMorphisms.coordinateChart_equiv_polynomial
declarations.doc:
The `i`-th standard blowup chart is polynomial affine space, with its original coordinates
given by `x_k`, `y_i`, and `y_j = y_i t_j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem coordinateChart_equiv_polynomial :
    ∃ e : coordinateChartAlgebra R m n i ≃+*
        MvPolynomial (coordinateChartVariables m n i) R,
      (∀ r : R,
        e (algebraMap R (coordinateChartAlgebra R m n i) r) = C r) ∧
      (∀ k : Fin m,
        e (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) R)
          (coordinateChartAlgebra R m n i) (X (Sum.inl k))) = X (Sum.inl k)) ∧
      (e (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) R)
          (coordinateChartAlgebra R m n i) (X (Sum.inr i))) = X (Sum.inr (Sum.inl ()))) ∧
      (∀ j : Fin n, ∀ h : j ≠ i,
        e (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) R)
          (coordinateChartAlgebra R m n i) (X (Sum.inr j))) =
          X (Sum.inr (Sum.inl ())) * X (Sum.inr (Sum.inr ⟨j, h⟩)))
declarations.comment: polynomial affine blowup charts

declarations.name: Stacks.MoreMorphisms.coordinateChart_exceptionalIdeal
declarations.doc:
On the `i`-th affine chart, the exceptional ideal is generated by the single coordinate
`y_i`.
declarations.comment: equation of the exceptional divisor in each chart

declarations.name: Stacks.MoreMorphisms.blowUp_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H1H.** The blowup of affine `(m + n)`-space along the coordinate
affine `m`-subspace is smooth over the base ring.

The hypothesis `0 < n` is the one the source carries and is not used; see
`Stacks.MoreMorphisms.blowUp_smooth_of_pos` for the same statement without it.
declarations.comment: smoothness of the blowup

declarations.name: Stacks.MoreMorphisms.exceptionalDivisor_smooth
declarations.doc:
The exceptional divisor of the blowup of affine `(m + n)`-space along the coordinate affine
`m`-subspace is smooth over the base ring.

The hypothesis `0 < n` is the one the source carries and is not used; see
`Stacks.MoreMorphisms.exceptionalDivisor_smooth_of_pos` for the same theorem without it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalDivisor_smooth (_hn : 0 < n) :
    Smooth ((exceptionalIdeal (coordinateIdeal R m n)).subschemeι ≫
      blowUpToBase (coordinateIdeal R m n) ≫
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (C : R →+* MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) R)))
declarations.comment: smoothness of the exceptional divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.MoreMorphisms.exists_coordinateReesPresentation
declarations.doc:
The Rees algebra of `A = R[x₁,…,x_m,y₁,…,y_n]` with respect to the ideal `(y₁,…,y_n)` is
`A[T₁,…,T_n]/(y_i T_j − y_j T_i)`, with `T_i` going to the degree-one element `y_i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_coordinateReesPresentation :
    ∃ E : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) R) ⧸
        Ideal.span (Set.range fun p : Fin n × Fin n ↦
          C (X (Sum.inr p.1)) * X p.2 - C (X (Sum.inr p.2)) * X p.1))
        ≃ₐ[MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) R] reesAlgebra (coordinateRingIdeal R m n),
      ∀ j : Fin n,
        (E (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (X j)) : Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin n) R)) =
          Polynomial.monomial 1 (X (Sum.inr j))
declarations.comment: the Rees algebra is A[T]/(y_i T_j - y_j T_i)

declarations.name: Stacks.MoreMorphisms.coordinateEmbedding_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc: The coordinate affine subspace is closed in the ambient affine space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem coordinateEmbedding_isClosedImmersion (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (m n : ℕ) :
    IsClosedImmersion (coordinateEmbedding R m n)
declarations.comment: coordinate closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFormallySmoothOnObjects_baseChange
declarations.doc: **Stacks 06D1.** Formal smoothness on objects is stable under base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormallySmoothOnObjects_baseChange
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, max u v, u + 1, max (u + 1) v w}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (q : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hp : Stack.IsFormallySmoothOnObjects B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 p) :
    Stack.IsFormallySmoothOnObjects B S hS
      (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 p q) 𝒵
      (twoFibreProductSnd B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 p q)
declarations.comment: base change of a formally smooth morphism of algebraic stacks is formally smooth

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFormallySmoothOnObjects_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 06D2.** A composite of morphisms formally smooth on objects is formally smooth on
objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormallySmoothOnObjects_comp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hp : Stack.IsFormallySmoothOnObjects B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 p)
    (hq : Stack.IsFormallySmoothOnObjects B S hS 𝒴 𝒵 q) :
    Stack.IsFormallySmoothOnObjects B S hS 𝒳 𝒵 (p ≫ q)
declarations.comment: the case of algebraic stacks, formally smooth being formally smooth on objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFormallySmoothOnObjects_iff_formallySmooth_terminalFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1K.** A 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category
of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces is formally smooth on objects exactly when,
for every scheme-valued point `U` of the target, every algebraic space representing the base
change of it along that point is formally smooth over `U`.

This is Stacks 06D3,
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFormallySmoothOnObjects_iff_isRelativelyFormallySmooth`, with
the structural morphism of the representing space read over `U` rather than over `S`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isRelativelyFormallySmooth_iff_formallySmooth_terminalFrom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormallySmoothOnObjects_iff_formallySmooth_terminalFrom (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hp : Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS p.hom) :
    Stack.IsFormallySmoothOnObjects B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 p ↔
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
          Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
            (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p y
              (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor p))
            (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
          Space.FormallySmooth (terminal.from F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_comp_fromSpecResidueField_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H1M.** A morphism from a reduced scheme whose image is contained in a
single point factors through the spectrum of the residue field of that point.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_comp_fromSpecResidueField_eq {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (x : X)
    [IsReduced Y] (hf : Set.range f.base ⊆ {x}) :
    ∃ g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of (X.residueField x)), g ≫ X.fromSpecResidueField x = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_factorization_through_residueFields
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H1N.** A morphism from a reduced scheme into a locally Noetherian
scheme, whose image lies in a set having no nontrivial specializations among its points, factors
through the coproduct of the corresponding residue-field points.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_through_residueFields
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : Set X)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsReduced Y]
    (hE : ∀ x x' : E, x.1 ⤳ x'.1 → x.1 = x'.1)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, f y ∈ E) :
    ∃ g : Y ⟶ ∐ fun x : E ↦ Spec (.of (X.residueField x.1)),
      g ≫ Sigma.desc (fun x : E ↦ X.fromSpecResidueField x.1) = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_specializes_of_chartPoint_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `a : h_U ⟶ X` be an étale scheme chart of `X`
whose scheme is locally Noetherian. Two points `u`, `u'` of `U` lying above the same point `x` of
`|X|` with `u' ⤳ u` are then equal.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_specializes_of_chartPoint_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
    (ha : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf a)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)]
    (u u' : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hu : ChartPoint B S hS U a u x) (hu' : ChartPoint B S hS U a u' x)
    (hs : u' ⤳ u) : u = u'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isIso_fieldMorphism_iff_hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1R**, the equivalence at a point. Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `x`
be a point of `|X|` and let `f : Z ⟶ X` be a residual space of `X` at `x`. Then `Z` is the
spectrum of a field if and only if `x` can be represented by a monomorphism from the spectrum
of a field.

For the easy implication, the presenting morphism of a field-valued point of `Z` which is an
isomorphism, composed with the monomorphism `f`, is a monomorphism representing `x`, since the
only point of `|Z|` maps to `x`.

Conversely, let `g : yoneda.obj (Spec k over S) ⟶ X` be a monomorphism representing `x`. The
only point of `|Z|` and the point of the field spectrum both map to `x`, so the fibre product
`Z ×_X Spec k` has a point by Stacks 03H4; its projection to the field spectrum is a
monomorphism, hence an isomorphism by Stacks 06MG. That produces a monomorphism
`Spec k ⟶ Z` with nonempty source, and `Z`, being reduced and locally Noetherian with exactly
one point, has a flat, surjective, locally finitely presented cover by the spectrum of a field
by Stacks 06QX, so the monomorphism is an isomorphism by Stacks 06QY.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIso_fieldMorphism_iff_hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (x : points B S hS X) (f : Z ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f) :
    (∃ q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z, IsIso (fieldMorphism B S hS Z q)) ↔
      HasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative B S hS X x
declarations.comment: the equivalence at a point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isIso_fieldMorphism_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1R**, the assertion for a decent algebraic space: every residual space of a
decent algebraic space over `S` is the spectrum of a field.

A decent algebraic space has a monomorphic field-valued representative at every point, which is
condition (4) of Stacks 03JV, so the equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isIso_fieldMorphism_iff_hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative`
applies at every point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIso_fieldMorphism_of_isDecentSpace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (x : points B S hS X) (f : Z ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f) :
    ∃ q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Z, IsIso (fieldMorphism B S hS Z q)
declarations.comment: the assertion for a decent algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_comp_eq_of_isResidualSpaceAt
declarations.doc:
**A morphism from a reduced space with image one point of a locally Noetherian space factors
through every residual space at that point.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` and let `x` be a point of `|X|`. Assume that the image of `|Y| → |X|` is
contained in `{x}`, that `Y` is reduced and that `X` is locally Noetherian. Then `f` factors
uniquely through any residual space `i : Z ⟶ X` of `X` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_comp_eq_of_isResidualSpaceAt
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (x : points B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x i)
    (himage : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Y f) ⊆ {x})
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T))
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    ∃! g : Y ⟶ Z, g ≫ i = f
declarations.comment: the factorization through a given residual space at the point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isResidualSpaceAt_and_existsUnique_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
**A morphism from a reduced space with image one point of a locally Noetherian space factors
through a residual space.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces whose image in `|X|`
is contained in `{x}`, with `Y` reduced and `X` locally Noetherian. Then there is a residual space
of `X` at `x` through which `f` factors, by a unique morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isResidualSpaceAt_and_existsUnique_comp_eq
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (x : points B S hS X)
    (himage : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Y f) ⊆ {x})
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T))
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    ∃ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (i : Z ⟶ X),
      IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x i ∧ ∃! g : Y ⟶ Z, g ≫ i = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isResidualSpaceAt_fieldMorphism_of_mono
declarations.doc:
The morphism presented by a monomorphic field-valued representative of a point `x` of an
algebraic space `X` over `S` exhibits the spectrum of its field as a residual space of `X`
at `x` in the sense of Stacks 06R0.

The spectrum of a field is reduced and locally Noetherian and has exactly one point, and that
point goes to `x` because the representative represents `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isResidualSpaceAt_fieldMorphism_of_mono
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (x : points B S hS X)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X) (hpx : p.class B S hS X = x)
    (hmono : Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS X p)) :
    IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x (fieldMorphism B S hS X p)
declarations.comment: the residual space at the point is the spectrum of the field of hypothesis (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_comp_fieldMorphism_eq_of_range_pointsMap_subset_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1T.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `x` be
a point of `|X|`. Assume that the image of `|Y|` in `|X|` is contained in `{x}`, that `Y` is
reduced, and that `x` is represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism from the spectrum of a
field. Then `f` factors through that monomorphism, which by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isResidualSpaceAt_fieldMorphism_of_mono` is a residual space of `X`
at `x`.

Replace `X` by a quasi-compact open subspace containing `x` and apply Stacks 0BBN: the point
lies in a stratum, a reduced closed subspace of an open subspace which is a scheme. Both `f`
and the representative factor through that open subspace by Stacks 03IE and through the
stratum by Stacks 03JJ, which is where reducedness of `Y` enters. That leaves the case of a
morphism into a representable presheaf monomorphic over `X`, which Stacks 0H1M and Stacks 0H2X
settle on a surjective étale scheme chart of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_comp_fieldMorphism_eq_of_range_pointsMap_subset_singleton
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : Y ⟶ X) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hf : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Y f) ⊆ {x})
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun W : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced W))
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X) (hpx : p.class B S hS X = x)
    (hmono : Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS X p))
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS (fieldMorphism B S hS X p)) :
    ∃ g : Y ⟶ yoneda.obj (p.siteObject B S hS X),
      g ≫ fieldMorphism B S hS X p = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isResidualSpaceAt_comp_fieldMorphism_eq_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1T** with hypothesis (3) supplied by its parenthetical: for a decent algebraic
space `X` over `S`, a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` from a reduced algebraic space whose image on
points is contained in `{x}` factors through a residual space of `X` at `x`, and that residual
space is the spectrum of a field.

Decency of Stacks 03I8 is condition (4) of Stacks 03JV at every point, which is hypothesis (3)
at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isResidualSpaceAt_comp_fieldMorphism_eq_of_isDecentSpace
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : Y ⟶ X) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hf : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Y f) ⊆ {x})
    (hred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun W : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced W))
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X,
      IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x (fieldMorphism B S hS X p) ∧
      ∃ g : Y ⟶ yoneda.obj (p.siteObject B S hS X),
        g ≫ fieldMorphism B S hS X p = f
declarations.comment: hypothesis (3) supplied by decency of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion_of_isResidualSpaceAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H1U.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`
which is locally Noetherian, let `x` be a point of `|X|`, and let `f : Z ⟶ X` be a residual
space of `X` at `x`. Then `x` is a closed point of `|X|` if and only if `f` is a closed
immersion. The hypothesis `huniq` is the uniqueness part of Stacks 06QZ: every residual space
of `X` at `x` is isomorphic to `f` over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion_of_isResidualSpaceAt
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (x : points B S hS X) (f : Z ⟶ X) (hf : IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f)
    (huniq : ∀ (W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (g : W ⟶ X),
      IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x g → ∃ e : W ≅ Z, e.hom ≫ f = g) :
    _root_.IsClosed ({x} : Set (points B S hS X)) ↔ IsClosedImmersion B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_singleton_iff_exists_isResidualSpaceAt_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H1U**, phrased so as not to refer to the uniqueness of the residual
space: a point `x` of the point set of a locally Noetherian algebraic space `X` over `S` is
closed exactly when some residual space of `X` at `x` is a closed subspace of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_singleton_iff_exists_isResidualSpaceAt_isClosedImmersion
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    _root_.IsClosed ({x} : Set (points B S hS X)) ↔
      ∃ (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : Y ⟶ X),
        IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f ∧ IsClosedImmersion B S hS f
declarations.comment: the equivalence through the existence of a residual space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsResidualSpaceAt.isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H1U.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`
which is locally Noetherian, let `x` be a point of `|X|`, and let `f : Z ⟶ X` be a residual
space of `X` at `x`. Then `x` is a closed point of `|X|` if and only if `f` is a closed
immersion.

One implication is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_singleton_of_isClosedImmersion_of_isResidualSpaceAt`. For the
other, the reduced closed subspace of `X` on the closed point `{x}` is a residual space of `X`
at `x` and its inclusion is a closed immersion; the uniqueness half of Stacks 06QZ identifies
`f` with that inclusion up to an isomorphism of its source over `X`, and being a closed
immersion is invariant under such an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsResidualSpaceAt.isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    {x : points B S hS X} {f : Z ⟶ X} (hf : IsResidualSpaceAt B S hS X x f) :
    _root_.IsClosed ({x} : Set (points B S hS X)) ↔ IsClosedImmersion B S hS f
declarations.comment: stated for any residual space of `X` at `x`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.discreteUniqueness_of_uniqueness
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1W, (2) implies (3).** Testing uniqueness of dotted arrows on all valuation
rings is stronger than testing it on the discrete ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem discreteUniqueness_of_uniqueness {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hu : ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness f) : ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteUniqueness f
declarations.comment: (2) implies (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.codimensionZeroUniqueness_of_discreteUniqueness
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1W, (3) implies (4).** Testing uniqueness of dotted arrows on all discrete
valuation rings is stronger than testing it only on the diagrams whose generic arrow picks out
a point of codimension zero.
declarations.comment: (3) implies (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.discreteUniqueness_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1W, (1) implies (3).** A separated morphism of algebraic spaces has at most one
dotted arrow in every valuative diagram with a discrete valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem discreteUniqueness_of_isSeparated (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteUniqueness f
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.codimensionZeroUniqueness_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1W, (1) implies (4).** A separated morphism of algebraic spaces has at most one
dotted arrow in every valuative diagram with a discrete valuation ring whose generic arrow
picks out a point of codimension zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem codimensionZeroUniqueness_of_isSeparated (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.CodimensionZeroUniqueness f
declarations.comment: (1) implies (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_iff_valuativeCriterion_uniqueness
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1W, (1) is equivalent to (2).** A quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces
is separated exactly when it satisfies the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_iff_valuativeCriterion_uniqueness
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f ↔ ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness f
declarations.comment: (1) is equivalent to (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_tfae_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_tfae_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsSeparated B S hS f,
        ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness f,
        ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteUniqueness f,
        ValuativeCriterion.CodimensionZeroUniqueness f ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_tfae_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_codimensionZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1X.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
quasi-separated and of finite type, with `Y` locally Noetherian. The following are equivalent:
1. `f` is proper;
2. `f` satisfies the valuative criterion (Stacks 03IX);
3. every valuative diagram (Stacks 0H1V) for `f` has exactly one dotted arrow;
4. every valuative diagram for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring has
   exactly one dotted arrow;
5. every valuative diagram for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring and whose
   generic arrow `Spec K ⟶ X` picks out a point of codimension zero of `X` has exactly one
   dotted arrow.

Conditions (1) to (3) are equivalent by Stacks 0A40, and (3) implies (4) implies (5) trivially.
Given (5), `f` is separated by Stacks 0H1W
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_codimensionZeroUniqueness`)
and universally closed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_of_codimensionZeroValuativeExistence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_tfae_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_codimensionZero
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsProper B S hS f,
        ValuativeCriterion f,
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, Nonempty q.Lift ∧ Subsingleton q.Lift,
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          Nonempty q.Lift ∧ Subsingleton q.Lift,
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          localRingDimension B S hS q.genericPoint = 0 →
            Nonempty q.Lift ∧ Subsingleton q.Lift ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1Y.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a decent morphism of finite type of algebraic spaces
over `S`, with `Y` locally Noetherian; for instance `f` quasi-separated. The following are
equivalent:

1. `f` is universally closed;
2. `f` satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion;
3. there are an object `V` of the site and a surjective étale morphism `V ⟶ Y` such that for
   every `n` the base change of `f` to affine `n`-space over `V` is closed;
4. every valuative square for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring acquires a
   dotted arrow after a finite separable extension of the fraction field and passage to a
   dominating discrete valuation ring;
5. every valuative square for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring acquires a
   dotted arrow after an extension of the fraction field and passage to a dominating valuation
   ring.

The source omits decency, and without it the statement is false. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_universallyClosed_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian`
(in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.NoetherianUniversallyClosedCounterexample`), whose
statement is this theorem with the hypothesis `IsDecent B S hS f` removed:
```
¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X →
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y → ∀ f : X ⟶ Y, IsFiniteType B S hS f →
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) →
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyClosed B S hS f,
        ValuativeCriterion.Existence f,
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V),
              IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
                IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f),
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension,
            IsDiscreteValuationRing e.square.R ∧
              (letI := e.fieldMap.toAlgebra
               Module.Finite q.K e.square.K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable q.K e.square.K) ∧
              Nonempty e.square.Lift,
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift]
```
The witness is the structure morphism `𝔸¹_ℚ/ℤ ⟶ Spec ℚ` of the quotient of the affine line by
the integer translations: it is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme `Spec ℚ` and
universally closed (Stacks 03IV), but the `ℚ((t))`-point `1/t` extends to no valuation ring
dominating `ℚ[[t]]`, so (1) holds and (2) fails. With decency, (1) implies (2) by Stacks 03M6,
`f` being quasi-compact as it is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (X_alg : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (Y_alg : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (decent : IsDecent B S hS f) (ft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (noeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyClosed B S hS f,
        ValuativeCriterion.Existence f,
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V),
              IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
                IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f),
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension,
            IsDiscreteValuationRing e.square.R ∧
              (letI := e.fieldMap.toAlgebra
               Module.Finite q.K e.square.K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable q.K e.square.K) ∧
              Nonempty e.square.Lift,
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift]
declarations.comment: for f decent (e.g. quasi-separated); without decency the statement is false, see not_forall_universallyClosed_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_implications_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1Y, the implications that hold without decency.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
finite type of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y` locally Noetherian. Number the conditions of
Stacks 0H1Y as follows:

1. `f` is universally closed;
2. `f` satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion;
3. there are an object `V` of the site and a surjective étale morphism `V ⟶ Y` such that for
   every `n` the base change of `f` to affine `n`-space over `V` is closed;
4. every valuative square for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring acquires a
   dotted arrow after a finite separable extension of the fraction field and passage to a
   dominating discrete valuation ring;
5. every valuative square for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring acquires a
   dotted arrow after an extension of the fraction field and passage to a dominating valuation
   ring.

Then (2) ⇒ (4), (4) ⇒ (5), (5) ⇒ (1) and (1) ⇔ (3); in particular (2) ⇒ (1).

**Correction.** The source asserts that the five conditions are equivalent under these
hypotheses alone, which is false: (1) ⇒ (2) fails for the structure morphism `𝔸¹_ℚ/ℤ ⟶ Spec ℚ`,
which is of finite type and universally closed (Stacks 03IV) but does not satisfy the existence
part of the valuative criterion (Stacks section 03K9); see
`not_forall_universallyClosed_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian`. The source's proof derives
(1) ⇔ (2) from Stacks 03KA, which only gives (2) ⇒ (1). Every other implication of the source
holds as stated, and they are the ones asserted here. The equivalence of all five conditions
for `f` decent is `universallyClosed_implications_and_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian`.

The proof follows the source: (1) ⇔ (3) is Stacks 0CM9 (`f` is quasi-compact, being of finite
type), (2) ⇒ (4) is Stacks 03KH with Krull–Akizuki (Stacks 00PG), (4) ⇒ (5) is immediate, and
(5) ⇒ (1) reduces to closedness over a Noetherian affine base by Stacks 0CMC.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_implications_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (X_alg : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (Y_alg : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (ft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (noeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    (ValuativeCriterion.Existence f →
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension,
            IsDiscreteValuationRing e.square.R ∧
              (letI := e.fieldMap.toAlgebra
               Module.Finite q.K e.square.K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable q.K e.square.K) ∧
              Nonempty e.square.Lift) ∧
      ((∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension,
            IsDiscreteValuationRing e.square.R ∧
              (letI := e.fieldMap.toAlgebra
               Module.Finite q.K e.square.K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable q.K e.square.K) ∧
              Nonempty e.square.Lift) →
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift) ∧
      ((∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift) →
        UniversallyClosed B S hS f) ∧
      (UniversallyClosed B S hS f ↔
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V),
              IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
                IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_implications_and_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H1Y, corrected.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of finite type of algebraic spaces
over `S`, with `Y` locally Noetherian, and number the conditions of Stacks 0H1Y as in
`universallyClosed_implications_of_isLocallyNoetherian`:

1. `f` is universally closed;
2. `f` satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion;
3. there are an object `V` of the site and a surjective étale morphism `V ⟶ Y` such that for
   every `n` the base change of `f` to affine `n`-space over `V` is closed;
4. every valuative square for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring acquires a
   dotted arrow after a finite separable extension of the fraction field and passage to a
   dominating discrete valuation ring;
5. every valuative square for `f` whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring acquires a
   dotted arrow after an extension of the fraction field and passage to a dominating valuation
   ring.

Then (2) ⇒ (4) ⇒ (5) ⇒ (1) ⇔ (3), and if `f` is decent (for instance quasi-separated) the five
conditions are equivalent.

**Correction.** The source asserts the equivalence of the five conditions with no hypothesis on
`f` beyond finite type. That is false, by
`not_forall_universallyClosed_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian`: the structure morphism
`𝔸¹_ℚ/ℤ ⟶ Spec ℚ` of the quotient of the affine line by the integer translations is of finite
type over a Noetherian scheme and universally closed (Stacks 03IV), but the `ℚ((t))`-point `1/t`
extends to no valuation ring dominating `ℚ[[t]]`, so (1) holds and (2) fails; that morphism is
not decent. The faulty step is the source's appeal to Stacks 03KA for (1) ⇔ (2): Stacks 03KA
only gives (2) ⇒ (1), and the converse needs decency (Stacks 03M6, `f` being quasi-compact as it
is of finite type) or quasi-separatedness (Stacks 0A3X). So decency is assumed exactly for the
full equivalence, which is `universallyClosed_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian`, and the remaining
implications are stated without it, as in
