`universallyClosed_implications_of_isLocallyNoetherian`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_implications_and_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (X_alg : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (Y_alg : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (ft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (noeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    ((ValuativeCriterion.Existence f →
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension,
            IsDiscreteValuationRing e.square.R ∧
              (letI := e.fieldMap.toAlgebra
               Module.Finite q.K e.square.K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable q.K e.square.K) ∧
              Nonempty e.square.Lift) ∧
      ((∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension,
            IsDiscreteValuationRing e.square.R ∧
              (letI := e.fieldMap.toAlgebra
               Module.Finite q.K e.square.K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable q.K e.square.K) ∧
              Nonempty e.square.Lift) →
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift) ∧
      ((∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
          ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift) →
        UniversallyClosed B S hS f) ∧
      (UniversallyClosed B S hS f ↔
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V),
              IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
                IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f))) ∧
    (IsDecent B S hS f →
      List.TFAE
        [UniversallyClosed B S hS f,
          ValuativeCriterion.Existence f,
          ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
            IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
              ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V),
                IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
                  IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f),
          ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
            ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension,
              IsDiscreteValuationRing e.square.R ∧
                (letI := e.fieldMap.toAlgebra
                 Module.Finite q.K e.square.K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable q.K e.square.K) ∧
                Nonempty e.square.Lift,
          ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
            ∃ e : q.DominatingExtension, Nonempty e.square.Lift])

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEmbedding_pointsMap_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H20, the homeomorphism onto the image.** An immersion of algebraic stacks over `S`
is a topological embedding on the spaces of points of Stacks 04XG and 04XL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmbedding_pointsMap_of_isImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f) :
    @Topology.IsEmbedding _ _ (Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)
      (Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)
      (Stack.pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property 𝒴.val.property f.hom.hom)
declarations.comment: homeomorphism onto the image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyClosed_range_pointsMap_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H20, the locally closed image.** The image on points of an immersion of algebraic
stacks over `S` is a locally closed subset of the space of points of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyClosed_range_pointsMap_of_isImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsImmersion B S hS f) :
    @IsLocallyClosed _ (Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)
      (Set.range (Stack.pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property 𝒴.val.property f.hom.hom))
declarations.comment: locally closed image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosedMap_pointsMap_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H20, closed immersions.** A closed immersion of algebraic stacks over `S` is a
closed map on the spaces of points of Stacks 04XG and 04XL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedMap_pointsMap_of_isClosedImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    @IsClosedMap _ _ (Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) (Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)
      (Stack.pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property 𝒴.val.property f.hom.hom)
declarations.comment: closed immersions are closed on points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isOpenMap_pointsMap_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H20, open immersions.** An open immersion of algebraic stacks over `S` is an open
map on the spaces of points of Stacks 04XG and 04XL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenMap_pointsMap_of_isOpenImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsOpenImmersion B S hS f) :
    @IsOpenMap _ _ (Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) (Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)
      (Stack.pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property 𝒴.val.property f.hom.hom)
declarations.comment: open immersions are open on points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isMonomorphism_and_isResidualGerbeAt_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H21, assertion (1).** Let `X` be an object of the big fppf site of `S`, let `x` be a
point of its underlying scheme and assume the spectrum of the residue field `κ(x)` lies in the
site. Identifying `x` with `Spec (κ(x))`, the 1-morphism `x ⟶ X` of algebraic stacks over `S` is
a monomorphism (**Stacks 04ZW**) and the strictly full subcategory of `(Sch/X)_fppf` it cuts out
is the residual gerbe of `(Sch/X)_fppf` at `x`, in the sense of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` (the specification of **Stacks 06MT**).

The point of `|(Sch/X)_fppf|` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.residueFieldPointClass`, the class of
the tautological field-valued point of `Spec (κ(x))`, which is the point determined by `x` under
the usual identification of the points of `(Sch/X)_fppf` with the points of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMonomorphism_and_isResidualGerbeAt_residueField
    (X : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X)
    (hx : B.Contains (Spec (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X).residueField x))) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsMonomorphism B S hS
        (schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS (residueFieldInclusion B S hS X x hx)) ∧
      IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS X)
        (residueFieldPointClass.{u, w} B S hS X x hx)
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor
          (schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS (residueFieldInclusion B S hS X x hx)).hom).essImage
declarations.comment: the scheme case: the monomorphism x ⟶ X out of the spectrum of the residue field at a point x of a scheme X is the residual gerbe of X at x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_algebraicSpaceStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H21, assertion (2).** Let `F` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `x` be a point
of `|F|`. Then the residual gerbe of `F` at `x` — the *residual space* at `x` — exists: the
algebraic stack of `F` satisfies condition (1) of **Stacks 06MT** at `x`, which by **Stacks 06MU**
is existence of the residual gerbe there.

The algebraic stack of `F` is represented by `F` itself, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace`, whose
witness is the 1-morphism induced by the residual space of **Stacks 06R0**; residual spaces exist
by **Stacks 06QZ**.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_algebraicSpaceStack
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS F hF)) :
    HasSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS (algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS F hF) x
declarations.comment: the algebraic space case: the residual gerbe at a point of an algebraic space, called the residual space, always exists

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isResidualGerbeAt_of_isLocallyNoetherianStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H22.** Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack. Then the residual gerbe of
`𝒳` at `x` exists for every `x ∈ |𝒳|`: some strictly full subcategory of `𝒳` meets the
specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of Stacks 06MT at `x`.

See the module documentation for the argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isResidualGerbeAt_of_isLocallyNoetherianStack (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack B S hS 𝒳) (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    ∃ P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj, IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**The existence clause of Stacks 0H24.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` make `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴` and let
`x` be a point of `𝒳`. If condition (1) of **Stacks 06MT** holds for `𝒴` at the image of `x`,
then it holds for `𝒳` at `x`; that is, the residual gerbe of `𝒳` at `x` exists as soon as the
residual gerbe of `𝒴` at `f(x)` does.

Writing `i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` for the one-point monomorphism over `f(x)`, the witness is the 2-fibre
product `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵` with its projection to `𝒳`, which is a monomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isMonomorphism_fst_twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks`.
Its projection to `𝒵` is again a gerbe (**Stacks 06QE**), hence injective on points, and `𝒵` has
a single point; so the apex has at most one point, and **Stacks 04XH** produces one lying over
`x`. The identification of the residual gerbe with that 2-fibre product is not proved.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSingletonPointMonomorphism_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsGerbeOver B S hS f)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property))
    (hy : HasSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒴
      (pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property)
        (Classical.choose 𝒴.property) f.hom.hom x)) :
    HasSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x
declarations.comment: existence clause: condition (1) of Stacks 06MT transports along a gerbe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isResidualGerbeAt_inverseImage_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H24.** Let `π : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` making `𝒳` a
gerbe over `𝒴`, let `x` be a point of `𝒳` and let `y` be its image in `|𝒴|`. Assume the residual
gerbe `𝒵_y ⊂ 𝒴` of `𝒴` at `y` exists, cut out by the object property `P` of `𝒴` (the
specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` of Stacks 06MT). Then
`𝒵_x = 𝒵_y ×_𝒴 𝒳` is the residual gerbe of `𝒳` at `x`:

* the inverse image `P ∘ π` of `P` meets the residual-gerbe specification of `𝒳` at `x`, so the
  residual gerbe `𝒵_x` of `𝒳` at `x` exists and is the strictly full subcategory of `𝒳` on the
  objects sent into `𝒵_y`; and
* the square formed by the 1-morphism `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒵_y` induced by `π`, the inclusion `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒳`, and
  the inclusion `𝒵_y ⟶ 𝒴`, which commutes on the nose, is a 2-fibre product: `𝒵_x` with its
  inclusion into `𝒳` is the 2-fibre product `𝒵_y ×_𝒴 𝒳`.

Following the source: the inverse image is algebraic and is the 2-fibre product
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_inverseImage`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_inverseImageSquare`); its projection to `𝒵_y` is a
base change of `π`, hence smooth (**Stacks 0DN8**, **Stacks 075W**) and a gerbe
(**Stacks 06QE**), so the apex is reduced and locally Noetherian as `𝒵_y` is (**Stacks 04YF**,
**Stacks 06R6**) and has exactly one point, which lies over `x` (**Stacks 04XH** and injectivity
of a gerbe on points).
declarations.statement:
theorem isResidualGerbeAt_inverseImage_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsGerbeOver B S hS f)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property))
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj)
    (hP : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒴
      (pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property)
        (Classical.choose 𝒴.property) f.hom.hom x) P) :
    ∃ hQ : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x (P.inverseImage f.hom.hom.toFunctor),
      Nonempty (Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct
        ({ pt := residualGerbe B S hS 𝒳 x _ hQ
           fst := residualGerbeMap B S hS f hQ.2.choose hP.2.choose (fun _ h => h)
           snd := residualGerbeInclusion B S hS 𝒳 x _ hQ
           iso := Iso.refl _ } :
          Bicategory.TwoCommSq (residualGerbeInclusion B S hS 𝒴 _ P hP) f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.residualGerbe_factorization_of_isReducedStack
declarations.doc:
**A reduced stack over a point factors through the residual gerbe.** Let `f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` be a
1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let `x ∈ |𝒳|`. Assume that
1. `𝒳` is decent or locally Noetherian (or both),
2. the inertia projection `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is quasi-compact,
3. `|f|(|𝒴|)` is contained in `{x}`, and
4. `𝒴` is reduced.

Then the residual gerbe `𝒵_x` of `𝒳` at `x` exists and `f` factors through it. Precisely:
* the residual gerbe of `𝒳` at `x` exists: some reduced algebraic stack admits a monomorphism to
  `𝒳` whose space of points is a single point lying over `x`;
* `f` factors, up to a 2-isomorphism, through every monomorphism `𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` from an algebraic stack
  with a single point lying over `x`, in particular through every residual gerbe so presented;
* `f` factors strictly through the inclusion of every residual gerbe of `𝒳` at `x`, the strictly
  full subcategory `residualGerbe`.
declarations.statement:
theorem residualGerbe_factorization_of_isReducedStack
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳) (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)
    (h1 : IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val ∨ IsLocallyNoetherianStack B S hS 𝒳)
    (h2 : IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳))
    (h3 : Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f) ⊆ {x})
    (h4 : IsReducedStack B S hS 𝒴) :
    HasReducedSingletonPointMonomorphism B S hS 𝒳 x ∧
      (∀ (𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (m : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳),
        AlgebraicStacks.IsMonomorphism B S hS m → HasUniquePointOver B S hS m x →
          ∃ g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵, Nonempty (g ≫ m ≅ f)) ∧
      ∀ (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hP : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P),
        ∃ g : 𝒴 ⟶ residualGerbe B S hS 𝒳 x P hP,
          g ≫ residualGerbeInclusion B S hS 𝒳 x P hP = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorsThroughSubstack_residualGerbe_of_isClosed_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H26, the closed-point case.** Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack over
`S`, let `x ∈ |𝒳|` be a closed point, and let `f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks with
`𝒴` reduced and `|f|(|𝒴|) ⊆ {x}`. Then the residual gerbe `𝒵_x` of `𝒳` at `x` exists and `f`
factors through it: every object property of `𝒳` cutting out a residual gerbe at `x` is one `f`
factors through.

This is the conclusion of **Stacks 0H25** with its quasi-compact-inertia hypothesis dropped, which
the remark says is true at a closed point because of **Stacks 0H27**. The remark's open question,
whether the conclusion holds at every point of a locally Noetherian `𝒳`, is not asserted.

The residual gerbe is the reduced closed substack on `{x}` (**Stacks 0509**), which is a residual
gerbe at `x` as in the proof of Stacks 0H27; every residual gerbe at `x` has closed immersion
inclusion by Stacks 0H27, so `f` factors through it by **Stacks 050B**.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThroughSubstack_residualGerbe_of_isClosed_singleton
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack B S hS 𝒳)
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)
    (hx : @IsClosed _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) {x})
    (f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳) (hf : Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f) ⊆ {x})
    (hred : IsReducedStack B S hS 𝒴) :
    (∃ P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj, IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P) ∧
      ∀ P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj, IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P →
        FactorsThroughSubstack f P
declarations.comment: the closed-point case the remark asserts: for X locally Noetherian and x a closed point, f : Y -> X with Y reduced and |f|(|Y|) in {x} factors through the residual gerbe at x, which exists (via 0H27). The remark's open question, whether Lemma 0H25 holds for every point of a locally Noetherian X without the quasi-compact inertia hypothesis, is NOT asserted

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isResidualGerbeAt_and_isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H27.** Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack over `S` and `x ∈ |𝒳|`.
The residual gerbe `𝒵_x ⊂ 𝒳` of `𝒳` at `x` exists (**Stacks 0H22**), and for it, `x` is a closed
point of `|𝒳|` if and only if the inclusion `𝒵_x ⟶ 𝒳` is a closed immersion.

The residual gerbe is the strictly full subcategory cut out by an object property meeting the
specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsResidualGerbeAt` (**Stacks 06MU**), which is unique by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isResidualGerbeAt_of_bootstrap`; the equivalence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion_residualGerbeInclusion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isResidualGerbeAt_and_isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒳 : IsLocallyNoetherianStack B S hS 𝒳)
    (x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) :
    ∃ (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hP : IsResidualGerbeAt B S hS 𝒳 x P),
      (@IsClosed _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) {x} ↔
        AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (residualGerbeInclusion B S hS 𝒳 x P hP))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_locallyFinitePresentation_separation_isClosed
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes, `g : T ⟶ S` a morphism, `t ∈ T` a
point and `E ⊆ X ×_S T` a closed subset whose image in `T` misses `t`. Then there are an affine
open neighbourhood `V` of `t`, a commutative square `V ⟶ T' ⟶ S`, `V ⟶ T ⟶ S` with `T'` affine and
`T' ⟶ S` locally of finite presentation, and a closed subset `E' ⊆ X ×_S T'` whose image in `T'`
misses the image of `t`, such that the preimage of `E` in `X ×_S V` lies in the preimage of `E'`.

This is the case of schemes, for closed subsets, of the separation lemma for algebraic stacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_locallyFinitePresentation_separation_isClosed
    {X S T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] (g : T ⟶ S)
    (t : T) (E : Set ↥(pullback f g)) (hE : IsClosed E)
    (ht : t ∉ Set.image (pullback.snd f g) E) :
    ∃ (V : T.affineOpens) (htV : t ∈ V.1)
      (T' : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine T') (b : T' ⟶ S)
      (_ : LocallyOfFinitePresentation b) (a : V.1.toScheme ⟶ T')
      (_ : V.1.ι ≫ g = a ≫ b)
      (E' : Set ↥(pullback f b)) (_ : IsClosed E')
      (p : pullback f (V.1.ι ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g)
      (q : pullback f (V.1.ι ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f b),
      (p ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (V.1.ι ≫ g)) ∧
      (p ≫ pullback.snd f g = pullback.snd f (V.1.ι ≫ g) ≫ V.1.ι) ∧
      (q ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst f (V.1.ι ≫ g)) ∧
      (q ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd f (V.1.ι ≫ g) ≫ a) ∧
      (a ⟨t, htV⟩ ∉ Set.image (pullback.snd f b) E') ∧
      (p ⁻¹' E ⊆ q ⁻¹' E')
declarations.comment: the case of schemes, for closed subsets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_affine_finitePresentation_separation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H29.** Let `g : Z ⟶ Y` be a morphism of the big fppf category of `S` between
objects with affine underlying schemes, let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over `S` with `𝒳` quasi-compact, let `z` be a point of `Z` and let
`T ⊆ |𝒳 ×_Y Z|` be a closed subset whose image in `|Z|` misses `z`. Then there are an open
neighbourhood `V` of `z` in `Z`, a commutative square `V ⟶ Z' ⟶ Y`, `V ⟶ Z ⟶ Y`, and a closed
subset `T' ⊆ |𝒳 ×_Y Z'|` such that

1. `Z'` is affine and of finite presentation over `Y`,
2. the image of `z` in `|Z'|` misses the image of `T'` in `|Z'|`, and
3. the inverse image of `T` in `|𝒳 ×_Y V|` maps into `T'`.

The two comparison 1-morphisms of the last two clauses are the canonical ones
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorMap`; their compatibilities with the projections of the three base
changes are `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorIsoFst` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorIsoSnd`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_finitePresentation_separation {Y Z : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (hY : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y))
    (hZ : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z)) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Y)
    (_hf : IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f)
    (h𝒳 : IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property)
    (z : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z))
    (T : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (baseChangeSquare B S hS f g).pt))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (pointTopology B S hS (baseChangeSquare B S hS f g).pt.val) T)
    (hz : z ∉ AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (baseChangeSquare B S hS f g).fst '' T) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (j : V ⟶ Z),
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map j) ∧
      ∃ v : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V),
        AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS j) v = z ∧
        ∃ (Z' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (b : Z' ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z') ∧
          FinitePresentation ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map b) ∧
          ∃ (a : V ⟶ Z') (hab : j ≫ g = a ≫ b)
            (T' : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS (baseChangeSquare B S hS f b).pt)),
            @IsClosed _ (pointTopology B S hS (baseChangeSquare B S hS f b).pt.val) T' ∧
            AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS a) v ∉
              AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (baseChangeSquare B S hS f b).fst '' T' ∧
            AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (factorMap B S hS f (j ≫ g) a b hab) ''
                (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
                  (factorMap B S hS f (j ≫ g) j g rfl) ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.image_preimage_eq_preimage_image_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
For a 2-fibre product square of algebraic stacks over `S` with legs `fst : 𝒫 ⟶ 𝒳` and
`snd : 𝒫 ⟶ 𝒬` over a cospan `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, `f : 𝒬 ⟶ 𝒴`, and for any subset `T` of `|𝒳|`, the
image in `|𝒬|` of the preimage of `T` in `|𝒫|` is the preimage in `|𝒬|` of the image of `T`
in `|𝒴|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_preimage_eq_preimage_image_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    {𝒳 𝒬 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} {f : 𝒬 ⟶ 𝒴}
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (T : Set (points B S hS 𝒳)) :
    pointsMap B S hS P.snd '' (pointsMap B S hS P.fst ⁻¹' T) =
      pointsMap B S hS f ⁻¹' (pointsMap B S hS g '' T)
declarations.comment: the cartesian-square step of the proof, on points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.image_closure_image_subset_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
Let `P` be a 2-fibre product square of algebraic stacks over `S` with legs `fst : 𝒫 ⟶ 𝒳` and
`snd : 𝒫 ⟶ 𝒬` over a cospan `g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, `f : 𝒬 ⟶ 𝒴`, with `f` surjective and open on points,
and let `π : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be a 1-morphism. If a closed subset `T' ⊆ |𝒬|` contains the image of the
preimage of `T ⊆ |𝒳|`, then the image in `|𝒵|` of the closure of the image of `T` in `|𝒴|` is
contained in the image of `T'` in `|𝒵|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_closure_image_subset_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    {𝒳 𝒬 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} {f : 𝒬 ⟶ 𝒴} (π : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS f))
    (hopen : letI := Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒬.val
      letI := Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val
      IsOpenMap (pointsMap B S hS f))
    (T : Set (points B S hS 𝒳)) (T' : Set (points B S hS 𝒬))
    (hT' : letI := Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒬.val
      IsClosed T')
    (hsub : pointsMap B S hS P.snd '' (pointsMap B S hS P.fst ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T') :
    letI := Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val
    pointsMap B S hS π '' closure (pointsMap B S hS g '' T) ⊆
      pointsMap B S hS (f ≫ π) '' T'
declarations.comment: the descent step of the proof, along a cartesian square with surjective open legs

declarations.name: IsOpenMap.image_closure_subset_image_of_preimage_subset
declarations.doc:
For a surjective open continuous map `q : X → Y`, a closed subset `T ⊆ X` containing
`q ⁻¹' A` also contains `q ⁻¹' closure A`; hence the image of `closure A` along any map
`π : Y → Z` is contained in the image of `T` along `π ∘ q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsOpenMap.image_closure_subset_image_of_preimage_subset
    {X Y Z : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {q : X → Y}
    (hopen : IsOpenMap q) (hcont : Continuous q) (hsurj : Function.Surjective q) (π : Y → Z)
    {A : Set Y} {T : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (h : q ⁻¹' A ⊆ T) :
    π '' closure A ⊆ (π ∘ q) '' T
declarations.comment: the closure step of the proof, along a surjective open map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_baseChange_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A: closedness of a base change descends along an immersion of the base.** Let
`F : 𝒬 ⟶ ℬ` be closed on points and let `ι : 𝒞 ⟶ ℬ` be an immersion of algebraic stacks over `S`.
Then the base change of `F` along `ι` — the map `|𝒬 ×_ℬ 𝒞| → |𝒞|` — is closed on points.

This is the step of the proof of Stacks 0H2A which writes a closed subset of `|𝒳 ×_𝒴 Z|` as the
pullback of a closed subset of `|𝐀ⁿ × 𝒳|` along the immersion `Z ⟶ 𝐀ⁿ_V` of Stacks 04II. The base
change of `ι` is an immersion by Stacks 045C at the immersion property, hence a topological
embedding on points by **Stacks 0H20**; the square is cartesian on points by **Stacks 04XH**; and
`isClosedMap_of_isEmbedding_of_cartesian` concludes. Only the embedding property of Stacks 0H20
is used, not the local closedness of the range.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_baseChange_of_isImmersion
    {𝒬 𝒞 ℬ : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (F : 𝒬 ⟶ ℬ) (ι : 𝒞 ⟶ ℬ)
    (hι : IsImmersion B S hS ι) (hF : IsClosed B S hS F) :
    IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS ι F).fst
declarations.comment: closedness of a base change descends along an immersion of the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, (1) implies (2).** If `f` is universally closed then, for every object `Z` of
the site whose scheme is *affine* and every 1-morphism `Stack.schemeStack Z ⟶ 𝒴` which is
*locally of finite presentation*, the map `|𝒳 ×_𝒴 Z| → |Z|` is closed. Neither adjective is
used: the clause is the restriction of universal closedness to those bases.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_universallyClosed
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : UniversallyClosed B S hS f) :
    ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
      ∀ (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ 𝒴),
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g →
          IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_chart_forall_isClosed_baseChange_affineSpaceChart_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, (1) implies (3).** If `f` is universally closed then there are a scheme `V` of
the site and a smooth surjective 1-morphism `Stack.schemeStack V ⟶ 𝒴` such that, for *every*
`n ≥ 0`, the base change of `f` to affine `n`-space over `V` — the map
`|𝐀^n × (𝒳 ×_𝒴 V)| → |𝐀^n × V|` — is closed.

Any smooth surjective chart of `𝒴` by a scheme of the site serves, and every one of the base
changes is closed because `f` is universally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chart_forall_isClosed_baseChange_affineSpaceChart_of_universallyClosed
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : UniversallyClosed B S hS f) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V ⟶ 𝒴),
      Stack.IsSurjective B S hS a ∧ IsSmooth B S hS a ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS
          (Stack.schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS (affineSpaceChartHom B S hS V n) ≫ a) f).fst
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_chart_forall_isClosed_baseChange_affineSpaceChart_of_isClosed_affine_lfp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, (2) implies (3).** Suppose every base change of `f` to an affine scheme of the
site along a 1-morphism locally of finite presentation is closed. Then the conclusion of (3)
holds for *any* smooth surjective chart `a : Stack.schemeStack V ⟶ 𝒴` of `𝒴` by a scheme of the
site.

Fix `n`. The target of the base change is the stack of affine `n`-space over `V`; its affine
opens cover it and their inclusions are open immersions, hence smooth, so closedness can be read
on that cover. Over one affine open `W` the base change of `f` is the base change along the
composite `W ⟶ 𝐀^n_V ⟶ V ⟶ 𝒴`, whose scheme `W` is affine and which is locally of finite
presentation — the inclusion of an open is, the projection of affine `n`-space is, and `a` is
smooth hence locally of finite presentation by Stacks 0DNP. So (2) applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chart_forall_isClosed_baseChange_affineSpaceChart_of_isClosed_affine_lfp
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h : ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
      ∀ (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ 𝒴),
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g →
          IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V ⟶ 𝒴),
      Stack.IsSurjective B S hS a ∧ IsSmooth B S hS a ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS
          (Stack.schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS (affineSpaceChartHom B S hS V n) ≫ a) f).fst
declarations.comment: (2) implies (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_baseChange_schemeStackMap_of_forall_isClosed_baseChange_affineSpaceChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, the step of (3) implies (2) at a target represented by a scheme.** Let
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ Stack.schemeStack W` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` whose base change to
affine `n`-space over `W` is closed on points for every `n ≥ 0`. Then for every morphism
`p : Z ⟶ W` of the site whose source scheme is quasi-affine and which is locally of finite type,
the base change of `f` along the 1-morphism that `p` induces is closed on points.

By **Stacks 04II** such a `Z` immerses over `W` into affine `n`-space over `W` for some `n`. That
immersion of schemes induces an immersion of the represented algebraic stacks, and closedness of
a base change descends along an immersion of the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_baseChange_schemeStackMap_of_forall_isClosed_baseChange_affineSpaceChart
    {𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {W : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS W)
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS
      (Stack.schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS (affineSpaceChartHom B S hS W n)) f).fst)
    {Z : BigFppfOver B S hS} (p : Z ⟶ W)
    (hZ : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z).IsQuasiAffine)
    (hp : LocallyOfFiniteType ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p)) :
    IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS
      (Stack.schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS p) f).fst
declarations.comment:
(3) implies (2), the step at a target represented by a scheme, stated at the
hypotheses of Tag 04II: a quasi-affine source and a morphism locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of Stacks 0H2A is inherited by a base change along a 1-morphism locally of
finite presentation.** Suppose every base change of `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` to an affine scheme of the site
along a 1-morphism locally of finite presentation is closed on points, and let `b : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` be
locally of finite presentation. Then the same holds for the base change of `f` along `b`: a
1-morphism `Stack.schemeStack Z ⟶ 𝒴'` locally of finite presentation composes with `b` to one
locally of finite presentation, and base changing twice is base changing once.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_baseChange
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (b : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hb : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS b)
    (h : ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
      ∀ (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ 𝒴), IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g →
        IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst)
    (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (hZ : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z))
    (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ 𝒴') (hg : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g) :
    IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g
      (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS b f).fst).fst
declarations.comment:
clause (2) is inherited by a base change along a 1-morphism locally of finite
presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_forall_schemeStack_target_of_isClosed_affine_lfp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, the reduction of (2) implies (1) to a target represented by a scheme.** If
clause (2) implies universal closedness whenever the target is the algebraic stack of a scheme of
the site, then it implies universal closedness for an arbitrary target.

Every algebraic stack over `S` has a smooth surjective chart by a scheme of the site, universal
closedness descends along it, and it is locally of finite presentation by Stacks 0DNP, so clause
(2) for `f` gives clause (2) for the base change of `f` to that chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_of_forall_schemeStack_target_of_isClosed_affine_lfp
    (hred : ∀ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (𝒲 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
      (f' : 𝒲 ⟶ Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V),
        (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
          ∀ (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V),
            IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g →
              IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f').fst) →
        UniversallyClosed B S hS f')
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h : ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
      ∀ (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ 𝒴), IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g →
        IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f
declarations.comment:
(2) implies (1), the reduction to a target represented by a scheme; the
remaining input is Tag 0H29 for algebraic stacks, carried as `hred`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_isClosed_affine_lfp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, (2) implies (1), with the reduction to a target represented by a scheme.** Let
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` such that the base change
of `f` to every affine scheme of the site along a 1-morphism locally of finite presentation is
closed on points. Then `f` is universally closed.

Pick a smooth surjective chart `a : Stack.schemeStack V ⟶ 𝒴` of `𝒴` by a scheme of the site.
Universal closedness descends along `a`, so it is enough to prove it for the base change of `f`
along `a`, whose target is represented by a scheme of the site; that base change is quasi-compact
by **Stacks 050V**, and it inherits the hypothesis because `a` is locally of finite presentation
by Stacks 0DNP and clause (2) is inherited by a base change along a 1-morphism locally of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_isClosed_affine_lfp
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f)
    (h : ∀ Z : BigFppfOver B S hS, IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
      ∀ g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ 𝒴, IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g →
        IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1), with the reduction to a target represented by a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_exists_chart_forall_isClosed_baseChange_affineSpaceChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, (3) implies (1).** Suppose there are a scheme `V` of the site and a smooth
surjective 1-morphism `a : Stack.schemeStack V ⟶ 𝒴` such that the base change of the quasi-compact
`f` to affine `n`-space over `V` is closed on points for every `n ≥ 0`. Then `f` is universally
closed.

Universal closedness descends along `a`, so it is enough to prove it for the base change `f'` of
`f` along `a`, whose target is represented by a scheme of the site. By (2) implies (1) at such a
target it is enough to show that the base change of `f'` to every affine scheme of the site along
a morphism of the site locally of finite presentation is closed on points; an affine scheme is
quasi-affine and a morphism locally of finite presentation is locally of finite type, so this is
the step of (3) implies (2) at a target represented by a scheme, which goes through the immersion
into affine `n`-space of **Stacks 04II**.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_of_exists_chart_forall_isClosed_baseChange_affineSpaceChart
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f)
    (h : ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V ⟶ 𝒴),
      Stack.IsSurjective B S hS a ∧ IsSmooth B S hS a ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS
          (Stack.schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS (affineSpaceChartHom B S hS V n) ≫ a) f).fst) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f
declarations.comment: (3) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_tfae_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`.
The following are equivalent:

1. `f` is universally closed;
2. for every object `Z` of the site whose underlying scheme is affine and every 1-morphism
   `Stack.schemeStack Z ⟶ 𝒴` locally of finite presentation, the map `|𝒳 ×_𝒴 Z| → |Z|` is closed;
3. there are an object `V` of the site and a smooth surjective 1-morphism
   `a : Stack.schemeStack V ⟶ 𝒴` such that `|𝐀^n × (𝒳 ×_𝒴 V)| → |𝐀^n × V|` is closed for every
   `n ≥ 0`.

Clause (3) is read as closedness of the base change of `f` along the composite
`𝐀^n_V ⟶ V ⟶ 𝒴`, which is what `|𝐀^n × (𝒳 ×_𝒴 V)| → |𝐀^n × V|` is over `V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_tfae_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyClosed B S hS f,
        ∀ Z : BigFppfOver B S hS, IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
          ∀ g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ 𝒴, IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g →
            IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst,
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS V ⟶ 𝒴),
          Stack.IsSurjective B S hS a ∧ IsSmooth B S hS a ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosed B S hS
              (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS
                (Stack.schemeStackMap.{u, w} B S hS (affineSpaceChartHom B S hS V n) ≫ a)
                f).fst]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_discreteValuationRing_of_mem_closure_range_pointsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2B.** A point in the closure of the image of a finite-type 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks whose target is locally Noetherian is reached by the closed point of a valuative square
whose valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_discreteValuationRing_of_mem_closure_range_pointsMap
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (h𝒴 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴)
    (y : points B S hS 𝒴.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒴.property))
    (hy : y ∈ @closure _
      (pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)
      (Set.range
        (pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property)
          (Classical.choose 𝒴.property) f.hom.hom))) :
    ∃ (q : ValuativeSquare B S hS f) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R)
      (hz : B.Contains
        (Spec (.of ((Spec (.of q.R)).residueField (IsLocalRing.closedPoint q.R))))),
      pointClass B S hS 𝒴.val.val
        (Classical.choose 𝒴.property)
        (fieldValuedPointMap B S hS
          (schemeFibredCategory B S hS
            (siteObject B S hS q.ring_mem q.base)).val
          q.y.hom
          (closedPointFieldValuedPoint B S hS
            (siteObject B S hS q.ring_mem q.base)
            (IsLocalRing.closedPoint q.R) hz)) = y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteExistence
declarations.doc:
**The hypothesis of Stacks 0H2C.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` satisfies the
*discrete* existence part of the valuative criterion when every valuative square for it whose
valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring admits a dotted arrow after an extension of the
fraction field and passage to a dominating valuation ring.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ValuativeCriterion.Existence` of **Stacks 0CLK** with the extra
clause `IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R`; the dominating valuation ring is not asked to be
discrete.
declarations.statement: abbrev DiscreteExistence (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop
declarations.comment:
the hypothesis of the lemma: the existence part of the valuative criterion,
restricted to discrete valuation rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.discreteExistence_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**The hypothesis of Stacks 0H2C is stable under base change.** A base change of a
1-morphism of algebraic stacks satisfying the discrete existence part of the valuative criterion
satisfies it as well.

The valuative square for `f` obtained by pasting the given square with the base-change square
has the same valuation ring, so discreteness transports, and the dotted arrow comes back along
the equivalence of **Stacks 0CLE**.
declarations.statement:
theorem discreteExistence_baseChange
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteExistence B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteExistence B S hS P.fst
declarations.comment: step 1 of the proof: the hypothesis is stable under base change, via Tag 0CLE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_of_discreteExistence
declarations.doc:
**Closedness on points from the hypothesis of Stacks 0H2C.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
finite-type 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` with `𝒴` locally Noetherian which satisfies
the discrete existence part of the valuative criterion. Then `f` is closed on points.

A closed subset of `|𝒳|` is the set of points of a closed substack `i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` by the existence
half of **Stacks 0509**, so its image is
the image of `|𝒵| → |𝒴|`. A point in the closure of that image is reached by a discrete
valuative square for `i ≫ f` (**Stacks 0H2B**); read as a square for `f` it yields a lift to `𝒳`
over a dominating valuation ring, and the full existence criterion, available for the closed
immersion `i` by **Stacks 0CLP**, lifts that further to `𝒵`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_of_discreteExistence (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (h𝒴 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴)
    (hlift : ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteExistence B S hS f) :
    IsClosed B S hS f
declarations.comment: steps 3 and 4 of the proof: closedness on points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_discreteExistence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, item (2), from the hypothesis of Stacks 0H2C.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
finite-type 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` with `𝒴` locally Noetherian which satisfies
the discrete existence part of the valuative criterion. Then for every object `Z` of the site
whose scheme is affine and every 1-morphism `Stack.schemeStack Z ⟶ 𝒴` locally of finite
presentation, the map `|𝒳 ×_𝒴 Z| → |Z|` is closed.

The base change is again of finite type (**Stacks 06Q7**), its target is again locally
Noetherian (**Stacks 06R6**), and it again satisfies the hypothesis by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.discreteExistence_baseChange`. Affineness of `Z` is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_discreteExistence
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (h𝒴 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴)
    (hlift : ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteExistence B S hS f) :
    ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
      ∀ (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Z ⟶ 𝒴),
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g →
          IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst
declarations.comment: clause (2) of Tag 0H2A for `f`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_discreteExistence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2C.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` with `𝒴`
locally Noetherian and `f` of finite type. If every valuative square for `f` whose valuation ring
is a discrete valuation ring admits a dotted arrow after an extension of the fraction field and
passage to a dominating valuation ring, then `f` is universally closed.

Clause (2) of **Stacks 0H2A** holds for `f` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks`
`.isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_discreteExistence`, and `f` is of
finite type, hence quasi-compact, so (2) implies (1) of **Stacks 0H2A**.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_of_discreteExistence
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (h𝒴 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴)
    (hlift : ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteExistence B S hS f) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f
declarations.comment: the lemma

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_of_discreteExistence'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2C, steps 3 and 4: closedness on points, with nothing assumed.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`
be a finite-type 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` with `𝒴` locally Noetherian which
satisfies the discrete existence part of the valuative criterion. Then `f` is closed on points.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_of_discreteExistence`.
declarations.statement: alias isClosed_of_discreteExistence'
declarations.comment: steps 3 and 4 of the proof: closedness on points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_discreteExistence'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2A, item (2), from the hypothesis of Stacks 0H2C, with nothing assumed.** For
every object `Z` of the site whose scheme is affine and every 1-morphism
`Stack.schemeStack Z ⟶ 𝒴` locally of finite presentation, the map `|𝒳 ×_𝒴 Z| → |Z|` is closed.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks`
`.isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_discreteExistence`.
declarations.statement: alias isClosed_baseChange_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_discreteExistence'
declarations.comment: clause (2) of Tag 0H2A for `f`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_discreteExistence'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2C.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` with `𝒴`
locally Noetherian and `f` of finite type. If every valuative square for `f` whose valuation ring
is a discrete valuation ring admits a dotted arrow after an extension of the fraction field and
passage to a dominating valuation ring, then `f` is universally closed.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_discreteExistence`.
declarations.statement: alias universallyClosed_of_discreteExistence'
declarations.comment: the lemma

declarations.name: Stacks.KaehlerDifferential.Presentation.presentation_square_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0H2F.** Given a commutative square of commutative rings
`φ ∘ α = β ∘ ψ` (here phrased as `φ.comp α = β.comp ψ`), the square of presentations
of Kähler differentials commutes:
`Φ_F ∘ ∂_{S/R} = ∂_{S'/R'} ∘ Φ_P`
as `φ`-semilinear maps `P_{S/R} → F_{S'/R'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presentation_square_comm
    {R S R' S' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S']
    (α : R →+* S) (β : R' →+* S') (φ : S →+* S') (ψ : R →+* R')
    (hcomm : φ.comp α = β.comp ψ) :
    (PhiF φ).comp (presentationMap α)
      = (presentationMap β).comp (PhiP φ ψ)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.annihilatorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2H.** The annihilator of an `𝒪_X`-module `F` is the
subsheaf of `𝒪_X` consisting of the local functions that act as zero on `F`.  Equivalently,
it is the kernel of the canonical map from `𝒪_X` to the internal endomorphism sheaf of
`F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def annihilatorSheaf :
    (SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X)).Submodule

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.stalk_annihilatorSheaf_le_annihilator_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2I.** The germs of local sections of the annihilator
sheaf at `x` annihilate the stalk `Fₓ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalk_annihilatorSheaf_le_annihilator_stalk (x : X) :
    { a : (show X.carrier.Presheaf RingCat from (structureSheafRing X).obj).stalk x |
      ∃ (U : Opens X.carrier) (hx : x ∈ U) (r : (structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op U)),
        r ∈ (annihilatorSheaf X F).toSubmodule.obj (op U) ∧
          (show X.carrier.Presheaf RingCat from (structureSheafRing X).obj).germ U x hx r = a } ⊆
      Module.annihilator
        ((show X.carrier.Presheaf RingCat from (structureSheafRing X).obj).stalk x)
        ((show X.carrier.Presheaf Ab.{u} from F.val.presheaf).stalk x)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.annihilatorSheaf_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2J.** For `F` of finite type, the germs at `x` of the local sections
of the annihilator sheaf of `F` are exactly the elements of the local ring `O_{X,x}` that
annihilate the stalk `F_x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem annihilatorSheaf_stalk [F.IsFiniteType] (x : X) :
    {r : TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) X.sheaf.obj x |
      ∃ (U : Opens X) (hx : x ∈ U) (s : (structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op U)),
        s ∈ (annihilatorSheaf X F).toSubmodule.obj (op U) ∧
          TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := CommRingCat.{u}) X.sheaf.obj U x hx s = r} =
      (Module.annihilator
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) X.sheaf.obj x)
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u})
          (show PresheafOfModules.{u}
              (X.sheaf.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) from F.val).presheaf x) :
          Set (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) X.sheaf.obj x))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quotientRingSheafModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2K.** The canonical `𝒪_X/I`-module structure on a sheaf of modules
annihilated by the ideal subsheaf `I`: its underlying presheaf of abelian groups is that of `F`,
and a local section of `𝒪_X/I` acts through any local lift of it to `𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientRingSheafModule (hI : I ≤ annihilatorSheaf X F) :
    SheafOfModules.{v} (quotientRingSheaf X I).sheaf
declarations.comment: the descended module structure

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quotientRingSheafModule_restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2K.** The descended action is compatible with the given one:
restricting scalars along the quotient map returns `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientRingSheafModule_restrictScalars (hI : I ≤ annihilatorSheaf X F) :
    (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars (quotientRingSheaf X I).quotientMap).obj
      (quotientRingSheafModule X I F hI) = F
declarations.comment: compatibility with the given action

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quotientRingSheafModule_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2K.** The descended action is the only `𝒪_X/I`-action whose
restriction of scalars along the quotient map is the given `𝒪_X`-action.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientRingSheafModule_unique (hI : I ≤ annihilatorSheaf X F)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{v} (quotientRingSheaf X I).sheaf)
    (hG : (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars (quotientRingSheaf X I).quotientMap).obj G = F) :
    G = quotientRingSheafModule X I F hI
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the descended action

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.quotientRingSheafModule_stalk_smul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2K.** On stalks the descended action is the ordinary action of the
quotient ring `𝒪_{X,x}/I_x` on the stalk `F_x`, which the stalk of `I` annihilates: the class of a
germ `r` acts on `F_x` exactly as `r` itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientRingSheafModule_stalk_smul (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hI : I ≤ annihilatorSheaf X F) (x : X.carrier)
    (r : TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := RingCat) (structureSheafRing X).obj x)
    (m : TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x) :
    quotientStalkSMul X I F hI x
        (quotientRingSheafStalkIdealEquiv X I x
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (idealSheafStalk X I x) r)) m = r • m
declarations.comment: the action on stalks

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_annihilatorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2L.** If the structure sheaf of a ringed space and an `𝒪_X`-module
`F` are coherent, then the annihilator of `F` is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_annihilatorSheaf (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    [IsCoherent (SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X))] [IsCoherent F] :
    IsCoherent (annihilatorSheaf X F).toSheafOfModules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_iff_lifts_injective_specMap
declarations.doc:
An affine morphism is a closed immersion exactly when maps out of spectra lift
against every injective map of commutative rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_lifts_injective_specMap
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsClosedImmersion f ↔
      ∀ (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (ψ : A →+* B),
        Function.Injective ψ →
        ∀ (g : Spec (.of B) ⟶ X) (h : Spec (.of A) ⟶ Y),
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ψ) ≫ h = g ≫ f) →
          ∃ l : Spec (.of A) ⟶ X,
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ψ) ≫ l = g) ∧ (l ≫ f = h)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.toSpecΓ_app_injective
declarations.doc:
If `X` is quasi-compact then `f^♯ : 𝒪_S ⟶ f_* 𝒪_X` is injective, for
`f : X ⟶ S = Spec Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` the canonical morphism: it is injective on the sections over every
open of `S`.

theorem toSpecΓ_app_injective [CompactSpace X] (U : (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)).Opens) :
