declarations.statement: theorem isDominant_toSpecΓ [CompactSpace X] : IsDominant X.toSpecΓ
declarations.comment: if `X` is quasi-compact then `f` is dominant

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_iff_lifts_injective_specMap_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact scheme morphism is a closed immersion exactly when maps out of
spectra lift against every injective homomorphism of commutative rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_lifts_injective_specMap_of_quasiCompact
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] :
    IsClosedImmersion f ↔
      ∀ (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (ψ : A →+* B),
      Function.Injective ψ →
      ∀ (g : Spec (.of B) ⟶ X) (h : Spec (.of A) ⟶ Y),
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ψ) ≫ h = g ≫ f) →
        ∃ l : Spec (.of A) ⟶ X,
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ψ) ≫ l = g) ∧ (l ≫ f = h)

declarations.name: isReduced_and_isReduced_fiber_of_isProper_over_valuationRing
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be a proper flat morphism where `R` is a valuation ring. If the special
fibre is reduced, then `X` and every fibre of `X ⟶ Spec R` are reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReduced_and_isReduced_fiber_of_isProper_over_valuationRing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [ValuationRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsProper f] [Flat f]
    (hspecial : IsReduced (f.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R))) :
    IsReduced X ∧ ∀ s : Spec (.of R), IsReduced (f.fiber s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAbelianVariety_iff_of_choices
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2U.** Let `k` be a field and `A` a group scheme over `k`. Pick one
property from each of the three sets

* projective, proper;
* geometrically irreducible, irreducible, geometrically connected, connected;
* smooth, geometrically reduced.

Then `A` is an abelian variety if and only if it has the three chosen properties over `k`; so the
sixteen choices are sixteen equivalent definitions of an abelian variety. The choice "proper,
geometrically irreducible, geometrically reduced" recovers Definition 03RO.

Every choice implies the weakest one, "proper, connected, geometrically reduced", which makes `A`
an abelian variety (`AlgebraicGeometry.isAbelianVariety_of_choices`); conversely an abelian
variety is projective by Tag 0BFA, smooth by Tag 0BFC and geometrically irreducible, which is the
strongest choice and implies every other.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbelianVariety_iff_of_choices
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (A : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj A] :
    ∀ P₁ ∈ [IsProjective A.hom, IsProper A.hom],
    ∀ P₂ ∈ [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom, IrreducibleSpace A.left,
      GeometricallyConnected A.hom, ConnectedSpace A.left],
    ∀ P₃ ∈ [Smooth A.hom, GeometricallyReduced A.hom],
      (IsAbelianVariety k A ↔ P₁ ∧ P₂ ∧ P₃)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CohenMacaulayCurveSituation.isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_two_mul_genus_add_one_le
declarations.doc:
**Invertible modules of degree at least `2g + 1` are very ample.** In Situation
[Stacks, Tag 0B5D] — a proper one-dimensional scheme `X` over a field `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` —
assume `X` geometrically integral over `k` of genus `g`, and let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module. If `deg(ℒ) ≥ 2g + 1`, then `ℒ` is very ample.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_of_two_mul_genus_add_one_le
    [AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIntegral S.f] (L : S.X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf S.X.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (hL : 2 * (genus S.f : ℤ) + 1 ≤
      invertibleCurveDegree S.k S.f (le_of_eq S.dimension_one) L) :
    Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple S.f L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtale_of_isUnramifiedInCodimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2W.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `U ⊆ X` a dense open
and `f : Y ⟶ U` finite étale. If `Y` is unramified over `X` in codimension one and `𝒪_{X, x}` is
regular for every `x` outside `U`, then `f` is the restriction of a finite étale cover of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteEtale_of_isUnramifiedInCodimensionOne
    (hExtend : ExtendsAcrossCodimensionOneBoundary.{u})
    (hPurity : PurityAtRegularLocalRings.{u})
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (U : X.Opens) (hdense : DenseRange U.ι.base)
    (hEssSurj : ∀ V : X.Opens, (∀ x : X, x ∉ V → HasPurity (X.presheaf.stalk x)) →
      (finiteEtaleBaseChange V.ι).EssSurj)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ U) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    (hunr : Stacks.FundamentalGroup.IsUnramifiedInCodimensionOne U.ι f)
    (hreg : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ (Y' : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y' ⟶ X), IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧
      ∃ e : pullback p U.ι ≅ Y, e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd p U.ι
declarations.comment: extension across a regular complement, with the two inputs carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtale_extension_of_isUnramifiedInCodimensionOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H2W.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `U ⊆ X` a dense open
and `f : Y ⟶ U` finite étale. If `Y` is unramified over `X` in codimension one and `𝒪_{X, x}` is
regular for every `x` outside `U`, then `f` is the restriction of a finite étale cover of `X`:
there is a finite étale `p : Y' ⟶ X` and an isomorphism `Y' ×_X U ≅ Y` over `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteEtale_extension_of_isUnramifiedInCodimensionOne
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (U : X.Opens) (hdense : DenseRange U.ι.base)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ U) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    (hunr : Stacks.FundamentalGroup.IsUnramifiedInCodimensionOne U.ι f)
    (hreg : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ (Y' : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y' ⟶ X), IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧
      ∃ e : pullback p U.ι ≅ Y, e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd p U.ι
declarations.comment: a finite étale cover unramified in codimension one extends across a regular complement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FieldValuedPoint.existsUnique_factor_of_class_eq_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2X.** Two representatives of the same point factor uniquely through a
representative whose map to the algebraic space is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem FieldValuedPoint.existsUnique_factor_of_class_eq_of_mono
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (p q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS F)
    [Mono (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)]
    (h : p.class B S hS F = q.class B S hS F) :
    ∃! f : q.siteObject B S hS F ⟶ p.siteObject B S hS F,
      F.map f.op p.value = q.value

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProfiniteTranslation.not_exists_comp_orbitMap_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**The orbit map of the origin admits no section.** For an infinite profinite group `G` and a
field `k`, the orbit map of the origin from the discrete `k`-scheme `Γ = ∐_{g ∈ G} Spec k` to the
zero-dimensional affine `k`-scheme `Y = Spec (LocallyConstant G k)` admits no section.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_exists_comp_orbitMap_eq_id [Group G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] [Infinite G] :
    ¬ ∃ s : Spec (.of (LocallyConstant G k)) ⟶ ∐ (fun _ : G => Spec (.of k)),
        s ≫ orbitMap k G = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: the orbit map of the origin has no section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_isLocallyNoetherian_and_not_isDecentSpace_of_not_exists_section
declarations.doc:
**The one-point quotient of an infinite profinite group by translation.** Let `k` be a field
and let `G` be an infinite profinite group. Let `Y = Spec (LocallyConstant G k)` be `G` as a
zero-dimensional affine `k`-scheme, let `Γ` be `G` as a discrete `k`-group scheme acting on `Y` by
translations, and let `X = Y/Γ` with projection `q : Y ⟶ X`. Then `X` is an algebraic space with a
single point, `Y` is reduced, the `k`-point of `X` at the origin is a monomorphism, and `q` factors
through no field-valued point of `X` whatsoever.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isLocallyNoetherian_and_not_isDecentSpace_of_not_exists_section :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS (profiniteTranslationQuotient k G B hS hY) ∧
      Subsingleton (points B (Spec (.of k)) hS
        (profiniteTranslationQuotient k G B hS hY)) ∧
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS
        (yoneda.obj (profiniteChart k G B hS hY)) (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T) ∧
      Mono (fieldMorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hS _ (originQuotientPoint k G B hS hY)) ∧
      ∀ (p : FieldValuedPoint B (Spec (.of k)) hS
          (profiniteTranslationQuotient k G B hS hY))
        (g : yoneda.obj (profiniteChart k G B hS hY) ⟶
          yoneda.obj (p.siteObject B (Spec (.of k)) hS _)),
        g ≫ fieldMorphism B (Spec (.of k)) hS _ p ≠ profiniteQuotientMap k G B hS hY
declarations.comment: the one-point algebraic space and the non-factorization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_isLocallyNoetherian_and_not_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**The quotient of an infinite profinite group by translation is neither locally Noetherian nor
decent.** For the quotient `X = Y/Γ` of the previous theorem, the conclusion of Stacks 0H1S and of
Stacks 0H1T fails for the projection `q : Y ⟶ X` at every residual space of `X` at its point.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isLocallyNoetherian_and_not_isDecentSpace :
    ¬ HasEtaleLocalProperty B (Spec (.of k)) hS (profiniteTranslationQuotient k G B hS hY)
        (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) ∧
      ¬ IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hS (profiniteTranslationQuotient k G B hS hY) ∧
      ∀ {W : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
        (i : W ⟶ profiniteTranslationQuotient k G B hS hY),
        IsResidualSpaceAt B (Spec (.of k)) hS (profiniteTranslationQuotient k G B hS hY)
          ((originQuotientPoint k G B hS hY).class B (Spec (.of k)) hS _) i →
        ¬ ∃ g : yoneda.obj (profiniteChart k G B hS hY) ⟶ W,
            g ≫ i = profiniteQuotientMap k G B hS hY
declarations.comment: the conclusion for the quotient of a profinite group by translation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H2Z.** An unramified 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` (**Stacks 0CIT**) is
locally quasi-finite (**Stacks 06PU**): it is quasi-DM, locally of finite type, and its fibre over
every field-valued point of the target has discrete space of points.

The three conjuncts are `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_of_isUnramified`,
the existential smooth-diagram test
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_of_isUnramified` at the
diagram `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSurjectiveEtaleSmoothDiagram_of_isDM`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.discreteTopology_points_fibre_of_isUnramified`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isUnramified
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiDM_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-DM conjunct of Stacks 0H2Z.** An unramified 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over
`S` is quasi-DM, with a representable relative diagonal.

Unramifiedness in the sense of **Stacks 0CIT** contains the Deligne–Mumford condition, and a
Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism is quasi-DM by **Stacks 050E**, part (2); the relative diagonal of a
1-morphism of algebraic stacks is always representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.comment:
the quasi-DM conjunct of local quasi-finiteness, unconditionally. The local finite
  type conjunct is `isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isUnramified`; the field-valued-fibre conjunct is
  NOT carried

declarations.name: Rlim.exists_sixTerm_exact_sequence_lim_rightDerived_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H31.** A short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups induces
the exact sequence
`0 ⟶ lim A ⟶ lim B ⟶ lim C ⟶ R¹lim A ⟶ R¹lim B ⟶ R¹lim C ⟶ 0`.
The maps other than the connecting morphism are the functorial maps of `lim` and `R¹lim`.
The connecting morphism is canonically obtained from the distinguished triangle of the short
exact sequence and is natural in morphisms of short exact sequences.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sixTerm_exact_sequence_lim_rightDerived_one
    {S : ShortComplex Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u}} (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    let F : Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u} ⥤ Ab.{u} := lim
    ∃ (RF : DerivedCategory Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u} ⥤ DerivedCategory Ab.{u})
      (α : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF) (commShift : RF.CommShift ℤ),
      letI : RF.CommShift ℤ := commShift
      RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
          (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
        RF.IsTriangulated ∧
        let R (n : ℤ) : Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u} ⥤ Ab.{u} :=
          DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u} 0 ⋙ RF ⋙
            DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{u} n
        ∃ e : F ≅ R 0,
          let δ : ∀ {T : ShortComplex Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u}}, T.ShortExact →
              (F.obj T.X₃ ⟶ (R 1).obj T.X₁) := fun {T} (hT : T.ShortExact) ↦ by
            change F.obj T.X₃ ⟶
              (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{u} 1).obj
                (RF.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u} 0).obj T.X₁))
            exact e.hom.app T.X₃ ≫
              DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ
                (RF.mapTriangle.obj hT.singleTriangle) 0 1 rfl
          (ComposableArrows.mk₅ (F.map S.f) (F.map S.g) (δ hS)
              ((R 1).map S.f) ((R 1).map S.g)).Exact ∧
            Mono (F.map S.f) ∧ Epi ((R 1).map S.g) ∧
            ∀ {T₁ T₂ : ShortComplex Rlim.InvSystemAb.{u}}
              (h₁ : T₁.ShortExact) (h₂ : T₂.ShortExact) (f : T₁ ⟶ T₂),
              δ h₁ ≫ (R 1).map f.τ₁ = F.map f.τ₃ ≫ δ h₂

declarations.name: PrincipalCompletionDiagram.derivedCompletion_principal_homology_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H32.** For `K ∈ D(A)`, the ordinary completion of `Hᵖ(K)`, the cohomology
of the derived completion of `Hᵖ(K)`, the cohomology of the derived completion of `K`, and the
inverse limits of the cohomology of `K ⊗ᴸ_A (A →[f^n] A)` form the canonical commutative
diagram of four short exact sequences from the source.  Its bottom comparison is an isomorphism
between the indicated first derived inverse limits.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedCompletion_principal_homology_comparison
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))]
    (f : A) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) (p : ℤ) :
    let I : Ideal A := Ideal.span {f}
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete I L
    ∀ (completion : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory)
      (adj : completion ⊣ P.ι),
      let completed := completion ⋙ P.ι
      ∃ S : CompletionSequences.PrincipalCompletionSequences A f completed adj.unit,
      let H (q : ℤ) := (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) q).obj K
      let C := DerivedCategory.Q.objPreimage K
      let eK := DerivedCategory.Q.objObjPreimageIso K
      let E := PrincipalTorsionTower.principalComplexSystem A f C
      let tensorSystem := principalDerivedTensorSystem A f K
      let homologySystem (q : ℤ) := tensorSystem ⋙ homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) q
      let T := CompletionSequences.milnorTriangle A E
      let completionIso := completed.mapIso eK.symm ≪≫ S.comparison.iso C
      let coneTriangle (n : ℕ) := DerivedCategory.Q.mapTriangle.obj
        (CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangle (f ^ (n + 1) • 𝟙 C))
      let ordinaryCompletion := limit (CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (H p) f)
      let limitHpTensor := limit (homologySystem p)
      let tate := CompletionSequences.adicTateModule A (H (p + 1)) f
      let H0CompletedHp := (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj
        (completed.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj (H p)))
      let HpCompletedK := (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) p).obj (completed.obj K)
      let R1Torsion := CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A
        (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H p) f)
      let R1PreviousTensor := CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A (homologySystem (p - 1))
      let middleIn : H0CompletedHp ⟶ HpCompletedK := (S.truncation K p).inclusion S.shift
      let middleOut : HpCompletedK ⟶ tate :=
        (S.truncation K p).projection f S.shift (S.moduleSequence (H (p + 1))).tateIso
      let leftIn : R1Torsion ⟶ H0CompletedHp := (S.moduleSequence (H p)).inclusion
      let leftOut : H0CompletedHp ⟶ ordinaryCompletion := (S.moduleSequence (H p)).projection
      ∃ (termIn : CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (H p) f ⟶ homologySystem p)
        (termOut : homologySystem p ⟶ PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H (p + 1)) f)
        (previousOut : homologySystem (p - 1) ⟶ PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H p) f)
        (productIso : (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) (p - 1)).obj T.obj₃ ≅
            CompletionSequences.moduleProduct A (homologySystem (p - 1)))
        (topIn : ordinaryCompletion ⟶ limitHpTensor)
        (topOut : limitHpTensor ⟶ tate)
        (htop : topIn ≫ topOut = 0)
        (columnIn : R1PreviousTensor ⟶ HpCompletedK)
        (columnOut : HpCompletedK ⟶ limitHpTensor)
        (hcolumn : columnIn ≫ columnOut = 0)
        (bottom : R1Torsion ≅ R1PreviousTensor),
        (∀ n : ℕ,
          cokernel.π (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerMultiplication A (H p) (f ^ (n + 1))) ≫
              termIn.app ⟨n⟩ =
            (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) p).map (eK.inv ≫ (coneTriangle n).mor₂)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ,
          termOut.app ⟨n⟩ ≫
              kernel.ι (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerMultiplication A (H (p + 1)) (f ^ (n + 1))) =
            (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).homologySequenceδ
              (coneTriangle n) p (p + 1) (by omega) ≫
                (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) (p + 1)).map eK.hom) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ,
          previousOut.app ⟨n⟩ ≫
              kernel.ι (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerMultiplication A (H p) (f ^ (n + 1))) =
            (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).homologySequenceδ
              (coneTriangle n) (p - 1) p (by omega) ≫
                (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) p).map eK.hom) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, topIn ≫ limit.π (homologySystem p) ⟨n⟩ =
          limit.π (CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (H p) f) ⟨n⟩ ≫ termIn.app ⟨n⟩) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, topOut ≫ limit.π (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H (p + 1)) f) ⟨n⟩ =
          limit.π (homologySystem p) ⟨n⟩ ≫ termOut.app ⟨n⟩) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, productIso.hom ≫
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (homologySystem (p - 1)).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
          (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) (p - 1)).map
            (DerivedCategory.Q.map (Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ E.obj ⟨n⟩) n))) ∧
        (productIso.hom ≫ cokernel.π (CompletionSequences.moduleDifference A (homologySystem (p -
          1))) ≫
            columnIn = (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).homologySequenceδ T (p - 1) p
              (by omega) ≫ (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) p).map completionIso.inv) ∧
        (cokernel.π (CompletionSequences.moduleDifference A (homologySystem (p - 1))) ≫ bottom.inv =
          (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (homologySystem (p - 1)).obj ⟨n⟩) n ≫
              previousOut.app ⟨n⟩) ≫
            cokernel.π (CompletionSequences.moduleDifference A
              (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H p) f))) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, columnOut ≫ limit.π (homologySystem p) ⟨n⟩ =
          (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) p).map (completionIso.hom ≫ T.mor₁ ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map (Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ E.obj ⟨n⟩) n))) ∧
        (ShortComplex.mk topIn topOut htop).ShortExact ∧
        (ShortComplex.mk middleIn middleOut (S.truncation_zero K p)).ShortExact ∧
        (ShortComplex.mk leftIn leftOut (S.moduleSequence (H p)).zero).ShortExact ∧
        (ShortComplex.mk columnIn columnOut hcolumn).ShortExact ∧
        middleIn ≫ columnOut = leftOut ≫ topIn ∧
        middleOut = columnOut ≫ topOut ∧
        bottom.hom ≫ columnIn = leftIn ≫ middleIn

declarations.name: PrincipalTorsionTower.isMittagLeffler_principalDerivedTensor_iff_powerTorsion
declarations.doc:
The cohomology tower of the derived reductions of `K` modulo the positive
powers of `f` is Mittag--Leffler if and only if the tower of elements of `H^(p + 1)(K)` killed
by those powers is Mittag--Leffler.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLeffler_principalDerivedTensor_iff_powerTorsion
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) (p : ℤ) :
    ((principalDerivedTensorSystem A f K ⋙
        homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) p) ⋙ forget (ModuleCat.{v} A)).IsMittagLeffler ↔
      ((powerTorsionSystem A ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) (p + 1)).obj K) f) ⋙
          forget (ModuleCat.{v} A)).IsMittagLeffler

declarations.name: Stacks.Invariant.QuotientComparison.charpolyFixed_map_mk_of_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H34 (tag 0H34 = Lemma 15.112.3).** For `x ∈ JR`, the characteristic
polynomial `∏_{σ ∈ G} (T - σ x) = T^n + a₁T^{n-1} + … + aₙ` has all its non-leading
coefficients `aᵢ` in `J`; equivalently, reducing the coefficients of `charpolyFixed G x`
modulo `J` gives `X ^ n`.

Implementation note: the coefficients `aᵢ` lie in `R^G`, and what has to be shown is that
they lie in `J` — the ideal of `R^G` — and not merely in the a priori larger `JR ∩ R^G`.
Writing `x = Σⱼ fⱼ bⱼ` with `fⱼ ∈ J ⊆ R^G` and `bⱼ ∈ R`, invariance of `fⱼ` gives
`σ x = Σⱼ fⱼ (σ bⱼ)`, so each elementary symmetric coefficient is a sum of products each
carrying a factor `∏ fⱼ ∈ J`, and symmetrizing over the orbit keeps the remaining cofactor
in `R^G`; hence `aᵢ ∈ J · R^G = J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem charpolyFixed_map_mk_of_mem [Fintype G] (J : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring R G))
    (x : R) (hx : x ∈ JRideal J) :
    Polynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) (charpolyFixed G x)
      = (Polynomial.X : Polynomial ((FixedPoints.subring R G) ⧸ J)) ^ (Fintype.card G)

declarations.name: Stacks.Invariant.QuotientComparison.exists_monic_map_eq_X_sub_C_pow
declarations.doc:
**(Lifting characteristic-polynomial form.)** For every `b ∈ (R / JR)^G`
there is a monic polynomial `P ∈ (R^G / J)[T]` whose image under
`Polynomial.map (invariantComparison J)` equals `(X - C b) ^ n`, where
`n = Fintype.card G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_monic_map_eq_X_sub_C_pow [Fintype G] (J : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring R G))
    (b : FixedPoints.subring (R ⧸ JRideal J) G) :
    ∃ P : Polynomial ((FixedPoints.subring R G) ⧸ J),
      P.Monic ∧
        P.map (invariantComparison J)
          = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) ^ (Fintype.card G)

declarations.name: Stacks.Invariant.QuotientComparison.X_sub_C_pow_eq_X_pow_of_mem_ker
declarations.doc:
**(Kernel elements are nilpotent-like.)** For every
`a ∈ ker(invariantComparison J)` we have `(X - C a) ^ n = X ^ n` in
`(R^G / J)[T]`, where `n = Fintype.card G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem X_sub_C_pow_eq_X_pow_of_mem_ker [Fintype G] (J : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring R G))
    (a : (FixedPoints.subring R G) ⧸ J) (ha : a ∈ RingHom.ker (invariantComparison J)) :
    (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) ^ (Fintype.card G)
      = (Polynomial.X : Polynomial ((FixedPoints.subring R G) ⧸ J)) ^ (Fintype.card G)

declarations.name: Stacks.Invariant.QuotientComparison.invariantComparison_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**(In particular: integrality.)** The comparison map
`Φ : R^G / J → (R / JR)^G` is an integral ring map: every `b ∈ (R / JR)^G` is a root
of the monic polynomial over `R^G / J` supplied by `exists_monic_map_eq_X_sub_C_pow`, because
that polynomial maps to `(X - C b) ^ n`, which vanishes at `b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invariantComparison_isIntegral [Fintype G] (J : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring R G)) :
    (invariantComparison J).IsIntegral
declarations.comment: final statement, integrality

declarations.name: Stacks.Invariant.QuotientComparison.invariantComparison_comap_isHomeomorph
declarations.doc:
**(In particular: homeomorphism on spectra.)** `Spec(Φ) : Spec((R / JR)^G) →
Spec(R^G / J)` is a homeomorphism.  This is `PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap`
(Stacks 0BR8) applied to the two facts extracted from parts (1) and (2): every
`b ∈ (R / JR)^G` has `b ^ n` in the range of `Φ` (`exists_apply_eq_pow`), and
`ker Φ` is nil (`ker_invariantComparison_le_nilradical`).
declarations.statement:
theorem invariantComparison_comap_isHomeomorph [Fintype G] (J : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring R G)) :
    IsHomeomorph (PrimeSpectrum.comap (invariantComparison J))
declarations.comment: final statement, homeomorphism on spectra

declarations.name: Stacks.Invariant.QuotientComparison.invariantComparison_residueField_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
**(In particular: purely inseparable residue extensions.)** For every prime
`𝔮 ⊆ (R / JR)^G` with contraction `𝔭 = Φ⁻¹(𝔮) ⊆ R^G / J`, the induced extension of
residue fields `κ(𝔭) → κ(𝔮)` is purely inseparable.  This is the abstract form of
Stacks 09EF (`isPurelyInseparable_residueField_of_sub_C_pow_witness`, proved with
Stacks 09EG) applied to the monic witness of part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem invariantComparison_residueField_isPurelyInseparable [Fintype G]
    (J : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring R G))
    (q : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring (R ⧸ JRideal J) G)) [q.IsPrime] :
    letI := (Ideal.ResidueField.map (q.comap (invariantComparison J)) q
      (invariantComparison J) rfl).toAlgebra
    IsPurelyInseparable (Ideal.ResidueField (q.comap (invariantComparison J)))
      (Ideal.ResidueField q)
declarations.comment: final statement, purely inseparable residue fields

declarations.name: Stacks.Invariant.QuotientComparison.invariantComparison_bijective_of_isUnit_card
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H36.** If the order of the finite group `G` acting on `R` is invertible in `R`,
the canonical comparison map `Φ : R^G / J → (R / JR)^G` is an isomorphism.

Injectivity: for `a ∈ ker Φ` the identity `(X - C a) ^ n = X ^ n` of
`X_sub_C_pow_eq_X_pow_of_mem_ker` has vanishing coefficient in degree `n - 1`, i.e. `n • a = 0`,
and `n` is invertible.  Surjectivity: `n⁻¹ ∑_{g ∈ G} g • r` is an invariant lift of any
invariant class `r̄`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invariantComparison_bijective_of_isUnit_card
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [MulSemiringAction G R]
    (J : Ideal (FixedPoints.subring R G)) (hG : IsUnit (Fintype.card G : R)) :
    Function.Bijective (invariantComparison J)

declarations.name: integralClosure_isValuationRing_of_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a valuation ring with fraction field `K` of exponential characteristic `p`, and
let `L/K` be a purely inseparable field extension. Then the integral closure `B` of `A` in `L`
satisfies the valuation-ring criterion, has fraction field `L`, and the inclusion `A → B` is an
injective local homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_isValuationRing_of_isPurelyInseparable [ExpChar K p] [IsPurelyInseparable K
  L] :
    -- (1) `B` is a valuation ring: the valuation criterion holds.
    (∀ x : L, x ∈ integralClosure A L ∨ x⁻¹ ∈ integralClosure A L) ∧
    -- (2) `Frac(B) = L`.
    IsFractionRing (integralClosure A L) L ∧
    -- (3) the inclusion `A → B` is injective and a local homomorphism.
    (Function.Injective (algebraMap A (integralClosure A L)) ∧
      IsLocalHom (algebraMap A (integralClosure A L)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InverseSystems.TorsionFreeDivisible.stacks0H39_one_iff_two
declarations.doc: Conditions (1) and (2) on an inverse system are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacks0H39_one_iff_two
    (f : End (𝟭 (SheafOfModules.{max u v} R)))
    (obj : ℕ → SheafOfModules.{max u v} R) (map : ∀ n, obj (n + 1) ⟶ obj n) :
    Condition1 f obj map ↔ Condition2 f obj map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InverseSystems.TorsionFreeDivisible.stacks0H39_two_iff_three
declarations.doc: Conditions (2) and (3) on an inverse system are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacks0H39_two_iff_three
    (f : End (𝟭 (SheafOfModules.{max u v} R)))
    (obj : ℕ → SheafOfModules.{max u v} R) (map : ∀ n, obj (n + 1) ⟶ obj n) :
    Condition2 f obj map ↔ Condition3 f obj map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InverseSystems.TorsionFreeDivisible.stacks0H39_four_imp_three
declarations.doc: Condition (4) on an inverse system implies condition (3).

    (obj : ℕ → SheafOfModules.{max u v} R) (map : ∀ n, obj (n + 1) ⟶ obj n) :
    Condition4 f obj map → Condition3 f obj map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PrincipalFormalFunctions.formalFunctionsDiagram_principalKoszulTower
declarations.doc:
**Formal functions for a principal ideal on a ringed space: [Stacks, Tag 0H3C].** Let
`(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space, let `ρ : A ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` be a homomorphism from a commutative ring
`A`, let `f ∈ A` and let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`. Let `E_n = E ⊗_{𝒪_X} (𝒪_X --f^(n+1)--> 𝒪_X)` be the
`f`-power Koszul tower, the cone of multiplication by `f^(n+1)` on `E`, so that there are
distinguished triangles `E ⟶ E ⟶ E_n ⟶ E[1]`, and let `E^ = R lim E_n`, given with its
distinguished triangle `E^ ⟶ ∏ E_n ⟶ ∏ E_n ⟶ E^[1]` whose middle map is `1 - shift`. Write
`Hᵖ(X, -)` for the cohomology of `RΓ(X, -) : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(A)`, let `(-)^∧` be derived `f`-adic
completion (a left adjoint `completion` to the inclusion of the derived-complete objects), and
let `p ∈ ℤ`. Then `RΓ(X, E^) ≅ RΓ(X, E)^∧` by an isomorphism `Φ` which, composed with the unit
`RΓ(X, E) ⟶ RΓ(X, E)^∧` and the projections `RΓ(X, E^) ⟶ RΓ(X, E_n)`, gives the maps
`RΓ(X, E) ⟶ RΓ(X, E_n)` induced by `E ⟶ E_n`, and there is the commutative diagram with exact
rows and columns

* the top row `0 ⟶ Hᵖ(X, E)^ ⟶ lim Hᵖ(X, E_n) ⟶ T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, E)) ⟶ 0`, where `Hᵖ(X, E)^` is the
  `f`-adic completion `lim Hᵖ(X, E)/fⁿ⁺¹` and `T_f` the `f`-adic Tate module `lim (-)[fⁿ⁺¹]`;
  its first map is the limit of the maps `Hᵖ(X, E)/fⁿ⁺¹ ⟶ Hᵖ(X, E_n)` induced by `E ⟶ E_n`, its
  second the limit of the boundaries `Hᵖ(X, E_n) ⟶ Hᵖ⁺¹(X, E)[fⁿ⁺¹]` of `E ⟶ E ⟶ E_n ⟶ E[1]`;
* the middle row `0 ⟶ H⁰(Hᵖ(X, E)^∧) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, E^) ⟶ T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, E)) ⟶ 0`, the sequence of
  [Stacks, Tag 0H32] for `K = RΓ(X, E)` read through `Hᵖ(Φ)`;
* the left column `0 ⟶ R¹lim Hᵖ(X, E)[fⁿ] ⟶ H⁰(Hᵖ(X, E)^∧) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, E)^ ⟶ 0` of
  [Stacks, Tag 0BKG];
* the middle column `0 ⟶ R¹lim Hᵖ⁻¹(X, E_n) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, E^) ⟶ lim Hᵖ(X, E_n) ⟶ 0`, whose second
  map is induced by the projections `E^ ⟶ E_n` and whose first descends the boundary of the
  image under `RΓ(X, -)` of the triangle of `E^`, read through the isomorphism
  `Hᵖ⁻¹(X, ∏ E_n) ≅ ∏ Hᵖ⁻¹(X, E_n)`;
* the bottom isomorphism `R¹lim Hᵖ(X, E)[fⁿ] ≅ R¹lim Hᵖ⁻¹(X, E_n)`, inverse to `R¹lim` of the
  boundaries `Hᵖ⁻¹(X, E_n) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, E)[fⁿ⁺¹]`;

the right-hand column being the identity of `T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, E))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem formalFunctionsDiagram_principalKoszulTower
    (E Ehat : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (a : Ehat ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ (principalKoszulTower X ρ f E).obj ⟨n⟩)
    (b : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ (principalKoszulTower X ρ f E).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ Ehat⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hT : Triangle.mk a (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (principalKoszulTower X ρ f E).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (principalKoszulTower X ρ f E).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
            (principalKoszulTower X ρ f E).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) b ∈
      distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))))
    (p : ℤ) :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span {f}) L
    ∀ (completion : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory)
      (adj : completion ⊣ P.ι),
      let completed := completion ⋙ P.ι
      let HH (q : ℤ) := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) q
      let RΓ := derivedSectionsOver X ρ
      let K := RΓ.obj E
      let H (q : ℤ) := (HH q).obj K
      let CE := DerivedCategory.Q.objPreimage E
      let eE := DerivedCategory.Q.objObjPreimageIso E
      let koszulTriangle (n : ℕ) := RΓ.mapTriangle.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.mapTriangle.obj
        (CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangle (smulComplex X (baseSmul X ρ f) CE ^ (n + 1)).asHom))
      let Y := fun n : ℕ ↦ (principalKoszulTower X ρ f E).obj ⟨n⟩
      let limitTriangle := RΓ.mapTriangle.obj (Triangle.mk a (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
        Pi.π Y n - Pi.π Y (n + 1) ≫
          (principalKoszulTower X ρ f E).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) b)
      let cohTower (q : ℤ) := (principalKoszulTower X ρ f E ⋙ RΓ) ⋙ HH q
      let ordinaryCompletion := limit (CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (H p) f)
      let limitCoh := limit (cohTower p)
      let tate := CompletionSequences.adicTateModule A (H (p + 1)) f
      let H0CompletedHp := (HH 0).obj
        (completed.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (H p)))
      let HpEhat := (HH p).obj (RΓ.obj Ehat)
      let R1Torsion := CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A
        (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H p) f)
      let R1PreviousCoh := CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A (cohTower (p - 1))
      let productComparison : (HH (p - 1)).obj (RΓ.obj (∏ᶜ Y)) ⟶
          CompletionSequences.moduleProduct A (cohTower (p - 1)) :=
        Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦ (HH (p - 1)).map (RΓ.map (Pi.π Y n))
      ∃ (S : CompletionSequences.PrincipalCompletionSequences A f completed adj.unit)
        (Φ : RΓ.obj Ehat ≅ completed.obj K),
        let middleIn : H0CompletedHp ⟶ HpEhat :=
          (S.truncation K p).inclusion S.shift ≫ (HH p).map Φ.inv
        let middleOut : HpEhat ⟶ tate := (HH p).map Φ.hom ≫
          (S.truncation K p).projection f S.shift (S.moduleSequence (H (p + 1))).tateIso
        let leftIn : R1Torsion ⟶ H0CompletedHp := (S.moduleSequence (H p)).inclusion
        let leftOut : H0CompletedHp ⟶ ordinaryCompletion := (S.moduleSequence (H p)).projection
        ∃ (termIn : CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (H p) f ⟶ cohTower p)
          (termOut : cohTower p ⟶ PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H (p + 1)) f)
          (previousOut : cohTower (p - 1) ⟶
            PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H p) f)
          (topIn : ordinaryCompletion ⟶ limitCoh)
          (topOut : limitCoh ⟶ tate)
          (htop : topIn ≫ topOut = 0)
          (hmiddle : middleIn ≫ middleOut = 0)
          (hleft : leftIn ≫ leftOut = 0)
          (columnIn : R1PreviousCoh ⟶ HpEhat)
          (columnOut : HpEhat ⟶ limitCoh)
          (hcolumn : columnIn ≫ columnOut = 0)
          (bottom : R1Torsion ≅ R1PreviousCoh),
          (∀ n : ℕ, adj.unit.app K ≫ Φ.inv ≫ RΓ.map a ≫ RΓ.map (Pi.π Y n) =
            RΓ.map (eE.inv ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map
              (CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr
                (smulComplex X (baseSmul X ρ f) CE ^ (n + 1)).asHom))) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ,
            cokernel.π (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerMultiplication A (H p) (f ^ (n + 1))) ≫
                termIn.app ⟨n⟩ =
              (HH p).map (RΓ.map (eE.inv ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map
                (CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr
                  (smulComplex X (baseSmul X ρ f) CE ^ (n + 1)).asHom)))) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ,
            termOut.app ⟨n⟩ ≫
                kernel.ι (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerMultiplication A (H (p + 1)) (f ^ (n + 1))) =
              (HH 0).homologySequenceδ (koszulTriangle n) p (p + 1) (by omega) ≫
                (HH (p + 1)).map (RΓ.map eE.hom)) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ,
            previousOut.app ⟨n⟩ ≫
                kernel.ι (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerMultiplication A (H p) (f ^ (n + 1))) =
              (HH 0).homologySequenceδ (koszulTriangle n) (p - 1) p (by omega) ≫
                (HH p).map (RΓ.map eE.hom)) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ, topIn ≫ limit.π (cohTower p) ⟨n⟩ =
            limit.π (CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (H p) f) ⟨n⟩ ≫ termIn.app ⟨n⟩) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ, topOut ≫
              limit.π (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H (p + 1)) f) ⟨n⟩ =
            limit.π (cohTower p) ⟨n⟩ ≫ termOut.app ⟨n⟩) ∧
          IsIso productComparison ∧
          (productComparison ≫
              cokernel.π (CompletionSequences.moduleDifference A (cohTower (p - 1))) ≫ columnIn =
            (HH 0).homologySequenceδ limitTriangle (p - 1) p (by omega)) ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ, columnOut ≫ limit.π (cohTower p) ⟨n⟩ =
            (HH p).map (RΓ.map a ≫ RΓ.map (Pi.π Y n))) ∧
          (cokernel.π (CompletionSequences.moduleDifference A (cohTower (p - 1))) ≫ bottom.inv =
            (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
              Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (cohTower (p - 1)).obj ⟨n⟩) n ≫ previousOut.app ⟨n⟩) ≫
              cokernel.π (CompletionSequences.moduleDifference A
                (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H p) f))) ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk topIn topOut htop).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk middleIn middleOut hmiddle).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk leftIn leftOut hleft).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk columnIn columnOut hcolumn).ShortExact ∧
          middleIn ≫ columnOut = leftOut ≫ topIn ∧
          middleOut = columnOut ≫ topOut ∧
          bottom.hom ≫ columnIn = leftIn ≫ middleIn
declarations.comment: the whole diagram, with its maps the ones induced by E ⟶ E_n, the boundaries of E ⟶ E ⟶ E_n ⟶ E[1], the projections E^ ⟶ E_n and the triangle of E^, the sequences of Stacks 0BKG and 0H32 read through RΓ(X, E^) ≅ RΓ(X, E)^∧ (compatible with the maps to RΓ(X, E_n)); exactness of rows and columns and the three commutativities

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PrincipalFormalFunctions.nonempty_iso_derivedSections_quotientTower_derivedCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Clause (7) of [Stacks, Tag 0H3E]: `RΓ(X, ℱ^) = RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧` on a ringed space.** Let
`(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space, let `ρ : A ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` be a homomorphism from a commutative ring
`A`, let `f ∈ A` and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules whose `f`-power torsion stabilizes.  Let
`ℱ^` be a derived limit of the tower of honest quotients `ℱ/f^(n+1)ℱ`.  Then

`RΓ(X, ℱ^) ≅ RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧`,

the object `RΓ(X, ℱ^)` is derived complete for `(f)`, and for every `p` its `p`-th cohomology
module is that of `RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧` — the identification `Hᵖ(X, ℱ^) = Hᵖ(RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧)` the diagram of
the source rests on.

This is the displayed equality of [Stacks, Tag 0BLD] on an arbitrary ringed space: the Koszul
form of it is `nonempty_iso_derivedSections_koszulTower_derivedCompletion`, and the
pro-isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0H3D] replaces the Koszul tower by the quotient tower.  No
quasi-coherence is needed, only stabilization of the `f`-power torsion.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_derivedSections_quotientTower_derivedCompletion
    (ℱ : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hstab : Stabilizes ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ))
    (Fhat : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hFhat : IsDerivedLimit (Csys ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ)) Fhat) :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span {f}) L
    ∀ (completion : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory)
      (_ : completion ⊣ P.ι),
      let completed := completion ⋙ P.ι
      let sglF :=
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) 0).obj ℱ
      Nonempty ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat ≅
          completed.obj ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj sglF)) ∧
        IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span {f}) ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat) ∧
        ∀ p : ℤ, Nonempty
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) p).obj
              ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat) ≅
            (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) p).obj
              (completed.obj ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj sglF)))
declarations.comment: the identification RΓ(X, ℱ^) = RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧ and the resulting Hᵖ(X, ℱ^) = Hᵖ(RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧), on a ringed space, with derived f-adic completion presented as in Stacks 0BKG by an arbitrary left adjoint to the inclusion of the derived-complete objects; also derived completeness of RΓ(X, ℱ^)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PrincipalFormalFunctions.exists_formalFunctionsDiagram_quotientTower
declarations.doc:
**Formal functions for a principal ideal along the quotient tower: the whole diagram of
[Stacks, Tag 0H3E].** Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space, let `ρ : A ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` be a homomorphism
from a commutative ring `A`, let `f ∈ A`, let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules whose `f`-power
torsion stabilizes, and let `ℱ^` be a derived limit of the tower of quotients `ℱ/f^(n+1)ℱ`.  Then
for every `p` the commutative diagram of the source exists, with exact rows and columns:

* the top row `0 ⟶ Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^ ⟶ lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, ℱ)) ⟶ 0`;
* the middle row `0 ⟶ H⁰(Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^∧) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, ℱ^) ⟶ T_f(Hᵖ⁺¹(X, ℱ)) ⟶ 0`;
* the left column `0 ⟶ R¹lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ)[fⁿ] ⟶ H⁰(Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^∧) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, ℱ)^ ⟶ 0`;
* the middle column `0 ⟶ R¹lim Hᵖ⁻¹(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, ℱ^) ⟶ lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ) ⟶ 0`;
* the bottom comparison `R¹lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ)[fⁿ] ≅ R¹lim Hᵖ⁻¹(X, ℱ/fⁿℱ)`;

the three commutativities that make the nine terms a diagram, and the identification
`RΓ(X, ℱ^) ≅ RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧`.  As in [Stacks, Tag 0H32], `S` is the data of the two completion
sequences of [Stacks, Tag 0BKG] for `RΓ(X, ℱ)`, so the middle row and the left column are that
source's own maps, and `γ` is the identification of `Hᵖ(X, ℱ^)` with `Hᵖ(RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧)`.

This is `exists_formalFunctionsDiagram_principalKoszulTower` with the `f`-power Koszul tower
replaced by the tower of honest quotients, the replacement being licensed by the pro-isomorphism
of [Stacks, Tag 0H3D].  Only the two tower-dependent terms and `Hᵖ(X, ℱ^)` change, and they
change by isomorphism: a pro-isomorphism shifts the index, so the limit and the first derived
limit of the two cohomology towers agree as modules while the individual projections do not
correspond, which is why the per-level normalizations of the Koszul form are not asserted here.
The middle column *is* available with its maps normalized directly by the Milnor triangle of the
quotient tower, as `Stacks.Cohomology.QuotientTowerFormalFunctions`
`.exists_shortExact_homology_derivedSections_quotientTower`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_formalFunctionsDiagram_quotientTower
    (ℱ : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hstab : Stabilizes ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ))
    (Fhat : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hFhat : IsDerivedLimit (Csys ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ)) Fhat)
    (p : ℤ) :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span {f}) L
    ∀ (completion : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory)
      (adj : completion ⊣ P.ι),
      let completed := completion ⋙ P.ι
      let HH (q : ℤ) := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) q
      let sglF :=
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) 0).obj ℱ
      let K := (derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj sglF
      let H (q : ℤ) := (HH q).obj K
      let quotTower (q : ℤ) :=
        (Csys ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ) ⋙ derivedSectionsOver X ρ) ⋙ HH q
      let ordinaryCompletion := limit (CompletionSequences.powerQuotientSystem A (H p) f)
      let limitQuot := limit (quotTower p)
      let tate := CompletionSequences.adicTateModule A (H (p + 1)) f
      let H0CompletedHp := (HH 0).obj
        (completed.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (H p)))
      let HpFhat := (HH p).obj ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat)
      let R1Torsion := CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A
        (PrincipalTorsionTower.powerTorsionSystem A (H p) f)
      let R1PreviousQuot := CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A (quotTower (p - 1))
      ∃ (S : CompletionSequences.PrincipalCompletionSequences A f completed adj.unit)
        (γ : HpFhat ≅ (HH p).obj (completed.obj K)),
        let middleIn : H0CompletedHp ⟶ HpFhat := (S.truncation K p).inclusion S.shift ≫ γ.inv
        let middleOut : HpFhat ⟶ tate := γ.hom ≫ (S.truncation K p).projection f S.shift
          (S.moduleSequence (H (p + 1))).tateIso
        let leftIn : R1Torsion ⟶ H0CompletedHp := (S.moduleSequence (H p)).inclusion
        let leftOut : H0CompletedHp ⟶ ordinaryCompletion := (S.moduleSequence (H p)).projection
        ∃ (topIn : ordinaryCompletion ⟶ limitQuot)
          (topOut : limitQuot ⟶ tate)
          (htop : topIn ≫ topOut = 0)
          (hmiddle : middleIn ≫ middleOut = 0)
          (hleft : leftIn ≫ leftOut = 0)
          (columnIn : R1PreviousQuot ⟶ HpFhat)
          (columnOut : HpFhat ⟶ limitQuot)
          (hcolumn : columnIn ≫ columnOut = 0)
          (bottom : R1Torsion ≅ R1PreviousQuot),
          (ShortComplex.mk topIn topOut htop).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk middleIn middleOut hmiddle).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk leftIn leftOut hleft).ShortExact ∧
          (ShortComplex.mk columnIn columnOut hcolumn).ShortExact ∧
          middleIn ≫ columnOut = leftOut ≫ topIn ∧
          middleOut = columnOut ≫ topOut ∧
          bottom.hom ≫ columnIn = leftIn ≫ middleIn ∧
          Nonempty ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat ≅ completed.obj K)
declarations.comment: the whole diagram for the quotient tower ℱ/fⁿℱ: the top row, the middle row, the left column, the middle column, the bottom isomorphism, the three commutativities, and the identification RΓ(X, ℱ^) = RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧; derived f-adic completion presented as in Stacks 0BKG by an arbitrary left adjoint to the inclusion of the derived-complete objects

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.QuotientTowerFormalFunctions.exists_shortExact_homology_derivedSections_quotientTower
declarations.doc:
**Formal functions for a principal ideal along the quotient tower: the middle column.**
Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space, let `ρ : A ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` be a homomorphism from a commutative
ring `A`, let `f ∈ A` and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules whose `f`-power torsion stabilizes.
Let `ℱ^` be a derived limit of the tower of quotients `ℱ/f^(n+1)ℱ` and let `E^` be a derived limit
of the `f`-power Koszul tower. Then `E^ ≅ ℱ^`, and for every `p` the cohomology of `RΓ(X, ℱ^)`
over `A` sits in a short exact sequence

`0 ⟶ R¹lim Hᵖ⁻¹(X, ℱ/f^(n+1)ℱ) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, ℱ^) ⟶ lim Hᵖ(X, ℱ/f^(n+1)ℱ) ⟶ 0`,

whose inclusion descends the connecting morphism of the Milnor triangle and whose projection is
characterized by the limit projections, and whose outer terms are isomorphic to the outer terms of
the corresponding sequence for the Koszul tower.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_homology_derivedSections_quotientTower (f : A)
    (ℱ : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (hstab : Stabilizes ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ))
    (Fhat Ehat : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hFhat : IsDerivedLimit (Csys ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ)) Fhat)
    (hEhat : IsDerivedLimit (Ksys ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ)) Ehat) :
    let F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) :=
      Csys ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ) ⋙ derivedSectionsOver X ρ
    let G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) :=
      Ksys ((baseSmul X ρ f).asHom.app ℱ) ⋙ derivedSectionsOver X ρ
    let Y : ℕ → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) := fun n ↦ F.obj (op n)
    let d : (∏ᶜ Y) ⟶ ∏ᶜ Y := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
      Pi.π Y n - Pi.π Y (n + 1) ≫ F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    Nonempty (Ehat ≅ Fhat) ∧
      ∃ (a : (derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat ⟶ ∏ᶜ Y)
        (b : (∏ᶜ Y) ⟶ ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
        let T := Triangle.mk a d b
        T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) ∧
          ∀ p : ℤ,
            let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) p
            let H₁ := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (p - 1)
            let homologySystem : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A := F ⋙ H
            let shiftedHomologySystem : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A := F ⋙ H₁
            let P : ModuleCat.{u} A :=
              ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)
            let δ : P ⟶ P := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
              Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)) n -
                Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (op n)) (n + 1) ≫
                  shiftedHomologySystem.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
            ∃ (e : H₁.obj (∏ᶜ Y) ≅ P)
              (i : cokernel δ ⟶ H.obj ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat))
              (q : H.obj ((derivedSectionsOver X ρ).obj Fhat) ⟶ limit homologySystem)
              (w : i ≫ q = 0),
              e.hom = piComparison H₁ Y ∧
                cokernel.π δ ≫ i = e.inv ≫
                  DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ T (p - 1) p ∧
                (∀ n : ℕ, q ≫ limit.π homologySystem (op n) =
                  H.map a ≫ H.map (Pi.π Y n)) ∧
                (ShortComplex.mk i q w).ShortExact ∧
                Nonempty (limit homologySystem ≅ limit (G ⋙ H)) ∧
                Nonempty (cokernel δ ≅
                  CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A (G ⋙ H₁))
declarations.comment:
the middle column of the diagram, transported to the quotient tower ℱ/fⁿℱ by
the pro-isomorphism of Tag 0H3D; its two maps normalized by the Milnor triangle of the quotient
tower itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeminormal_iff_isIso_seminormalizationHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3G.** A scheme is seminormal if and only if its canonical
seminormalization morphism is an isomorphism, i.e. if and only if it equals its own
seminormalization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeminormal_iff_isIso_seminormalizationHom (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsSeminormal X ↔ IsIso X.seminormalizationHom
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeminormal_iff_isIso_of_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3G.** A scheme is seminormal if and only if every universal
homeomorphism to it from a reduced scheme inducing isomorphisms on all residue fields is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeminormal_iff_isIso_of_universalHomeomorphism (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsSeminormal X ↔
      ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (π : Y ⟶ X), UniversalHomeomorphism π →
        (∀ y : Y, IsIso (π.residueFieldMap y)) → IsReduced Y → IsIso π
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAbsolutelyWeaklyNormal_iff_isIso_absoluteWeakNormalizationHom'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3H.** A scheme is absolutely weakly normal if and only if its
canonical absolute weak normalization morphism is an isomorphism, i.e. if and only if it equals
its own absolute weak normalization.

theorem isAbsolutelyWeaklyNormal_iff_isIso_absoluteWeakNormalizationHom' (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsAbsolutelyWeaklyNormal X ↔ IsIso X.absoluteWeakNormalizationHom
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAbsolutelyWeaklyNormal_iff_isIso_of_universalHomeomorphism'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3H.** A scheme is absolutely weakly normal if and only if every
universal homeomorphism to it from a reduced scheme is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyWeaklyNormal_iff_isIso_of_universalHomeomorphism' (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsAbsolutelyWeaklyNormal X ↔
      ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (π : Y ⟶ X), UniversalHomeomorphism π → IsReduced Y → IsIso π
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeWeakNormalization
declarations.doc:
The relative weak normalization of `A` in `B`: the largest `A`-subalgebra of `B` whose
spectrum is a universal homeomorphism over `Spec(A)`.
declarations.statement:
def relativeWeakNormalization (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] :
    Subalgebra A B
declarations.comment: the algebra

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeWeakNormalization_isUniversalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
If `Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is dominant, the relative weak normalization has spectrum
universally homeomorphic to `Spec(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeWeakNormalization_isUniversalHomeomorphism
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (_h : IsDominant (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op)) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (relativeWeakNormalization A B))).op)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.range_le_relativeWeakNormalization
declarations.doc:
The image of every intermediate `A`-algebra universally homeomorphic over `Spec(A)` is
contained in the relative weak normalization.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_le_relativeWeakNormalization
    (A B C : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C]
    (g : C →ₐ[A] B)
    (_hB : IsDominant (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op))
    (hC : UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A C)).op)) :
    g.range ≤ relativeWeakNormalization A B
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeWeakNormalization_localization
declarations.doc: Relative weak normalization commutes with localization at a submonoid of the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeWeakNormalization_localization
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (h : IsDominant (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op))
    (S : Submonoid A) :
    let f : Localization S →+* Localization (S.map (algebraMap A B)) :=
      IsLocalization.map (Localization (S.map (algebraMap A B))) (algebraMap A B)
        S.le_comap_map
    let _ : Algebra (Localization S) (Localization (S.map (algebraMap A B))) := f.toAlgebra
    Algebra.adjoin (Localization S)
        (algebraMap B (Localization (S.map (algebraMap A B))) ''
          (relativeWeakNormalization A B : Set B)) =
      relativeWeakNormalization (Localization S)
    (Localization (S.map (algebraMap A B)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSeminormalization
declarations.doc: The relative seminormalization of `A` in `B`, for a dominant map `Spec B ⟶ Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def relativeSeminormalization
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (_hdom : IsDominant
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op)) :
    Subalgebra A B
declarations.comment: the algebra

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSeminormalization_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
The spectrum of the relative seminormalization is universally homeomorphic to the spectrum of
the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeSeminormalization_universalHomeomorphism
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hdom : IsDominant
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op)) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap A (relativeSeminormalization A B hdom))).op)
declarations.comment: part (1), universal homeomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSeminormalization_residueFieldMap_isIso
declarations.doc: The relative seminormalization induces isomorphisms on all residue fields.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeSeminormalization_residueFieldMap_isIso
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hdom : IsDominant
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op)) :
    let f := Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (algebraMap A (relativeSeminormalization A B hdom))).op
    ∀ x, IsIso (f.residueFieldMap x)
declarations.comment: part (1), residue fields

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.map_mem_relativeSeminormalization
declarations.doc:
Every intermediate algebra universally homeomorphic to the base and with unchanged residue
fields maps into the relative seminormalization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem map_mem_relativeSeminormalization
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hdom : IsDominant
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op))
    {C : Type u} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] (g : C →ₐ[A] B)
    [UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A C)).op)]
    (hres : ∀ x, IsIso ((Scheme.Spec.map
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A C)).op).residueFieldMap x)) :
    ∀ c, g c ∈ relativeSeminormalization A B hdom
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_relativeSeminormalization_localization_iff
declarations.doc:
An element of the relative seminormalization after localization is exactly a fraction whose
numerator belongs to the original relative seminormalization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_relativeSeminormalization_localization_iff
    (A B Aₛ Bₛ : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Aₛ] [CommRing Bₛ]
    [Algebra A B] (S : Submonoid A)
    [Algebra A Aₛ] [IsLocalization S Aₛ]
    [Algebra B Bₛ] [IsLocalization (S.map (algebraMap A B)) Bₛ]
    [Algebra A Bₛ] [IsScalarTower A B Bₛ]
    [Algebra Aₛ Bₛ] [IsScalarTower A Aₛ Bₛ]
    (hdom : IsDominant
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op))
    (hdomₛ : IsDominant
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Aₛ Bₛ)).op))
    (x : Bₛ) :
    x ∈ relativeSeminormalization Aₛ Bₛ hdomₛ ↔
      ∃ (b : B), b ∈ relativeSeminormalization A B hdom ∧
        ∃ s : S, x = IsLocalization.mk' Bₛ b
          ⟨algebraMap A B s.1, Submonoid.mem_map.mpr ⟨s.1, s.2, rfl⟩⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_initial_universalHomeomorphismFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Relative weak normalization** ([Stacks, Tag 0H3N]). A quasi-compact, quasi-separated,
dominant morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` has an initial factorization `Y ⟶ X' ⟶ X` with `X' ⟶ X` a universal
homeomorphism, and this factorization is glued from the affine relative weak normalizations.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_initial_universalHomeomorphismFactorization
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [IsDominant f] :
    ∃ F : UniversalHomeomorphismFactorization f,
      Nonempty (Limits.IsInitial F) ∧ Nonempty F.AffineGluingData
declarations.comment: weak_initial

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weakNormalization_isPullback_open
declarations.doc:
Relative weak normalization commutes with restriction to an open subscheme
of the target, as a factorization of the restricted morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem weakNormalization_isPullback_open
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [IsDominant f] (U : X.Opens) :
    letI : IsDominant (f ∣_ U) := IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.restrict (‹IsDominant f›) U
    let F := weakNormalizationFactorization f
    let F_U := weakNormalizationFactorization (f ∣_ U)
    ∃! h : F_U.middle ⟶ F.middle,
      IsPullback h F_U.toBase F.toBase U.ι ∧
      F_U.toMiddle ≫ h = (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ≫ F.toMiddle
declarations.comment: weak_open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_initial_subintegralFactorization
declarations.doc:
The category of factorizations through universal homeomorphisms inducing
isomorphisms on residue fields has an initial object.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_initial_subintegralFactorization
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [IsDominant f] :
    ∃ F : SubintegralFactorization f, Nonempty (Limits.IsInitial F)
declarations.comment: part (2), the seminormalization factorization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_isPullback_seminormalizationFactorization_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3N.** Formation of the relative seminormalization factorization
commutes with base change to an open subscheme of the target: the intermediate scheme of the
factorization of `f ∣_ U` is the restriction of the intermediate scheme of the factorization of
`f`, by a unique morphism compatible with both legs.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_isPullback_seminormalizationFactorization_restrict
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [IsDominant f] (U : X.Opens) :
    letI : IsDominant (f ∣_ U) := IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.restrict (‹IsDominant f›) U
    ∃! h : (seminormalizationFactorization (f ∣_ U)).middle ⟶
        (seminormalizationFactorization f).middle,
      IsPullback h (seminormalizationFactorization (f ∣_ U)).toBase
          (seminormalizationFactorization f).toBase U.ι ∧
        (seminormalizationFactorization (f ∣_ U)).toMiddle ≫ h =
          (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ≫ (seminormalizationFactorization f).toMiddle
declarations.comment: part (3), compatibility with restriction to opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_iso_seminormalization_seminormalizationFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3Q.** If every quasi-compact open of `X` has finitely many
irreducible components, the seminormalization of `X` in its normalization is canonically
isomorphic over `X` to the seminormalization of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_seminormalization_seminormalizationFactorization (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    letI := Scheme.quasiCompactFromGenericPointResidueFields X hX
    letI := Scheme.quasiSeparatedFromGenericPointResidueFields X
    letI := Scheme.normalization_isDominant X hX
    ∃! e : (seminormalizationFactorization (Scheme.normalization X hX)).middle ≅
        X.seminormalization,
      e.hom ≫ X.seminormalizationHom =
        (seminormalizationFactorization (Scheme.normalization X hX)).toBase
declarations.comment:
the seminormalization of `X` in its normalization agrees with the
seminormalization of `X`; the only hypothesis is the tag's own assumption `hX` that every
quasi-compact open of `X` has finitely many irreducible components, which is what makes the
normalization of `X` exist

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.weakNormalizationFactorization
declarations.doc: The weak normalization of `X` in its normalization, as a factorization.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsWeaklyNormal
declarations.doc: A scheme is weakly normal if its weak normalization morphism is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsWeaklyNormal (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isWeaklyNormal_spec_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3T.** An affine scheme with finitely many irreducible components
is weakly normal exactly when its coordinate ring is seminormal and satisfies the prime-power
divisibility condition for nonzerodivisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyNormal_spec_iff (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (hA : ∀ U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens, IsCompact (U : Set (Spec (.of A))) →
      (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    Scheme.IsWeaklyNormal (Spec (.of A)) hA ↔ IsWeaklyNormalRing A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isWeaklyNormal_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3U.** Every open subscheme of a weakly normal scheme is weakly
normal.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyNormal_open {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (hX : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    (hWN : Scheme.IsWeaklyNormal X hX) (U : X.Opens) :
    ∃ hU : ∀ V : U.toScheme.Opens,
      IsCompact (V : Set U.toScheme) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite,
      Scheme.IsWeaklyNormal U.toScheme hU
declarations.comment: open subschemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isWeaklyNormal_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3U.** For a scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many
irreducible components, weak normality is equivalent to the two ring conditions of Tag 0H3T on
every affine open, to those conditions on a single affine open covering, and to the existence of
an open covering by weakly normal schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyNormal_tfae (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    List.TFAE [
      Scheme.IsWeaklyNormal X hX,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, IsWeaklyNormalRing Γ(X, U.1),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        (⨆ i, (U i).1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, IsWeaklyNormalRing Γ(X, (U i).1),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧
          ∀ i, ∃ hUi : ∀ V : (U i).toScheme.Opens,
            IsCompact (V : Set (U i).toScheme) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite,
            Scheme.IsWeaklyNormal (U i).toScheme hUi]
declarations.comment: equivalent conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_relativeDimensionLE_baseChange_of_limitBaseChange
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Tag 081D, if the base change of `f₀` to the limit has relative
dimension at most `d` and `f₀` is locally of finite type, then the base change of `f₀` to some
later stage has relative dimension at most `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_relativeDimensionLE_baseChange_of_limitBaseChange
    (D : DescentSituation.{u, u} I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.system.obj (op D.base))) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left] (d : ℕ)
    (h : RelativeDimensionLE (baseChangeMap (D.limitCone.π.app (op D.base)) X₀ Y₀ f₀) d) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : D.base ≤ i),
      RelativeDimensionLE (baseChangeMap (D.system.map (homOfLE hi).op) X₀ Y₀ f₀) d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_purelyInseparable_extension_smooth_stratification
declarations.doc:
A finite-type scheme over a field has a finite smooth stratification after a finite purely
inseparable extension of the field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_purelyInseparable_extension_smooth_stratification
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k')
      (_ : Module.Finite k k') (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k k'),
      let g : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))
      let Y : Scheme.{u} := pullback f g
      let p : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k') := pullback.snd f g
      ∃ (t : ℕ) (Z : Fin (t + 1) → Y.IdealSheafData),
        Z 0 = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds Y) ∧
        Z ⟨t, Nat.lt_succ_self t⟩ = ⊤ ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, Z i.castSucc ≤ Z i.succ) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, ∃ U : (Z i.castSucc).subscheme.Opens,
          (U : Set (Z i.castSucc).subscheme) =
            {x | (Z i.castSucc).subschemeι x ∉ (Z i.succ).support} ∧
          Smooth (U.ι ≫ (Z i.castSucc).subschemeι ≫ p))

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.topologicalKrullDim_supp_fiber_le_of_generic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H3X.** The dimension of the support of a finite type quasi-coherent
module flat over an irreducible base does not increase from the generic fibre to any other
fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_supp_fiber_le_of_generic
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F)
    [IrreducibleSpace S] (η : S) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (r : WithBot ℕ∞)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim
      (SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι η)).obj F)) ≤
        r)
    (s : S) :
    topologicalKrullDim
      (SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).obj F)) ≤
        r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HasFlatStratification.of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A morphism of finite presentation between quasi-compact quasi-separated
schemes has a flat stratification of its base: a finite descending chain of closed subschemes,
each cut out by an ideal sheaf of finite type, beginning with a thickening of the base and ending
with the empty scheme, over each of whose locally closed strata the base change of the morphism
is flat.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HasFlatStratification.of_finitePresentation_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**The Noetherian case of Stacks 0H3Z**, with the hypotheses of the tag: a morphism of finite
presentation to a Noetherian base has a flat stratification.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasFlatStratification.of_finitePresentation_of_isNoetherian {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian S] (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : FinitePresentation f) : HasFlatStratification f
declarations.comment: the case of a Noetherian base. The general quasi-compact quasi-separated case of the tag is `AlgebraicGeometry.HasFlatStratification.of_finitePresentation`, which reduces to this one by absolute Noetherian approximation

declarations.name: Module.exists_flat_localizedModule_coker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H40.** A map from a finite `A`-module to a finite
`B`-module, for finite type algebras `R → A → B` over a Noetherian domain,
has flat cokernel over `R` after a suitable principal localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.exists_flat_localizedModule_coker
    {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FiniteType R A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
    {M : Type uM} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R A M]
    {N : Type uN} [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N] [Module.Finite B N]
    [Module A N] [IsScalarTower A B N]
    [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R A N]
    (φ : M →ₗ[A] N) :
    ∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧
      Module.Flat (Localization.Away f)
        (LocalizedModule.Away f (N ⧸ LinearMap.range (φ.restrictScalars R)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasImageBaseChangeStratification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H41.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and
`f : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of schemes over `S` with both `X` and `Y` of finite presentation over `S`.
Then there are a `t ≥ 0` and closed subschemes `S ⊇ S₀ ⊇ S₁ ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ S_t = ∅` such that each
`S_i → S` is defined by a finite type ideal sheaf, `S₀ ⊆ S` is a thickening, and formation of the
scheme-theoretic image of the base change of `f` to each stratum `S_i ∖ S_{i+1}` commutes with
arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasImageBaseChangeStratification {S : Scheme.{u}}
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (X Y : Over S) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : FinitePresentation X.hom) (hY : FinitePresentation Y.hom) :
    HasImageBaseChangeStratification f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smooth_stratification_at_generic_point
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H43.** Smooth stratification near the generic
point of an irreducible component of a reduced base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_stratification_at_generic_point
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : FinitePresentation f)
    [IsReduced S] (η : S)
    (hη : ∃ C ∈ irreducibleComponents S, IsGenericPoint η C) :
    ∃ (U : S.Opens) (_ : η ∈ U) (V : Scheme.{u}) (g : V ⟶ U.toScheme),
      Function.Surjective g ∧ UniversallyInjective g ∧
        Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree g ∧
        ∃ (t : ℕ) (Z : Fin (t + 1) → Scheme.{u})
            (j : (i : Fin (t + 1)) → Z i ⟶ pullback f (g ≫ U.ι))
            (k : (i : Fin t) → Z i.succ ⟶ Z i.castSucc)
            (W : (i : Fin t) → (Z i.castSucc).Opens),
          (∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (j i)) ∧
          (∀ i, (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.idealSheaf (j i).toLRSHom.toShHom).IsFiniteType) ∧
          Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening (j 0) ∧
          IsEmpty (Z (Fin.last t)) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin t, IsClosedImmersion (k i)) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin t, k i ≫ j i.castSucc = j i.succ) ∧
          (∀ (i : Fin t) (x : Z i.castSucc),
            x ∈ W i ↔ j i.castSucc x ∉ Set.range (j i.succ)) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin t, Smooth ((W i).ι ≫ j i.castSucc ≫
            pullback.snd f (g ≫ U.ι)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasSmoothStratificationAfterFiniteLocallyFreeCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H44.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of finite presentation between
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes. Then there are a `t ≥ 0` and closed subschemes
`S ⊇ S₀ ⊇ S₁ ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ S_t = ∅` such that each `S_i → S` is defined by a finite type ideal sheaf,
`S₀ ⊆ S` is a thickening, each stratum `S_i ∖ S_{i+1}` carries a surjective finite locally free
morphism `T_i → S_i ∖ S_{i+1}`, and `X ×_S T_i` carries closed subschemes
`X ×_S T_i ⊇ Z_{i,0} ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ Z_{i,t_i} = ∅`, each defined by a finite type ideal sheaf, with
`Z_{i,0} ⊆ X ×_S T_i` a thickening and each `Z_{i,j} ∖ Z_{i,j+1} → T_i` smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSmoothStratificationAfterFiniteLocallyFreeCover {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : FinitePresentation f) :
    HasSmoothStratificationAfterFiniteLocallyFreeCover f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isHCovering_iff_isPHCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H45.** Over a locally Noetherian scheme a family of morphisms is an h covering
if and only if it is a ph covering, because there local finite presentation and local finite
type agree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isHCovering_iff_isPHCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian T]
    {I : Type v} (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) :
    IsHCovering X f ↔ IsPHCovering X f

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H46.** The support of a cycle `α = ∑ n_Z [Z]` on `X`, namely the union
`Supp(α) = ⋃_{n_Z ≠ 0} Z` of the integral closed subschemes occurring in `α` with a nonzero
coefficient.

An integral closed subscheme of `X` is given by its underlying irreducible closed subset
`Z : IrreducibleCloseds X`, and a cycle is a locally finitely supported function on the points
of `X` which records the coefficient of `Z` at the generic point of `Z`, so that
`n_Z = α Z.isIrreducible.genericPoint`.
declarations.statement: def cycleSupport (α : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ) : Set X
declarations.comment: support of a cycle

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.IsEffectiveCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H47.** A cycle is *effective* when it can be written as a sum
`∑ n_Z [Z]` of integral closed subschemes with all `n_Z ≥ 0`, that is, when every coefficient
of the cycle is nonnegative.
declarations.statement: def IsEffectiveCycle {X : Scheme.{u}} (c : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonMap_first_of_middle_and_third
declarations.doc:
For a short exact sequence `0 → F' → F → F'' → 0` of
coherent modules on `U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)` with `A` Noetherian, if the comparison maps of
`Stacks.Algebraization.comparisonMap` for `F` and `F''` are isomorphisms, so is that for `F'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_comparisonMap_first_of_middle_and_third
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I a : Ideal A)
    (S : ShortComplex (complementZeroLocus A a : Scheme).Modules) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    [S.X₁.IsCoherent] [S.X₂.IsCoherent] [S.X₃.IsCoherent]
    (h₂ : IsIso (comparisonMap A I a S.X₂)) (h₃ : IsIso (comparisonMap A I a S.X₃)) :
    IsIso (comparisonMap A I a S.X₁)
declarations.comment: first comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonMap_middle_of_ends
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H48, the middle comparison.** For a short exact sequence `0 → F' → F → F'' → 0` of
coherent modules on `U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)` with `A` Noetherian, if the comparison maps of
`Stacks.Algebraization.comparisonMap` for `F'` and `F''` are isomorphisms, so is that for `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_comparisonMap_middle_of_ends (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I a : Ideal A) (S : ShortComplex (complementZeroLocus A a : Scheme).Modules)
    (hS : S.ShortExact) [S.X₁.IsCoherent] [S.X₂.IsCoherent] [S.X₃.IsCoherent]
    (h₁ : IsIso (comparisonMap A I a S.X₁)) (h₃ : IsIso (comparisonMap A I a S.X₃)) :
    IsIso (comparisonMap A I a S.X₂)
declarations.comment: middle comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonMap_span_singleton_of_two_lt_closureLocalDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H49.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let `f ∈ 𝔞 ⊆ A` and let `ℱ` be
a coherent module on `U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)`. Assume `A` is `f`-adically complete and has a
dualizing complex, and that whenever `x` is an associated point of `ℱ` with `f ∉ 𝔭_x`, whose
closure meets `V(f)` outside `V(𝔞)`, and `z ∈ closure{x} ∩ V(𝔞)`, the local ring of
`closure{x}` at `z` has dimension greater than two. Then the comparison map

`colim_V Γ(V, ℱ) ⟶ lim Γ(U, ℱ / fⁿ ℱ)`

is an isomorphism, the colimit being over the opens `V ⊆ U` containing `U ∩ V(f)`.

The closure of `x` in `Spec(A)` is `V(𝔭_x)`, so "`closure{x} ∩ V(f) ⊄ V(𝔞)`" is the existence
of a prime `y ⊇ 𝔭_x` with `f ∈ y` and `𝔞 ⊄ y`, and "`z ∈ closure{x} ∩ V(𝔞)`" is `𝔭_x ≤ z` and
`𝔞 ≤ z`. The dimension of `𝒪_{closure{x}, z}` is the Krull dimension of the primes of `A`
between `𝔭_x` and `z`, which is `Stacks.Algebraization.closureLocalDimension A 𝔭_x z`. No
hypothesis supplying the surjectivity half of Stacks 0EG2
(`Stacks.Algebraization.ComparisonSurjectivity`) is assumed.

The dualizing complex enters through its two consequences used by the source, universal
catenarity (Stacks 0A80) and Gorenstein, hence `(S₁)`, formal fibres (Stacks 0AWY); see the
module documentation for the rest of the argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_comparisonMap_span_singleton_of_two_lt_closureLocalDimension
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (a : Ideal A) (f : A) (_hf : f ∈ a)
    (F : (complementZeroLocus A a : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) A)
    (hdualizing : ∃ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A), Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hdimension : ∀ x : (complementZeroLocus A a : Scheme),
      x ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F → f ∉ x.1.asIdeal →
      (∃ y : PrimeSpectrum A,
        x.1.asIdeal ≤ y.asIdeal ∧ f ∈ y.asIdeal ∧ ¬ a ≤ y.asIdeal) →
      ∀ z : PrimeSpectrum A, x.1.asIdeal ≤ z.asIdeal → a ≤ z.asIdeal →
        (2 : WithBot ℕ∞) < closureLocalDimension A x.1 z) :
    IsIso (comparisonMap A (Ideal.span {f}) a F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.mono_comparisonMap_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H49, the injectivity half.** For a coherent module `ℱ` on
`U = Spec(A) ∖ V(𝔞)` over a Noetherian ring `A` and an element `f ∈ A`, the map

`colim_V Γ(V, ℱ) ⟶ lim Γ(U, ℱ / fⁿ ℱ)`

of the tag, the colimit being over the opens `V ⊆ U` containing `U ∩ V(f)`, is a monomorphism.

None of the tag's hypotheses is needed: `A` is not assumed `f`-adically complete, no dualizing
complex is assumed, `f` is not assumed to lie in `𝔞`, and no bound on the local dimensions along
the associated points of `ℱ` is assumed. This is
`Stacks.Algebraization.mono_comparisonMap` at the principal ideal `(f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_comparisonMap_span_singleton (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (a : Ideal A) (f : A) (F : (complementZeroLocus A a : Scheme).Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    Mono (comparisonMap A (Ideal.span {f}) a F)
declarations.comment: injectivity
