declarations.comment: exact_rows_columns

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HomDoubleComplexSetup.d₂_exact
declarations.doc: Consecutive vertical differentials in the Hom double complex are exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem d₂_exact (K : HomDoubleComplexSetup (C := C)) (p q : ℤ) :
    Function.Exact (K.d₂ p q) (K.d₂ p (q + 1))
declarations.comment: exact_rows_columns

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HomDoubleComplexSetup.d₁_comp_d₁
declarations.doc: Consecutive horizontal differentials in the Hom double complex compose to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma d₁_comp_d₁ (K : HomDoubleComplexSetup (C := C)) (p q : ℤ) :
    AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (K.d₁ p q) ≫ AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (K.d₁ (p + 1) q) = 0
declarations.comment: hom_double_complex: the horizontal differential squares to zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HomDoubleComplexSetup.d₂_comp_d₂
declarations.doc: Consecutive vertical differentials in the Hom double complex compose to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma d₂_comp_d₂ (K : HomDoubleComplexSetup (C := C)) (p q : ℤ) :
    AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (K.d₂ p q) ≫ AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (K.d₂ p (q + 1)) = 0
declarations.comment: hom_double_complex: the vertical differential squares to zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HomDoubleComplexSetup.d₂_comp_d₁
declarations.doc: The horizontal and vertical differentials in the Hom double complex commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma d₂_comp_d₁ (K : HomDoubleComplexSetup (C := C)) (p q : ℤ) :
    AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (K.d₂ p q) ≫ AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (K.d₁ p (q + 1)) =
      AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (K.d₁ p q) ≫ AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (K.d₂ (p + 1) q)
declarations.comment: hom_double_complex: the two differentials commute

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HomDoubleComplexSetup.homDoubleComplex
declarations.doc: The double complex of abelian groups obtained from a pair of distinguished triangles.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homDoubleComplex (K : HomDoubleComplexSetup (C := C)) :
    HomologicalComplex₂.DoubleComplex AddCommGrpCat
declarations.comment: hom_double_complex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HomDoubleComplexSetup.exists_fill
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8B.** The filling property of the Hom double complex: a commuting square between
two three-periodic sequences of distinguished triangles extends one step further along the
diagonal, where it closes up with the periodicity identification. This is axiom TR3.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fill (K : HomDoubleComplexSetup (C := C)) (a q : ℤ)
    (α : triangleObject K.X a ⟶ triangleObject K.Y q)
    (β : triangleObject K.X (a + 1) ⟶ triangleObject K.Y (q + 1))
    (hαβ : triangleMap K.X a ≫ β = α ≫ triangleMap K.Y q) :
    ∃ γ : triangleObject K.X (a + 2) ⟶ triangleObject K.Y (q + 2),
      (triangleMap K.X (a + 1) ≫
          eqToHom (congrArg (triangleObject K.X) (show a + 1 + 1 = a + 2 by omega))) ≫ γ =
        β ≫ triangleMap K.Y (q + 1) ≫
          eqToHom (congrArg (triangleObject K.Y) (show q + 1 + 1 = q + 2 by omega)) ∧
      (triangleObjectPeriodicityIso K.X (a + 2)).hom ≫
          (γ ≫ triangleMap K.Y (q + 2) ≫
            eqToHom (congrArg (triangleObject K.Y)
              (show q + 2 + 1 = q + 3 by omega)))⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧' ≫
          (triangleObjectPeriodicityIso K.Y (q + 3)).inv =
        -(triangleMap K.X (a + 2 - 3) ≫
          eqToHom (congrArg (triangleObject K.X) (show a + 2 - 3 + 1 = a by omega)) ≫ α ≫
          eqToHom (congrArg (triangleObject K.Y) (show q = q + 3 - 3 by omega)))
declarations.comment: the filling property of the Hom double complex, i.e. axiom TR3 in the form the remark states it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HomDoubleComplexSetup.homDoubleComplexMatress
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8B.** The double complex of morphism groups between the three-periodic sequences
of two distinguished triangles is a matress: its rows and columns are exact, it is three-periodic
compatibly with both differentials, and it satisfies the filling condition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homDoubleComplexMatress (K : HomDoubleComplexSetup (C := C)) :
    HomologicalComplex₂.Matress (homDoubleComplex K)
declarations.comment: the whole remark for the Hom double complex of two distinguished triangles: the matress structure, so exact rows and columns, three-periodicity compatible with both differentials, and the TR3 filling condition

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₂.Matress
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H8B.** A matress structure on a concrete double complex of abelian
groups: its rows and columns are exact, it is compatibly three-periodic, and every compatible
pair on a diagonal admits the prescribed filling.
declarations.statement: structure Matress (K : HomologicalComplex₂.DoubleComplex C)
declarations.comment: matress

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.segmentTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8B.** Three consecutive steps of the three-periodic sequence of a distinguished
triangle form a distinguished triangle.
declarations.statement:
theorem segmentTriangle_distinguished (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) (p : ℤ) :
    segmentTriangle T p ∈ distTriang C
declarations.comment: the shifting the remark appeals to: three consecutive steps of a three-periodic sequence form a distinguished triangle, so TR3 applies in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedEquivalence.exists_dual_matress
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0H8C.** The dual of a finite-dimensional matress is a matress.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dual_matress (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (K : HomologicalComplex₂.DoubleComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} k))
    [∀ p q : ℤ, FiniteDimensional k (K.X p q)]
    (hK : HomologicalComplex₂.Matress K) :
    ∃ L : HomologicalComplex₂.DoubleComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} k),
      (∀ p q : ℤ, L.X p q = ModuleCat.of k (Module.Dual k (K.X (-q) (-p)))) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ,
        HEq (L.d₁ p q)
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (K.d₂ (-q) (-p - 1)).hom.dualMap)) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ,
        HEq (L.d₂ p q)
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (K.d₁ (-q - 1) (-p)).hom.dualMap)) ∧
      Nonempty (HomologicalComplex₂.Matress L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_torsorSectionsRestrictGenericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8E, the injectivity half of part (1).** Let `W` be a regular integral Noetherian
scheme with function field `K` and let `G → W` be an abelian scheme. For every fppf `G`-torsor
`P` the restriction map `P(W) → P(K)` on sections is injective. No hypothesis on the dimension of
`W` enters.

A torsor with no section over `W` has nothing to separate. A torsor with one is trivial, and by
naturality of the trivialising isomorphism its restriction map is then conjugate to the
restriction map `G(W) → G(K)` on the points of `G`, which is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_torsorSectionsRestrictGenericPoint
    [IsIntegral W] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian W] (_hreg : IsRegular W)
    (hK : B.Contains (Spec W.functionField))
    (G : Over W) [GrpObj G] [IsAbelianScheme G] (hG : B.Contains G.left)
    (F : Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.AbelianTorsor (pointsSheaf B W hW G hG)) :
    Function.Injective (torsorSectionsRestrictGenericPoint B W hW hK G hG F)
declarations.comment: part (1), the injectivity half, for every G-torsor and with the two-dimensionality hypothesis of Stacks 0AF9 absent: the hypotheses on W are exactly noetherian, regular and integral. The surjectivity half of part (1) is the statement that the schematic closure of a rational section of P → W is a section; it is not proved, and is the hypothesis hsurj of bijective_torsorSectionsRestrictGenericPoint_of_surjective, which states part (1) in full. The tag obtains surjectivity by identifying G with the identity component of the Picard scheme of the dual abelian scheme and extending a generically defined invertible sheaf over the regular base, and neither the dual abelian scheme nor that identity component is available in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fppfH1_restriction_genericPoint_injective_of_isTrivial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8E, part (2).** Let `W` be a regular integral Noetherian scheme with function
field `K` and let `G → W` be an abelian scheme. Then the restriction map
`H¹_fppf(W, G) → H¹_fppf(Spec K, G)` on first cohomology is injective. No hypothesis on the
dimension of `W` enters.

A class in the kernel of the restriction map is the class of a torsor having a section over
`Spec K`, and such a torsor is trivial by the hypothesis `htrivial`, so the class is zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fppfH1_restriction_genericPoint_injective_of_isTrivial
    [IsIntegral W] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian W] (_hreg : IsRegular W)
    (hK : B.Contains (Spec W.functionField))
    (G : Over W) [GrpObj G] [IsAbelianScheme G] (hG : B.Contains G.left)
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B W hW) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B W hW) AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    (htrivial : ∀ F : Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.AbelianTorsor (pointsSheaf B W hW G hG),
      Nonempty (F.1.presheaf.obj (op (genericPointObj B W hW hK))) → F.1.IsTrivial) :
    Function.Injective (((pointsSheaf B W hW G hG).cohomologyPresheaf 1).map
      (genericPointToBase B W hW hK).op)
declarations.comment: part (2): the conclusion of Stacks 0AF9 with its two-dimensionality hypothesis dropped, which is what the tag asserts; the hypotheses on W are exactly noetherian, regular and integral. As in Stacks 0AF9 the geometric content is the hypothesis htrivial, that a G-torsor with a section over Spec K is trivial. The tag derives part (2) from its part (1), the bijectivity of P(W) → P(K): the injectivity half of part (1) is proved here, in injective_torsorSectionsRestrictGenericPoint, and its surjectivity half -- the statement that the schematic closure of a rational section of P → W is a section, which supplies htrivial by fppfH1_restriction_genericPoint_injective_of_surjective_sections -- is not, the tag obtaining it by identifying G with the identity component of the Picard scheme of the dual abelian scheme and extending a generically defined invertible sheaf over the regular base, and neither the dual abelian scheme nor that identity component is available in this library. The tag's further remarks, that regularity may be weakened to local factoriality of smooth W-schemes and the attribution of the argument, carry no assertion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isDominant_pullback_snd_of_isOpenMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H8F.** The base change of a dominant morphism of schemes along an
open morphism is dominant.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_iff_irreducibleSpace_self_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H8G.** A scheme over a field is geometrically irreducible
if and only if its self-product over the field is irreducible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIrreducible_iff_irreducibleSpace_self_pullback
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible f ↔ IrreducibleSpace ↥(pullback f f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_isDominant_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0H8H.** Being quasi-compact and dominant is fpqc local on the base.
declarations.statement:
instance quasiCompact_isDominant_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (@QuasiCompact ⊓ @IsDominant : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isDominant_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H8I.** A morphism of schemes over a field is dominant exactly
when its base change along a field extension is dominant.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDominant_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : f ≫ pY = pX) :
    let g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))
    let fK : pullback pX g ⟶ pullback pY g :=
      pullback.map pX g pY g f (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by simpa using h.symm) (by simp)
    IsDominant f ↔ IsDominant fK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isDominant_isLocalAtTarget_fppf
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0H8J.** Being dominant is fppf local on the base.
declarations.statement:
instance isDominant_isLocalAtTarget_fppf :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget (@IsDominant : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.fppfPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_cardinalMk_geometricFibre_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H8K.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a surjective finite locally free morphism
of schemes and let `d` be a positive integer such that every geometric fibre of `f` has at most
`d` points. Let `D` be a descent datum relative to `f` whose underlying scheme `V` has the
property that any `d` points of `V` lying over one point of `Y` have a common affine open
neighbourhood. Then `D` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_of_cardinalMk_geometricFibre_le
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} [Surjective f] [IsFiniteLocallyFree f]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hfib : ∀ p : GeometricPoint Y,
      Cardinal.mk (pullback p.hom f : Scheme.{u}) ≤ (d : Cardinal.{u}))
    (D : DescentDatum f)
    (hV : ∀ (y : Y) (v : Fin d → D.over.left),
      (∀ i, (D.over.hom ≫ f) (v i) = y) →
        ∃ U : D.over.left.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ i, v i ∈ U) :
    DescentData.IsEffective D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_universallyInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H8L.** Every descent datum relative to a surjective finite locally
free radicial morphism of schemes is effective: such a morphism is universally injective, so
each of its geometric fibres is a single point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_of_universallyInjective
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} [Surjective f] [IsFiniteLocallyFree f]
    [UniversallyInjective f] (D : DescentDatum f) : DescentData.IsEffective D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_completionSubspaceComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8N, the positive half.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `Z ⊆ X`
be a closed subspace with point set `T = |Z|`. If `Z ⟶ X` is of finite presentation, the
canonical morphism `c : X^∧_Z ⟶ X_{/T}` is an isomorphism.

Both sides are sheafifications of subfunctors of `X`, and `c` is the sheafification of the
inclusion of the first into the second. That inclusion is injective on sections, hence locally
injective; and it is locally surjective because the affine objects of the site generate the
fppf topology (Stacks 021V) and over an affine object the two subfunctors agree, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_completionSubspaceSubfunctor_of_hasImageIn_of_isAffine`. A locally
bijective morphism of sheaves of types is an isomorphism.

The negative half of the source's statement — that `c` is *not* an isomorphism in general — is
not formalized here; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_completionSubspaceComparison (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (Z : Subfunctor X.1)
    (hZ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z) (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z.ι) :
    IsIso (completionSubspaceComparison B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: the comparison is an isomorphism for a closed subspace of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_isIso_completionSubspaceComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8N, the negative half.** There are a scheme `S` in a big fppf site `B`, an
algebraic space `X` over `S` and a closed subspace `Z ⊆ X` for which the canonical morphism
`c : X^∧_Z ⟶ X_{/T}`, `T = |Z|`, is **not** an isomorphism.

Take `A = ℤ[x₀, x₁, x₂, …]`, `S = X = Spec A` and `Z = Spec (A ⧸ I)` the closed subscheme cut
out by `I = (x₀, x₁, x₂, …)`, which is not of finite presentation. The section
`Spec (A ⧸ (xₙ ^ (n+1) : n)) ⟶ Spec A` is supported on `|Z|`, because every variable is
nilpotent in the quotient and so dies in any field-valued point; but no infinitesimal
neighbourhood of `Z` contains it, not even after an fppf covering, because the exponent needed
to kill `xₘ` in the quotient grows with `m` while a covering supplies only finitely many
exponents and detects vanishing faithfully.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isIso_completionSubspaceComparison :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{0}) (S : Scheme.{0}) (hS : B.Contains S)
      (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (Z : Subfunctor X.1),
      IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z ∧
        ¬ IsIso (completionSubspaceComparison B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: the comparison is not an isomorphism in general

declarations.name: quasiFiniteAt_forall_iff_finite_fiber
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag 0H8X, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2): a finite type ring
map `R → S` is quasi-finite at every prime of `S` lying over a prime `p` of `R` if
and only if the fibre `S ⊗_R κ(p)` is a finite `κ(p)`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFiniteAt_forall_iff_finite_fiber
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    -- (1) quasi-finite at every prime of S lying over p
    (∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], q.comap (algebraMap R S) = p →
        Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q)
    -- (2) the fibre S ⊗_R κ(p) is a finite κ(p)-module
    ↔ Module.Finite p.ResidueField (p.Fiber S)

declarations.name: moduleFinite_fiber_iff_finite_primeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag 0H8X, the equivalence of conditions (2) and (3): for a finite type
ring map `R → S` and a prime `p` of `R`, the fibre `S ⊗_R κ(p)` is a finite
`κ(p)`-module if and only if its prime spectrum `Spec(S ⊗_R κ(p))` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_fiber_iff_finite_primeSpectrum
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    -- (2) the fibre S ⊗_R κ(p) is a finite κ(p)-module
    Module.Finite p.ResidueField (p.Fiber S)
    -- (3) Spec(S ⊗_R κ(p)) is a finite set
    ↔ Finite (PrimeSpectrum (p.Fiber S))

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.isBaseChange_exteriorPower_and_deRhamDifferential_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8Y.** Let `A → A'` and `A → B` be ring maps, let `B' = B ⊗_A A'`, and let `ψ` be
the canonical map `⋀^p (KaehlerDifferential.map A A' B B')`.  Then `ψ` exhibits
`Ω^•_{B'/A'}` as the base change of `Ω^•_{B/A}` along `A → A'`, i.e.
`Ω^•_{B/A} ⊗_A A' = Ω^•_{B'/A'}`, and it is a map of complexes for the de Rham differentials
of `B` over `A` and of `B'` over `A'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBaseChange_exteriorPower_and_deRhamDifferential_comm
    {A A' B B' : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B] [CommRing B']
    [Algebra A A'] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A B'] [Algebra A' B'] [Algebra B B']
    [IsScalarTower A A' B'] [IsScalarTower A B B'] [Algebra.IsPushout A A' B B']
    (ψ : ∀ p : ℕ, ⋀[B]^p (Ω[B⁄A]) →ₗ[B] ⋀[B']^p (Ω[B'⁄A']))
    (hψ : ∀ (p : ℕ) (ω : Fin p → Ω[B⁄A]),
      ψ p (exteriorPower.ιMulti B p ω) =
        exteriorPower.ιMulti B' p fun i ↦ map A A' B B' (ω i)) :
    (∀ p : ℕ, IsBaseChange A' ((ψ p).restrictScalars A)) ∧
      ∀ (p : ℕ) (ω : ⋀[B]^p (Ω[B⁄A])), ψ (p + 1) (deRhamDifferential p ω) =
        deRhamDifferential (A := A') (B := B') p (ψ p ω)

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE.isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H8Z.** Let `A → A'` and `A → B` be ring maps, let `B' = B ⊗_A A'`, let `M` be a
`B`-module and let `M' = M ⊗_A A'`, a `B'`-module, with `φ : M → M'` the canonical map. Let
`D : M → P` be a universal differential operator of order at most `k` relative to `A → B` and let
`D' : M' → P'` be one relative to `A' → B'`, so that `P = Pᵏ_{B/A}(M)` and `P' = Pᵏ_{B'/A'}(M')`
are modules of principal parts. Then the map `ψ : P → P'` of Remark 09CP, i.e. the unique
`B`-linear map with `ψ ∘ D = D' ∘ φ`, exhibits `P'` as the base change of `P` along `A → A'`:
`Pᵏ_{B/A}(M) ⊗_A A' = Pᵏ_{B'/A'}(M')`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBaseChange
    [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B] [CommRing B']
    [Algebra A A'] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A B'] [Algebra A' B'] [Algebra B B']
    [IsScalarTower A A' B'] [IsScalarTower A B B'] [Algebra.IsPushout A A' B B']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module A M'] [Module A' M'] [Module B M'] [Module B' M']
    [IsScalarTower A A' M'] [IsScalarTower A B M'] [IsScalarTower A' B' M']
    [IsScalarTower B B' M']
    [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module B P] [IsScalarTower A B P]
    [AddCommGroup P'] [Module A P'] [Module A' P'] [Module B P'] [Module B' P']
    [IsScalarTower A A' P'] [IsScalarTower A B P'] [IsScalarTower A' B' P']
    [IsScalarTower B B' P']
    {k : ℕ} {D : M →ₗ[A] P} {D' : M' →ₗ[A'] P'}
    (hD : D.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE B k)
    (φ : M →ₗ[B] M') (hφ : IsBaseChange A' (φ.restrictScalars A))
    (hD' : D'.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE B' k)
    (ψ : P →ₗ[B] P') (hψ : ∀ m : M, ψ (D m) = D' (φ m)) :
    IsBaseChange A' (ψ.restrictScalars A)
declarations.comment:
Modules of principal parts appear through the universal property of Definition 09CL
rather than as chosen constructions, and both base changes in Mathlib's `IsBaseChange` form. The
map of Remark 09CP is the hypothesis `hψ`, which pins it since a universal `D` generates `P` over
`B`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: LinearMap.isUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE_mkQ_comp_mk_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H90.** Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` be an `S`-module, let `k : ℕ` and let
`J = Ker(S ⊗[R] S → S)` be the kernel of the multiplication map. Then the `S`-module
`(S ⊗[R] M)/J^{k + 1}(S ⊗[R] M)`, with `s` acting as multiplication by `s ⊗ₜ 1`, together with
the `R`-linear map `m ↦ class of 1 ⊗ₜ m`, is a module of principal parts of order `k` of `M`:
that map is a differential operator of order at most `k` relative to `R → S` and every such
operator out of `M` factors uniquely `S`-linearly through it. Equivalently, there is a canonical
isomorphism `Pᵏ_{S/R}(M) → (S ⊗[R] M)/J^{k + 1}(S ⊗[R] M)` carrying the universal differential
operator of order `k` to `m ↦ class of 1 ⊗ₜ m`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE_mkQ_comp_mk_one
    [Module (S ⊗[R] S) (S ⊗[R] M)] [IsScalarTower S (S ⊗[R] S) (S ⊗[R] M)]
    (hsmul : ∀ (a b t : S) (m : M), (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (t ⊗ₜ[R] m) = (a * t) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • m)) (k : ℕ) :
    (((KaehlerDifferential.ideal R S ^ (k + 1) •
          (⊤ : Submodule (S ⊗[R] S) (S ⊗[R] M))).restrictScalars S).mkQ.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ
        TensorProduct.mk R S M 1).IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S k
declarations.comment:
Stated as: the quotient, with the map `m ↦ class of 1 ⊗ₜ m`, is a module of
principal parts of order `k` (Definition 09CL), which supplies the source's canonical isomorphism
by uniqueness of a representing pair and pins the map. The `S ⊗[R] S`-action on `S ⊗[R] M` is the
hypothesis `hsmul`, which determines it; it cannot be an instance, as it restricts to two
different `Module S (S ⊗[R] M)` structures. See the module docstring.

registrations.name: Algebra.FormallyUnramified.base_change
registrations.comment: formal unramifiedness is stable under base change

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.isBaseChange_quotient_ideal_pow_of_formallyEtale
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S → S'` be ring maps and let `J`, resp. `J'`, be the kernel of the
multiplication map `S ⊗[R] S → S`, resp. `S' ⊗[R] S' → S'`. If `S → S'` is formally étale, then
the canonical ring map `(S ⊗[R] S) ⧸ J ^ n → (S' ⊗[R] S') ⧸ (J') ^ n`, i.e. the unique one sending
the class of `a ⊗ₜ b` to the class of `a ⊗ₜ b`, exhibits its target as the base change of its
source along `S → S'`:
`S' ⊗_S ((S ⊗[R] S) ⧸ J ^ n) = (S' ⊗[R] S') ⧸ (J') ^ n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBaseChange_quotient_ideal_pow_of_formallyEtale [Algebra.FormallyEtale S S']
    (n : ℕ)
    (φ : ((S ⊗[R] S) ⧸ KaehlerDifferential.ideal R S ^ n) →ₐ[S]
      ((S' ⊗[R] S') ⧸ KaehlerDifferential.ideal R S' ^ n))
    (hφ : ∀ a b : S, φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (a ⊗ₜ[R] b)) =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap S S' a ⊗ₜ[R] algebraMap S S' b)) :
    IsBaseChange S' φ.toLinearMap
declarations.comment:
Stated for an arbitrary exponent `n` in place of the source's `k + 1`, and in
Mathlib's `IsBaseChange` form; the map is the hypothesis `hφ`, which pins it. The source's final
assertion, that `S' ⊗_S Ω[S⁄R] → Ω[S'⁄R]` is an isomorphism, is
`KaehlerDifferential.isBaseChange_of_formallyEtale`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE.isBaseChange_of_formallyEtale
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S → S'` be ring maps with `S → S'` formally étale (for example
étale), let `M` be an `S`-module, let `k : ℕ` and set `M' = S' ⊗[S] M`, the base change of `M`
along `S → S'` given by `f`. Let `(P, D)` be a module of principal parts of order `k` of `M`
relative to `R → S` and let `(P', D')` be one of `M'` relative to `R → S'`. Then the unique
`S`-linear map `g : P → P'` with `g ∘ D = D' ∘ f` exhibits `P'` as the base change of `P` along
`S → S'`:
`S' ⊗[S] Pᵏ_{S/R}(M) = Pᵏ_{S'/R}(M')`.
It follows that every differential operator `M → N` of order at most `k` has a unique extension
to a differential operator `M' → S' ⊗[S] N` of order at most `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBaseChange_of_formallyEtale [Algebra.FormallyEtale S S'] (k : ℕ)
    {D : M →ₗ[R] P} (hD : D.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S k)
    {D' : M' →ₗ[R] P'} (hD' : D'.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S' k)
    (f : M →ₗ[S] M') (hf : IsBaseChange S' f) (g : P →ₗ[S] P')
    (hg : ∀ m : M, g (D m) = D' (f m)) :
    IsBaseChange S' g
declarations.comment:
Stated in Mathlib's `IsBaseChange` form, for an arbitrary base change `M'` of `M`
and arbitrary modules of principal parts on both sides (Definition 09CL); the map is pinned by
`hg`, compatibility with the universal differential operators, and its existence is elementary.
The source's second assertion, the unique extension of a finite order differential operator,
follows formally, as the source's `It follows that` says. The source sets `M' = S' ⊗_R M`, a slip
for `S' ⊗_S M`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFinitePresentation_cokernel

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.LocalCokernel.isFinitePresentation_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0H98.** The cokernel of a morphism from a finite-type sheaf of

    [∀ U : X.C, HasWeakSheafify (X.J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct_derivedBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H99: the relative cup product is compatible with a commutative square of ringed
spaces.**

For a commutative square `g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` of ringed spaces and arbitrary `K, L ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, the
hexagon `RelativeCupProductBaseChangeSquare` commutes at the relative cup product of Stacks 0B68
for `f` and for `f'` and the derived base change map of Stacks 08HY: the derived pullback along
`g` of the cup product for `f`, followed by the base change map and by `Rf'_*` of the comparison
of Stacks 079U for `g'`, equals the comparison of Stacks 079U for `g`, followed by the base
change map in each tensor factor and by the cup product for `f'`.

There is no boundedness, flatness or quasi-coherence hypothesis on `K` and `L`, and no associator
or symmetry of `⊗^L` is used: the hexagon has binary tensor products only.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_derivedBaseChangeMap
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    RelativeCupProductBaseChangeSquare
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f)
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward f')
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g)
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g')
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.sheaf))
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf))
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor Y'.sheaf))
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.sheaf))
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.pullbackTensorComparison g)
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedProjectionFormula.pullbackTensorComparison g') K L
      (relativeCupProduct f K L)
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq
        (((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj L))
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq K)
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq L)
      (relativeCupProduct f'
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g').obj K)
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback g').obj L))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeCupProductOnRingedTopoi.relativeCupProduct_baseChange_square
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0H9A].**  For a commutative square of morphisms of ringed topoi

```
                g'
  (Sh(C'), 𝒪_{C'}) --→ (Sh(C), 𝒪_C)
        |  f'                |  f
        v                    v
  (Sh(D'), 𝒪_{D'}) --→ (Sh(D), 𝒪_D)
                g
```

and arbitrary `K`, `L` in `D(𝒪_C)`, the relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0B6C] is compatible
with the square: the composite down the left (the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 07A4] for `g`, then
the base change map of [Stacks, Tag 07A7] in each tensor factor) and along the bottom (the
relative cup product for `f'`) equals the composite along the top (`Lg^*` of the relative cup
product for `f`) and down the right (the base change map, then `R(f')_*` of the comparison of
[Stacks, Tag 07A4] for `g'`), as maps
`Lg^*(Rf_*K ⊗^L Rf_*L) ⟶ R(f')_*(L(g')^*K ⊗^L L(g')^*L)` in `D(𝒪_{D'})`.

The four morphisms are morphisms of ringed topoi in the sense of Tag 01D3, part (2), and the
only hypothesis on them is the commutativity `h` of the square.  The relative cup product of
Tag 0B6C is written out as `adjunctionCupProduct` of the derived adjunction of Tag 07A6 and the
comparison of Tag 07A4.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeCupProduct_baseChange_square
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.OfToposHom.derivedPullbackTensorIso g).hom.app
          ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.derivedPushforward f).obj K,
            (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.derivedPushforward f).obj L) ≫
        (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y'.O)).map
            (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChangeOfToposHom.derivedBaseChangeMap f g' f' g h K ×ₘ
              Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChangeOfToposHom.derivedBaseChangeMap f g' f' g h L) ≫
          adjunctionCupProduct (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedAdjunction f')
            (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y'.O))
            (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.O))
            (Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.OfToposHom.derivedPullbackTensorIso f').hom
            ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback g').obj K)
            ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback g').obj L) =
      (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedPullback g).map
          (adjunctionCupProduct (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedAdjunction f)
            (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor Y.O))
            (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O))
            (Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.OfToposHom.derivedPullbackTensorIso f).hom K L) ≫
        Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChangeOfToposHom.derivedBaseChangeMap f g' f' g h
            (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O).obj K).obj L) ≫
          (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.derivedPushforward f').map
            ((Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.OfToposHom.derivedPullbackTensorIso g').hom.app
              (K, L))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_mapped_to_basicOpens
declarations.doc:
A point of a scheme admitting open immersions into two affine schemes has an affine open
neighbourhood whose image in each scheme is a basic open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineOpen_mapped_to_basicOpens
    (U V W : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine U] [IsAffine V]
    (i : W ⟶ U) (j : W ⟶ V) [IsOpenImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j] (w : W) :
    ∃ (W' : W.Opens) (f : Γ(U, ⊤)) (g : Γ(V, ⊤)),
      IsAffineOpen W' ∧ w ∈ W' ∧
        i.opensFunctor.obj W' = U.basicOpen f ∧
        j.opensFunctor.obj W' = V.basicOpen g

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.funnyMap_naturality
declarations.doc:
The canonical maps `Stacks.DeRham.funnyMap` are natural for compatible morphisms of two-term
diagrams, provided the two terms of the complex are carried isomorphically to their scalar
extensions.
declarations.statement:
theorem funnyMap_naturality
    {K₁ L₁ N₁ Z₁ K₂ L₂ N₂ Z₂ : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup K₁] [Module R₁ K₁]
    [AddCommGroup L₁] [Module R₁ L₁]
    [AddCommGroup N₁] [Module R₁ N₁]
    [AddCommGroup Z₁] [Module R₁ Z₁]
    [AddCommGroup K₂] [Module R₂ K₂]
    [AddCommGroup L₂] [Module R₂ L₂]
    [AddCommGroup N₂] [Module R₂ N₂]
    [AddCommGroup Z₂] [Module R₂ Z₂]
    (n p : ℕ)
    (i₁ : K₁ →ₗ[R₁] L₁) (π₁ : L₁ →ₗ[R₁] Z₁)
    (d₁ : N₁ →ₗ[R₁] L₁) (dM₁ : N₁ →ₗ[R₁] Z₁)
    (i₂ : K₂ →ₗ[R₂] L₂) (π₂ : L₂ →ₗ[R₂] Z₂)
    (d₂ : N₂ →ₗ[R₂] L₂) (dM₂ : N₂ →ₗ[R₂] Z₂)
    (hi₁ : Function.Injective i₁) (hexact₁ : Function.Exact i₁ π₁)
    (hπ₁ : Function.Surjective π₁) (hsquare₁ : π₁.comp d₁ = dM₁)
    (hi₂ : Function.Injective i₂) (hexact₂ : Function.Exact i₂ π₂)
    (hπ₂ : Function.Surjective π₂) (hsquare₂ : π₂.comp d₂ = dM₂)
    (hZ₁ : Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin n) R₁ Z₁))
    (hN₁ : Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin n) R₁ N₁))
    (hZ₂ : Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin n) R₂ Z₂))
    (hN₂ : Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin n) R₂ N₂))
    (k : K₁ →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂] K₂)
    (l : L₁ →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂] L₂)
    (neg : N₁ →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂] N₂)
    (zero : Z₁ →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂] Z₂)
    (hki : ∀ x, l (i₁ x) = i₂ (k x))
    (hlπ : ∀ x, zero (π₁ x) = π₂ (l x))
    (hnd : ∀ x, l (d₁ x) = d₂ (neg x))
    (negBaseChange : TensorProduct R₁ R₂ N₁ ≃ₗ[R₂] N₂)
    (zeroBaseChange : TensorProduct R₁ R₂ Z₁ ≃ₗ[R₂] Z₂)
    (hnegBaseChange : ∀ x r, negBaseChange (r ⊗ₜ[R₁] x) = r • neg x)
    (hzeroBaseChange : ∀ x r, zeroBaseChange (r ⊗ₜ[R₁] x) = r • zero x)
    (onH : (⋀[R₁]^p (L₁ ⧸ LinearMap.range d₁)) →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂]
      (⋀[R₂]^p (L₂ ⧸ LinearMap.range d₂)))
    (onK : (⋀[R₁]^p K₁) →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂] (⋀[R₂]^p K₂))
    (onNegTop : (⋀[R₁]^n N₁) →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂] (⋀[R₂]^n N₂))
    (onZeroTop : (⋀[R₁]^n Z₁) →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂] (⋀[R₂]^n Z₂))
    (onNegDual : Module.Dual R₁ (⋀[R₁]^n N₁) →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂]
      Module.Dual R₂ (⋀[R₂]^n N₂))
    (onDet : twoTermDeterminant R₁ n N₁ Z₁ →ₛₗ[algebraMap R₁ R₂]
      twoTermDeterminant R₂ n N₂ Z₂)
    (honH : ∀ x : Fin p → L₁,
      onH (exteriorPower.ιMulti R₁ p (fun j ↦ (LinearMap.range d₁).mkQ (x j))) =
        exteriorPower.ιMulti R₂ p (fun j ↦ (LinearMap.range d₂).mkQ (l (x j))))
    (honK : ∀ x : Fin p → K₁,
      onK (exteriorPower.ιMulti R₁ p x) =
        exteriorPower.ιMulti R₂ p (fun j ↦ k (x j)))
    (honNegTop : ∀ x : Fin n → N₁,
      onNegTop (exteriorPower.ιMulti R₁ n x) =
        exteriorPower.ιMulti R₂ n (fun j ↦ neg (x j)))
    (honZeroTop : ∀ x : Fin n → Z₁,
      onZeroTop (exteriorPower.ιMulti R₁ n x) =
        exteriorPower.ιMulti R₂ n (fun j ↦ zero (x j)))
    (honNegDual : ∀ (φ : Module.Dual R₁ (⋀[R₁]^n N₁)) (x : ⋀[R₁]^n N₁),
      onNegDual φ (onNegTop x) = algebraMap R₁ R₂ (φ x))
    (honDet : ∀ (z : ⋀[R₁]^n Z₁) (φ : Module.Dual R₁ (⋀[R₁]^n N₁)),
      onDet (z ⊗ₜ[R₁] φ) = onZeroTop z ⊗ₜ[R₂] onNegDual φ) :
    (TensorProduct.map onK onDet).comp
        (funnyMap n i₁ π₁ d₁ dM₁ hi₁ hexact₁ hπ₁ hsquare₁ hZ₁ hN₁ p) =
      (funnyMap n i₂ π₂ d₂ dM₂ hi₂ hexact₂ hπ₂ hsquare₂ hZ₂ hN₂ p).comp onH

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.GarelMaps.subsingleton_isCompatible_detNLPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Lemma 0H9G.** Consider a commutative square `b ≫ f = f' ≫ a` of schemes
which induces an isomorphism of `Y'` with an open subscheme of `X' ×_X Y`, with `f` locally
quasi-finite and syntomic (so that `f'` is too), and maps
`c^p : Ω^p_{Y/ℤ} ⟶ f^*Ω^p_{X/ℤ} ⊗ det(NL_{Y/X})` satisfying (0H9C) and (0H9D). Then there is at
most one collection of maps `c'^p : Ω^p_{Y'/ℤ} ⟶ f'^*Ω^p_{X'/ℤ} ⊗ det(NL_{Y'/X'})` satisfying
(0H9C) and (0H9D) for which the squares of the lemma commute, the right-hand vertical arrows
using the maps `b^*Ω^p_{Y/ℤ} ⟶ Ω^p_{Y'/ℤ}` and `a^*Ω^p_{X/ℤ} ⟶ Ω^p_{X'/ℤ}` of Section 07HX and the
identification `b^*det(NL_{Y/X}) = det(NL_{Y'/X'})` of Section 0FKB.
declarations.statement:
theorem GarelMaps.subsingleton_isCompatible_detNLPullbackIso (w : b ≫ f = f' ≫ a)
    [IsOpenImmersion (pullback.lift b f' w)] (hf : Syntomic f) [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    (c : f.GarelMaps (f.detNL hf)) :
    haveI := locallyQuasiFinite_of_isOpenImmersion_lift w
    c.IsNormalized (f.deltaNL hf) → c.IsMultiplicative →
      {c' : f'.GarelMaps (f'.detNL (syntomic_of_isOpenImmersion_lift w hf)) |
        c'.IsNormalized (f'.deltaNL (syntomic_of_isOpenImmersion_lift w hf)) ∧
          c'.IsMultiplicative ∧
          GarelMaps.IsCompatible w
            (detNLPullbackIso w hf (syntomic_of_isOpenImmersion_lift w hf)).hom c c'}.Subsingleton
declarations.comment: at most one collection c'^p satisfying 0H9C and 0H9D compatible with c through the square, using the 07HX maps and the 0FKB identification b^*det(NL_{Y/X}) = det(NL_{Y'/X'})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_garelMaps_isCompatible_resLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Lemma 0H9H.** Let `b ≫ f = f' ≫ a` be a commutative square of schemes
which induces an isomorphism of `Y'` with an open subscheme of `X' ×_X Y`, with `f` locally
quasi-finite and syntomic. Then for every `y' ∈ Y'` there are opens `V' ⊆ Y'`, `V ⊆ Y`,
`U' ⊆ X'`, `U ⊆ X` with `y' ∈ V'`, `f'(V') ⊆ U'`, `b(V') ⊆ V`, `a(U') ⊆ U` and `f(V) ⊆ U`, and
maps `c^p_{V/U}` and `c^p_{V'/U'}` satisfying (0H9C) and (0H9D) which are compatible with the
restricted square in the sense of Lemma 0H9G, through the identification
`b^*det(NL_{V/U}) = det(NL_{V'/U'})` of Lemma 0FKB.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_garelMaps_isCompatible_resLE (w : b ≫ f = f' ≫ a)
    [IsOpenImmersion (pullback.lift b f' w)] (hf : Syntomic f) [LocallyQuasiFinite f] (y' : Y') :
    ∃ (V' : Y'.Opens) (V : Y.Opens) (U' : X'.Opens) (U : X.Opens) (e' : V' ≤ f' ⁻¹ᵁ U')
      (hV : V' ≤ b ⁻¹ᵁ V) (hU : U' ≤ a ⁻¹ᵁ U) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U), y' ∈ V' ∧
      haveI := isOpenImmersion_lift_resLE_resLE w e e' hU hV
      haveI := locallyQuasiFinite_of_isOpenImmersion_lift (resLE_comp_resLE_eq w e e' hU hV)
      ∃ (c : (f.resLE U V e).GarelMaps
          ((f.resLE U V e).detNL (IsZariskiLocalAtSource.resLE (P := @Syntomic) e hf)))
        (c' : (f'.resLE U' V' e').GarelMaps ((f'.resLE U' V' e').detNL
          (syntomic_of_isOpenImmersion_lift (resLE_comp_resLE_eq w e e' hU hV)
            (IsZariskiLocalAtSource.resLE (P := @Syntomic) e hf)))),
        c.IsNormalized
            ((f.resLE U V e).deltaNL (IsZariskiLocalAtSource.resLE (P := @Syntomic) e hf)) ∧
          c.IsMultiplicative ∧
          c'.IsNormalized ((f'.resLE U' V' e').deltaNL
            (syntomic_of_isOpenImmersion_lift (resLE_comp_resLE_eq w e e' hU hV)
              (IsZariskiLocalAtSource.resLE (P := @Syntomic) e hf))) ∧
          c'.IsMultiplicative ∧
          GarelMaps.IsCompatible (resLE_comp_resLE_eq w e e' hU hV)
            (detNLPullbackIso (resLE_comp_resLE_eq w e e' hU hV)
              (IsZariskiLocalAtSource.resLE (P := @Syntomic) e hf)
              (syntomic_of_isOpenImmersion_lift (resLE_comp_resLE_eq w e e' hU hV)
                (IsZariskiLocalAtSource.resLE (P := @Syntomic) e hf))).hom c c'

declarations.name: reflects_injections
declarations.doc:

    (hf : Function.Injective (LinearMap.rTensor S f)) :
    Function.Injective f

declarations.name: Rlim.Pro.exists_map_lim_and_cokernel_delta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H9K.** Morphisms of pro-systems of abelian groups induce maps on inverse limits
and first derived inverse limits. The maps are functorial in the pro-morphism, and both are
isomorphisms when the pro-morphism is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_map_lim_and_cokernel_delta :
    let Rlim.InvSystemAb := ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{w}
    let proYoneda (A : Rlim.InvSystemAb) : Ab.{w} ⥤ Type w := colimit (A.op ⋙ coyoneda)
    let P (A : Rlim.InvSystemAb) : Ab.{w} := ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ A.obj (op n)
    let shift (A : Rlim.InvSystemAb) : P A ⟶ P A := Pi.lift fun n ↦
      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ A.obj (op n)) (n + 1) ≫
        A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    let δ (A : Rlim.InvSystemAb) : P A ⟶ P A := 𝟙 (P A) - shift A
    ∃ (mapLim : ∀ A B : Rlim.InvSystemAb,
          (proYoneda B ⟶ proYoneda A) → (limit A ⟶ limit B))
      (mapR1lim : ∀ A B : Rlim.InvSystemAb,
          (proYoneda B ⟶ proYoneda A) →
            (cokernel (δ A) ⟶ cokernel (δ B))),
      (∀ A : Rlim.InvSystemAb, mapLim A A (𝟙 _) = 𝟙 _) ∧
      (∀ A : Rlim.InvSystemAb, mapR1lim A A (𝟙 _) = 𝟙 _) ∧
      (∀ (A B C : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (φ : proYoneda B ⟶ proYoneda A)
          (ψ : proYoneda C ⟶ proYoneda B),
        mapLim A C (ψ ≫ φ) = mapLim A B φ ≫ mapLim B C ψ) ∧
      (∀ (A B C : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (φ : proYoneda B ⟶ proYoneda A)
          (ψ : proYoneda C ⟶ proYoneda B),
        mapR1lim A C (ψ ≫ φ) = mapR1lim A B φ ≫ mapR1lim B C ψ) ∧
      (∀ (A B : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (φ : proYoneda B ⟶ proYoneda A),
        IsIso φ → IsIso (mapLim A B φ) ∧ IsIso (mapR1lim A B φ)) ∧
      (∀ (A B : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (r : SequentialRep A B),
        Rlim.delta A ≫ r.productSecond = r.productFirst ≫ Rlim.delta B) ∧
      (∀ (A : Rlim.InvSystemAb),
        (SequentialRep.id A).productFirst = 𝟙 _ ∧
        (SequentialRep.id A).productSecond = 𝟙 _) ∧
      (∀ (A B C : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (r : SequentialRep A B) (s : SequentialRep B C),
        (r.comp s).productFirst = r.productFirst ≫ s.productFirst ∧
        (r.comp s).productSecond = r.productSecond ≫ s.productSecond) ∧
      (∀ (A B : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (r s : SequentialRep A B),
        r.Refines s → r.mapLim = s.mapLim ∧
          r.productSecond ≫ cokernel.π (Rlim.delta B) =
            s.productSecond ≫ cokernel.π (Rlim.delta B)) ∧
      (∀ (A B : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (φ : proYoneda B ⟶ proYoneda A),
        ∃ r : SequentialRep A B, r.Represents φ) ∧
      (∀ (A B : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (φ : proYoneda B ⟶ proYoneda A)
        (r : SequentialRep A B), r.Represents φ →
        ∃ hδ : Rlim.delta A ≫ r.productSecond =
            r.productFirst ≫ Rlim.delta B,
          mapLim A B φ = r.mapLim ∧
          mapR1lim A B φ = r.mapR1lim hδ ∧
          Rlim.limitToProduct A ≫ r.productFirst =
            mapLim A B φ ≫ Rlim.limitToProduct B ∧
          cokernel.π (Rlim.delta A) ≫ mapR1lim A B φ =
            r.productSecond ≫ cokernel.π (Rlim.delta B)) ∧
      (∀ (A B : Rlim.InvSystemAb) (a : InverseSequence.ProIso A B),
        ∃ (φ : proYoneda B ⟶ proYoneda A),
          proIsoRepresents a φ ∧ IsIso φ ∧
          IsIso (mapLim A B φ) ∧ IsIso (mapR1lim A B φ)) ∧
      (∀ {D : Type u} [Category.{w} D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ]
          [Preadditive D] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive]
          [Pretriangulated D]
          (F G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ D)
          [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => F.obj (op n)]
          [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => G.obj (op n)] (L : D)
          (f₁ f₂ : Rlim.Hom.systemProduct F ⟶ Rlim.Hom.systemProduct G)
          (φ₀ : proYoneda (Rlim.Hom.homSystem L G) ⟶
            proYoneda (Rlim.Hom.homSystem L F))
          (φ₁ : proYoneda (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomSystem L G) ⟶
            proYoneda (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomSystem L F))
          (r₀ : SequentialRep (Rlim.Hom.homSystem L F)
            (Rlim.Hom.homSystem L G))
          (r₁ : SequentialRep (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomSystem L F)
            (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomSystem L G)),
          r₀.Represents φ₀ → r₁.Represents φ₁ →
          r₀.productFirst = Rlim.Hom.homProductMap L F G f₁ →
          r₁.productFirst = Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomProductMap L F G f₁ →
          r₁.productSecond = Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomProductMap L F G f₂ →
          ∃ hδ : Rlim.delta (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomSystem L F) ≫
              Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomProductMap L F G f₂ =
            Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomProductMap L F G f₁ ≫
              Rlim.delta (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomSystem L G),
            Rlim.limitToProduct (Rlim.Hom.homSystem L F) ≫
                Rlim.Hom.homProductMap L F G f₁ =
              mapLim _ _ φ₀ ≫
                Rlim.limitToProduct (Rlim.Hom.homSystem L G) ∧
            mapR1lim _ _ φ₁ =
              cokernel.map (Rlim.delta (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomSystem L F))
                (Rlim.delta (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomSystem L G))
                (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomProductMap L F G f₁)
                (Rlim.Hom.shiftedHomProductMap L F G f₂) hδ)

declarations.name: Rlim.Pro.nonempty_iso_of_isDerivedLimit_of_pro_isomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0H9L.** Derived limits of pro-isomorphic inverse systems in a pretriangulated
category are non-canonically isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_iso_of_isDerivedLimit_of_pro_isomorphism
    {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    (F G : CategoryTheory.Functor ℕᵒᵖ D) [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => F.obj (op n)]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => G.obj (op n)] (K M : D)
    (hK : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit F K) (hM : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit G M)
    (a : InverseSequence.ProIso F G) : Nonempty (K ≅ M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.counitSplitEpiOfSeparatedEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0HAP.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated étale morphism of algebraic spaces over a
scheme `S` contained in a big fppf site `B`, and let `ℱ` be an `𝒪_X`-module.  Then the counit
`f^*f_*ℱ ⟶ ℱ` of the adjunction of Stacks 03LU is a split epimorphism.

The reduction to the diagonal is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.counitSplitEpiOfSplitEpiChartUnit`, and the splitting along the
diagonal is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.splitEpiDiagonalChartUnit`: extension by zero across the
clopen diagonal.

Stacks 0HAP assumes `f` quasi-compact and `ℱ` quasi-coherent; neither hypothesis is used here,
see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def counitSplitEpiOfSeparatedEtale (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    SplitEpi ((modulePullbackAdjunction B S hS f).counit.app F)
